News.title: Melania opens up on son Barron’s love life with two-word warning and reveals truth about lack of PDA with Donald Trump
News.content:
Next

THE First Lady has pulled back the curtain on some of the most private parts of family life in her new docuseries.

Melania: The Series, a two part series, aired on Amazon Prime Video on Friday, and she revealed her fears for her son Barron and the truth about her lack of public displays of affection with her husband.



In an intimate moment, the 56-year-old revealed she has repeatedly told her 20-year-old son, whom she shares with Donald Trump, to “be careful” when it comes to love.

“I always say it’s a dangerous world out there,” she said when discussing Barron’s dating life.



While the NYU Business student keeps his life incredibly private, his mom gushed that regardless of what happens, “I will always be there for him.”

“We have very open communication regarding life. I will always be there for him. I am, and I will always be,” she said.

read more on melania ORDER UP Melania Trump sets the record straight on husband Donald’s love for McDonald’s

“And he knows that he’s my priority, and he will always be my priority.”

Little is known about Barron’s love life, only that last year an entire floor of Trump Tower in New York City was closed for a date, which he had at home for security reasons, a source told Page Six at the time.



It is not publicly known if he is currently dating anyone as he continues his junior year at the Stern School of Business while living with his parents at the White House after transferring to the DC campus.

Meanwhile, towards the end of the docuseries, the First Lady also divulged more information about her much-discussed relationship with the president.

The pair met at a New York Fashion Week party in 1998 and tied the knot in January 2005.

Melania: The Series director Brett Ratner told her how one of the biggest things he has learned from working with her on the program is the “beautiful relationship” the pair have.

“Well, people, they don’t see that because we are not so public outside,” she said.



Many have noted that the president and first lady are not overly affectionate in public, often using it to hint at marriage troubles.

Melania swiftly pushed away any speculation with a rare comment about the lack of public displays of affection, saying, “We are not that way. It’s not my style.”

“You know, that’s private,” she added.



The docuseries features two episodes, the first focused on family and trust as she prepared to return to the White House for Trump’s second term, and the second on the honor of serving as first lady.

News.title: Athlete, 32, dies after being ‘tied to bed, punched & smothered with pillow’ in psychiatric hospital as eight arrested
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

HOSPITAL 'MURDER' Athlete, 32, dies after being ‘tied to bed, punched & smothered with pillow’ in psychiatric hospital as eight arrested







Next

AN athlete died in a psychiatric hospital after being tied to a bed, punched and smothered by a group of medics, it is alleged.

Kristian Josip Periš, 32, was found dead in Sveti Ivan Psychiatric Hospital in Croatia on October 21.



The former athlete and coach had been admitted to the clinic in Zagreb after his mental health deteriorated.

Distressing footage from hospital surveillance cameras shows a team of medics using brutal force to restrain Kristian to a bed.



One man can be seen holding a pillow down over the patient’s face while others land powerful punches across his head.

Leon Zrnic, the family’s lawyer, said staff “hit him and strangled him” in a terrifying assault that left Kristian with broken ribs.



“As a result of that illegal procedure, he lost ‌his ⁠life,” Zrnic said.

Kristian’s death sparked ​public outrage across Croatia after the footage was published by local media.



On Saturday evening, crowds of people carrying candles and white pillows gathered in Ban Jelacic Square in Zagreb.

At the same time around 1,000 people marched through the coastal town of Rijeka.

Mirna Strugar, who ​attended the protest in Zagreb, said: “I watched ⁠the video and I was in shock to see that evil.

“I hope this ​will never ⁠be repeated.”

Zrnić, who is also Kristian’s godfather, told local media outlet RTL that the family were comforted by the turnout of support.



“It shows that there is still compassion and that we have not completely alienated ourselves from each other,” he said.

Croatian authorities have arrested eight hospital employees as part of an investigation, Al Jazeera reports.

Four medical technicians, aged 22, 28, 32 and 52, are under investigation on suspicion of ⁠the ​aggravated murder of a vulnerable person.



Prosecutors have expanded inquiries to other staff who were present during the incident.

Investigators allege that two technicians pressed their knees against Kristian’s neck, while a pillow was held over his face.

One technician allegedly punched him in the chest, while others struck him in the head and abdomen.

The Croatian Chamber of Nurses (HKMS) described the released CCTV footage as deeply disturbing.

It said “the application of coercive measures” violated “professional and ethical standards of healthcare for psychiatric patients”.



A full autopsy report has not been publicly released.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But initial findings reportedly identified multiple abrasions, bruising, fractures and swelling of the brain.

A definitive cause of death has not yet been publicly established.

News.title: Paedo axe murderer shot dead by cops after fleeing prison & holding kidnapped boy, 10, hostage in abandoned house
News.content:
Next

A PAEDOPHILE axe murderer who escaped prison was gunned down by cops after snatching a ten-year-old boy and holding him hostage at knifepoint.

Nikolai Valov, 37, dragged the terrified schoolboy into a derelict house before threatening to kill him as armed police closed in.



In a desperate bid to save his son, the boy’s father offered himself up as a replacement hostage.

But the twisted killer refused to hand over the youngster, sparking a tense stand-off that ended in a hail of police gunfire.



Valov had been on the run for eight days after fleeing a correctional centre where he was serving ten years for hacking a man to death with an axe.

The fugitive pounced on his young victim near a shop in the Russian village of Bolshebrusyanskoye on Saturday evening.



Witnesses watched in horror as he grabbed the boy by his clothes and hauled him into a crumbling house.

Another child who saw the chilling abduction raised the alarm.

Within hours, the rundown hideout in Russia’s Sverdlovsk region was surrounded by heavily armed police and National Guard officers.

But Valov refused to give himself up and threatened his young captive with a knife and demanded to negotiate with a human rights ombudsman.



A police officer also volunteered to take the child’s place.

But the convicted killer rejected both offers, leaving the youngster trapped inside with his armed captor.

With negotiations going nowhere, officers launched a dramatic raid on the building.



Up to five shots rang out as armed cops stormed the hideout and shot Valov dead.

His young hostage was pulled to safety and taken to hospital after the terrifying ordeal.

Doctors found his life was not in danger, although children’s ombudsman Tatyana Titova warned he would need rehabilitation.

Footage from inside the killer’s grim hideout revealed the squalid room where the boy had been held.

Rubbish covered the floor, while a bed, kettle and empty bottles were among the few items inside.



Valov was convicted of sexually assaulting a child in 2009 before going on to commit a savage axe murder in 2020.

In the frenzied attack, he struck a man in the head 14 times with an axe.

He then robbed his dying victim of just 26,000 roubles (£250).



The brutal killing landed him a ten-year prison sentence.

Yet despite his sickening criminal past, Valov was allowed to leave his correctional centre unescorted every day to carry out forced labour.

The astonishing arrangement gave the dangerous convict the chance to simply disappear.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His escape triggered a nationwide manhunt as authorities scrambled to track down the convicted killer.

Eight days later, his deadly rampage ended in a hail of bullets after he seized an innocent child.

‘DISTRESSING’ CRASH Wheelchair-using pensioner in her 70s dies days after being hit by car on country road







Next

A DISABLED pensioner has died days after getting into a car crash while using her wheelchair

Police scrambled to the collision in Bayford, Hertfordshire, on November 8 after reports of an accident.

It is believed a Land Rover Freelander collided with the woman’s electronically-powered wheelchair at around 11pm.

The woman in her late 70s was taken to hospital with serious injuries.





Sadly despite undergoing surgery, she passed away on November 16.

Police are now appealing for any dash cam footage or witnesses of the accident.

The driver remained on site following the tragic incident and is continuing to assist police.

Detective Constable Felicity Walker said: “Firstly, my thoughts are with the woman’s loved ones at this incredibly sad and distressing time.



“As we continue to fully establish the circumstances of the collision, I am appealing for anyone with information to get in touch.

“If you were driving in the area at the time and saw what happened, captured anything on a dash cam or have any further details, please email me.”

Anyone with information has been asked to contact 101 quoting ISR 795 of 8 November, 2026.

Or, you can anonymously speak to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Woman, 61, found dead inside house in UK market town as man, 62, arrested over ‘murder’
News.content:
MURDER PROBE Woman, 61, found dead inside house in UK market town as man, 62, arrested over ‘murder’







Next

A WOMAN has been found dead inside a house in a UK market town – as cops arrest a man on suspicion of murder.

Cops descended on a property in Wisbech, Cambridgeshire, at around 9.50pm on Saturday evening.

Cambridgeshire Police said they had been called to reports a 61-year-old woman had been found dead inside a home.

The force arrested a 62-year-old man at the scene on suspicion of murder and he remains in police custody.





Detectives have now launched a murder probe with specialist officers remaining at the scene.

Detective Inspector Andrew Moralee, from the Major Crime Unit, said: “I understand this is likely to be concerning for residents, but we believe this to be an isolated incident and are not looking for anybody else at this time.

“Our thoughts are very much with the woman’s family and friends.”

Anyone with information is urged to come forward to police, quoting Op Emeth.

News.title: Man, 28, charged after woman in her 20s ‘raped’ by major UK seaside tourist attraction
News.content:
RAPE PROBE Man, 28, charged after woman in her 20s ‘raped’ by major UK seaside tourist attraction







Next

A MAN has been charged with rape after a woman was allegedly attacked at a UK seaside spot.

The victim, aged in her 20s, was reportedly assaulted on the night of August 4 on Brighton beach near to the i360.



A large police cordon was in place across the shoreline as cops investigated the incident.

A 28-year-old man has now been charged with two counts of rape.



Oleksandr Bryndzei, a Ukrainian national, was first arrested on August 5 – a day after the alleged attack.

He was then conditionally bailed while enquiries took place.



Bryndzei was re-arrested on Friday, November 20, and has now been charged with two counts of rape.

He remains in custody awaiting his next hearing at Lewes Crown Court on December 18.

Public Protection Detective Inspector, Caroline Jeffery, said: “A number of enquiries have been carried out to reach this stage of the investigation, with a man now charged with two counts of rape.

“Violence against women and girls will never be tolerated, and we remain committed to identifying, pursuing and holding accountable those intent on causing harm.



“Significant work continues on Brighton seafront to make it a safe place for all, and we are continually introducing new tactics and initiatives to improve safety, deter offending and protect women and girls.”

News.title: Putin’s warship with 90 crew ‘destroyed’ in huge blast in Libya port as fireball rises from Mediterranean ‘drone attack’
News.content:
Next

A RUSSIAN warship has reportedly been destroyed off the coast of Libya in a humiliating blow to Vladimir Putin more than 1,000 miles from the frontline.

The vessel, believed to be Russia’s £150million Merkury, exploded after it was blitzed in a suspected Ukrainian drone attack in the port of Benghazi overnight.



It comes just hours after a Russian cargo ship was engulfed in flames after being struck by two drones near Finland.

Astonishing footage of the blast in Libya showed the anchored vessel erupting in a huge explosion.



A fireball ripped through the ship as thick plumes of black smoke poured into the sky.

No one has claimed responsibility for the attack, but a source told Axios that Ukraine’s SBU conducted the long-range strike.

The 344ft-long corvette had been stationed at the port in the Mediterranean for several days when it was struck, according to Naval News.

It was escorting a convoy of Putin’s cargo ships used to transport military supplies.



The Project 20380 Steregushchiy-class naval vessel is assigned to Russia’s Black Sea Fleet – but is currently operating out of Northern Fleet bases.

Commissioned in 2023, the vessel had a crew of 90 sailors.

The cause of the explosion – roughly 1,300 miles from the frontline in Ukraine – remains unclear.

Drone boats were later reported to be continuing their attacks on shipping off the Libyan coast, according to the country’s military.

Footage captured at least one boat burning off the coast of Benghazi while another video appeared to show a drone boat being destroyed.



Last year, Kyiv said it attacked a Russian shadow tanker with aerial drones off the coast of Libya 1,250 miles from its borders.

Libya’s eastern-based government said that an initial probe indicated an explosion aboard a Russian ship in the Benghazi naval base at the city’s port.

The government said the vessel had stopped in Benghazi to refuel and resupply on its way back to Russia.



Residents quoted by Libyan outlet Ean Libya said they heard three loud blasts near the port, followed by flames and flying debris.

Local witnesses also reported aircraft overhead and apparent anti-aircraft fire.

Tawfiq al-Shamekh, a spokesman for eastern Libya’s emergency authorities, said the flames had been extinguished.

Experts were still investigating what triggered the explosion, he said.

The government condemned the attack -and said it would take legal and diplomatic measures against anyone found responsible.



“The Libyan government will not allow Libyan ports, territory or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts,” it said.

Since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Ukrainian forces have repeatedly used naval drones and missiles to target Russian warships and naval facilities in the Black Sea.

On Saturday, Putin’s Sparta II cargo ship was struck by two drones in the Gulf of Finland.

The sanctioned ship – a cargo vessel linked to the Russian military – was still burning this morning as it floated in Finnish waters.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The dramatic strike came as Ukraine unleashed a massive drone blitz on Russia’s Leningrad region, which borders Nato members Finland and Estonia.



The fresh blow to Russian shipping came days after Ukrainian strikes badly damaged Putin’s prized billion-pound Crimean Bridge.

News.title: Inside UK’s ‘real-life CORRIE’ estate where ‘crackhead’ locals come out at night – but residents say ‘it’s worth it’
News.content:
CORR-BLIMEY! Inside UK’s ‘real-life CORRIE’ estate where ‘crackhead’ locals come out at night – but residents say ‘it’s worth it’







Next

‘BE UNDER no illusions,’ on-site manager David Forster tells us: ‘It can be a lovely place one minute, a nightmare the next’.

The 43-year-old is on call 24/7 in case trouble kicks off within the brutalist style housing block he manages – which consists of 172 properties and is nicknamed Prisoner Cell Block H.



Locals have even dubbed it a real-life Coronation Street after witnessing scenes out of a soap.

A section of the complex – Waterloo Walk, in Sulgrave, Washington, Tyne and Wear – is a very affordable place to live.



Across five years, starting from 2020, the one, two and three bed flats sold for an average of £16.8K – less than it costs to buy a family car, or a Rolex watch.

It is peaceful and quiet on a sunny Friday afternoon, and while many of the properties in the gated complex are clearly empty and stairwells are littered with rubbish – it does feel like a bargain place to live.

Waterloo Walk sits above the terraced houses of Waterloo Court, overlooking a verdant lawn, and well kept gardens.

But David tells us the housing block undergoes a transformation once the sun goes down.



He adds: “There are nice people here.

“But come night, when the lights go down, they are different people.

“The police are here regularly.

“All the emergency calls come to me. I sleep with my phone.

“Some of the tenants get out of hand.



“It happens when they’ve had a drink and they just don’t stop.

“But apart from that it’s not too bad.”

David explains that much of Waterloo Walk is owned by absentee landlords, and the flats are leasehold.

The current lease runs out in 2079, but can be extended by 999 years for £7K.

Most of the people we approach speak positively about Waterloo Walk and its neighbouring streets, and two tell us the cheap housing helped them to get off the streets.



One woman, who lived on the street her whole life before she recently moved out, said: “Mainly crack heads, druggies in here.

“There are arguments all the time.

“The best thing is it is all blocked in for the kids and the animals.



“They can’t get out.

“Some of my relatives still live here.

“It’s worth the problems, for the cheap rent.

“It’s also worth it for the drama sometimes.

“It’s like Coronation Street. You can just sit and watch it.



“You see people try and jump off their balconies.

“You have no idea what it’s like.”

Glen McCarthy spent two and a half years sleeping on the streets before finding a home on Waterloo Walk.

The 39-year-old, who pays £450 a month for a one-bed flat, says: “It’s absolutely spot on.

“Quiet, peaceful. You don’t get much hassle.



“It’s a nice place to settle down and it’s not too far from the Galleries Shopping Centre.

“I have been here for four months now.

“I was homeless in South Shields before this.



“It’s a big change for us. It’s a safe haven.

“The best thing about living here is that it’s a gated community and you’re close to the shops.

“In all, it’s a very nice place to live. It’s a new start for me.”

Richard, 59, was also sleeping rough before a flat on the street became his home.

He said: “I was homeless, and living on the streets in Brighton.



“I was taken in by a charity.

“I had the choice of moving in here or going back on the streets.

“I decided to move here.

“I have lived here about five years now.

“It’s pretty good. It’s rough, but I don’t have any problems.



“The best thing is how cheap it is.

“I rent this for £475 a month. It’s a maisonette, two bed.

“It’s more or less quiet and peaceful but it can be noisy at times.

“There’s nothing I don’t like about it. I am quite happy here.”

There are currently seven properties up for grabs on the street, the cheapest of which is a one-bed on sale for just £5K.



Meanwhile, the most expensive flat has three beds but is still a bargain at a mere £45K.

Former pit village Washington and its surrounding areas were officially made a “new town” in 1964, triggering a colossal redevelopment programme.

As part of this, Victorian terraces were demolished to make way for new housing, such as Waterloo Walk.

When it opened in around 1968, it was initially lauded for its modern amenities and even won awards for its design.

However, it was taken over by the council in the late 1980s, when problem tenants were moved into the complex and there was a shift in its reputation.



It is now owned and run as a private, gated community, by Wellington & Waterloo Services Limited.

One woman, who didn’t want to be named, told how she’s nicknamed the complex Prisoner Cell Block H.

She said: “It looks a bit like a jail from above.

“Plus, you are locked in. It’s gated. You can’t just walk in.

“When you see it from the outside, it does look terrible.



“But once you’re inside, it’s quiet nice.

“My partner lives here and my sister has just moved in.

“It’s definitely cheaper than where I live, in South Shields.

“I pay nearly £700, some of these flats are only £425.

“It’s canny. All the families look after each other.



“It’s lovely to see the kids running around.

“I call this my holiday place.

“When I am off work, I come here. It’s my little getaway.

“Though don’t get me wrong, there is the odd nutcase.”

Driver Pawel, 49, moved to Waterloo Walk ten years ago after fleeing high rents in the capital and paid just £25K for his three-bed flat.



He said: “This was a huge bargain for me.

“I was paying over £1000 monthly on rent in London.

“We had some problems with our accommodation and decided to move here because it’s so much more affordable.



“It’s easier to buy in the North East than it is to rent in London.

“When I lived in London, I thought, the North East? Where is it?

“I worried there might be a problem getting a job.

“But because you are close to Sunderland, Newcastle and Durham, jobs are easy to find.

“They are planning to connect Washington with the Metro system.



“That’s another positive.

“You can be on the minimum wage, come here, and buy a property without a mortgage.

“I love the North East. It’s much better than London.

“I have no mortgage and it’s made a huge difference to my financial security.”

Home maker Amie Martin, who posed for pictures with her dog Tramp, believes there nowhere better than the gated complex she calls home.



She said: “I love it here me, I absolutely love it.

“It’s mint. I am 41 years of age, and this is the best place I’ve lived.

“And I’ve lived in some posh places, and all.



“Everybody is friendly. It’s quiet.

“You feel safe because of the gates.

“It’s lush to see the kids playing out. Everybody knows everybody.

“It costs me £600 a month including the service charge and I have a big, massive two-bed.

“If I won the lottery, I wouldn’t bother moving.



“I have lived here for about three and a half years altogether, in two different properties.

“It just needs a bit of painting and tidying up. It’s great.”

Professional magician and TikToker Chris Mann, 49, who lives in a three-bed flat with his partner on Wellington Walk, in the same block, is also a huge fan.

He said: “I moved here in 2011 with our lass.

“She paid £27K for it in 2005.



“I love it. It’s quiet enough.

“It was rough when I came here but most of the idiots have moved out or died off now.

“People like to have a good time, have a few drinks.

“But mostly it’s peaceful and quiet.

“I think it would benefit from some painting.



“I am not too keen on the drains either.

“But the guys do a good job of keeping things tidy.

“It’s cheap, not bad. Another five years and then it’s paid for.”

Wellington & Waterloo Services Limited was set up in the 1990s to enable the residents’ association to take over the Edith Avenue flats.

A WWSL spokesperson said they were previously “plagued with anti-social behaviour” but have worked closely with the residents’ association, community police and council’s antisocial behaviour unit to “reduce the levels”.



They said this has included installing a security fence, gates and CCTV “which were successful”.

“Although there is an element of antisocial behaviour, it’s nowhere near where it used to be,” they added.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The spokesperson went on to say lack of funds also “causes problems” for the complex’s maintenance, including keeping up with essential repairs – though property maintenance operatives do their best to keep common areas clean.

The Sun has also contacted the council and police for comment.

Vladimir Putin's £150million warship 'blown apart near Libya' in major blow to Russia

A warship believed to be Russia's £150million corvette Merkury was reportedly destroyed off the coast of Libya in yet another blow to Vladimir Putin

Russian warship reportedly struck near Benghazi

A Russian warship thought to be worth £150million has reportedly been rocked by a huge explosion at a Libyan port, with dramatic footage capturing a fireball tearing through the vessel.

The blast ripped through the ship while it was anchored at the port of Benghazi, in what is being investigated as a possible drone attack. The vessel is believed to be Russia's £150m corvette Merkury, although the circumstances surrounding the explosion remain unclear.

Footage circulating online shows massive flames engulfing the ship followed by clouds of smoke rising high above the Mediterranean port.

The Merkury is a Project 20380 Steregushchiy-class corvette assigned to Russia's Black Sea Fleet although it has reportedly been operating from Northern Fleet bases. It was commissioned in 2023 and has a crew of around 90 sailors.

The explosion happened about 1,300 miles from the frontline in Ukraine.

News.title: Psychologist's five-minute technique 'makes you fall asleep faster'
News.content:
Psychologist's five-minute technique 'makes you fall asleep faster'

Roughly one in three people in the UK struggle with sleep or insomnia

Doctors explains 'worst ever' sleeping position that causes illness

Struggling to sleep? A psychologist has shared a simple five-minute technique that she says could help you fall asleep faster.

‌



‌



Dr Ritz Birah, consultant counselling psychologist at Panda London, has explained how a quick bedtime brain dump can help park worries, clear your mind and take the pressure out of falling asleep. Dr Ritz Birah (Ritika Suk Birah) is an HCPC-registered Consultant Counselling Psychologist who serves on the Sleep Expert Panel at Panda London, advising on sleep habits, brain health, and wellbeing.

‌



She says that when people are struggling to sleep, the instinct is often to try harder. But she says that psychologically, that effort can sometimes become part of the problem. To help struggling Brits, Dr Ritz Birah has shared four techniques to take some of the pressure out of sleep, with one taking just five minutes.

‌



1. The 5-minute “park it” technique

Dr Ritz Birah says that one of the most counterintuitive things you can do at bedtime is give yourself permission not to solve anything. She says our brains often use the first quiet moment of the day to surface everything we have not yet processed: tomorrow's tasks, something somebody said, the conversation we need to have, or the thing we are worried we might forget.

Sleep expert shares top tips on how to set up bedroom to get the best night's sleep

She explained: "Try a five-minute bedtime brain dump. Keep a notebook beside the bed and use a simple ‘park it’ technique. Write down the tasks or worries on your mind, then note one next step for tomorrow. You are telling the brain: I have captured this, I know what I am going to do about it, and I do not need to keep rehearsing it tonight.

‌



"Sometimes the best way to quieten a busy brain is not to tell it to stop thinking, but to reassure it that nothing important is being forgotten."

2. Try to stay awake

Dr Ritz explains: "This might seem like the last thing you should do when you’re struggling to sleep, but rather than forcing yourself to fall asleep, deliberately allow yourself to stay awake instead. This is the principle behind a psychological technique known as paradoxical intention."

‌



She added: "When we start thinking, ‘I have to sleep now’, sleep can begin to feel like a task we have to perform. That pressure creates frustration and alertness, which are exactly the opposite of what we need."

Instead, allow yourself to lie quietly without trying to make sleep happen, she recommends. Don’t check the clock or calculate how much sleep you have left.

‌



"If sleepiness arrives, let it," she said. "The aim isn’t to stay awake all night, it is to remove some of the performance anxiety around falling asleep."

View Image About 1 in 3 people in the UK experience trouble getting to sleep or staying asleep

3. Give your brain something random to think about

If your mind becomes busy at bedtime, cognitive shuffle offers an alternative to trying to empty it completely. The technique involves moving your attention between unrelated, neutral objects or images, such as picturing a book, then a banana, then a bicycle.

‌



She said: "Trying to force the mind to go blank can become another form of effort. Instead, cognitive shuffling gives the brain just enough to focus on without creating a storyline, problem to solve or emotionally loaded train of thought. I particularly like this technique for people whose minds immediately jump into planning mode when their head hits the pillow."

4. Get out of bed when you can't sleep

When you’re struggling to sleep, getting out of a warm bed can feel completely counterproductive, but lying there becoming increasingly frustrated can teach the brain that bed is somewhere we stay awake and worry, Dr Ritz Birah said.

Article continues below

"This is why stimulus control is used within CBT for insomnia," she said. "If you have been awake for a while and feel yourself becoming frustrated or increasingly alert, get up and do something quiet in low light, such as reading a few pages of a book or listening to something calming.

"Then return to bed when you notice yourself becoming sleepy again. You are helping to rebuild the association between getting into bed and actually sleeping."

News.title: Pharmacist issues 'ask your GP' Mounjaro warning to parents of teenagers
News.content:
Pharmacist issues 'ask your GP' Mounjaro warning to parents of teenagers

A new study has put the weight-loss injection in the spotlight, but a TikTok pharmacist says there is more parents need to understand

View 2 Images Around 2.6 million adults in Great Britain use GLP-1 weight-loss medications (Image: Nikos Pekiaridis/NurPhoto)

Weight-loss medication continues to create plenty of discussion, but now its potential use among children and young people is under the spotlight. Pharmacist Raj Patel, known as the Straight Talking Pharmacist to his more than 100,000 followers on TikTok, has issued a warning to parents about what the latest research means for their teenagers.

‌



‌



The medical professional turned content creator discussed a clinical trial involving teenagers with obesity, as well as some young people who were overweight and had a related health problem. The study examined tirzepatide, the active ingredient in Mounjaro, alongside support with diet and physical activity.

‌



Published in JAMA in November, the Lilly-funded trial followed 160 young people for 72 weeks. Researchers found average BMI fell by 18.5 per cent among those receiving tirzepatide, compared with a 0.5 per cent increase in the placebo group.

‌



View 2 Images Weight loss jabs are popularly used across the UK (Image: Getty Images)

BMI is a measurement based on a person's weight in relation to their height, and a percentage change in BMI should not be confused with the same percentage change in body weight. The trial also found that 10 of the 108 participants who received tirzepatide stopped treatment because of adverse effects, equivalent to around one in 11.

‌



There is also an important distinction between the trial results and what is currently authorised in the UK. Mounjaro is licensed for treating type 2 diabetes in children and teenagers aged 10 and over, but its product information says its safety and effectiveness for weight management have not been established in people under 18.

Ensure our latest Health headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings

‌



Mr Patel warned parents against assuming the research means the injection is now an approved weight-loss option for teenagers: "Mounjaro isn't licenced in the UK for weight management under 18 year olds and the trial result is not the same as a new licence."

Article continues below

The NHS advises parents who are concerned about a child's weight to speak to their GP, school nurse or practice nurse, who can offer support with diet and lifestyle changes. The pharmacist also urged families to seek professional advice rather than sharing medication, saying: "And if you're worried about your teenager's weight ask your GP what is available and please don't ever share injections."

The trial provides new evidence about tirzepatide in adolescents, but it does not change the current UK position on its use for weight management in under-18s.

News.title: Keep homes warm with simple £3 window trick that saves £55 on energy bills
News.content:
Keep homes warm with simple £3 window trick that saves £55 on energy bills

A cheap home improvement could help reduce heat loss as temperatures drop

View 3 Images Make a change to your windows (Image: Kiko Jimenez)

Households looking for ways to keep their homes warm this winter could benefit from a simple, low-cost fix around their windows. The trick involves sealing small gaps where cold air can creep in, helping to reduce draughts without spending a fortune.

‌



‌



The Energy Saving Trust recommends draught-proofing around windows, doors and floors to help prevent heat escaping from homes. It estimates that tackling these areas could save households around £55 a year, although that figure covers draught-proofing throughout the home.

‌



It comes as households contend with another rise in energy costs, with Ofgem's price cap increasing by 4 per cent on October 1. This took the typical annual bill for a household using gas and electricity and paying by direct debit from £1,663 to £1,723.

‌



View 3 Images It's time to insulate your home (Image: Getty Images)

There are also concerns that bills could climb once again in January, with energy analysts forecasting a further sharp increase. Cornwall Insight's latest prediction suggests the typical annual price-cap figure could reach £2,166 from January 1, a rise of around 26 per cent, although Ofgem is not due to confirm the new cap until November 25.

Ensure our latest money headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings

‌



One option available from B&Q is the Stormguard Sureseal Brown Foam Draught Excluder, which is designed to seal gaps of up to 3mm. The self-adhesive foam strip comes in 5m rolls and is sold in a pack of two for £5.99, working out at just under £3 per roll.

The product is available online through B&Q, although it is sold and shipped by third-party retailer Low Energy Supermarket Ltd rather than being stocked in B&Q stores. Its adhesive backing means it can be applied around suitable window frames to help close small spaces where air may be getting through.

‌



View 3 Images Simple ways to keep warm at home during the colder months could help households reduce their energy bills this winter. (Image: Getty Images)

According to the Energy Saving Trust, draught-proofing can make a home feel more comfortable by reducing cold air entering and warm air escaping. However, the amount saved will depend on the property and how much draught-proofing is carried out.

Article continues below

There are some important points to consider before sealing gaps around the home. The Energy Saving Trust warns that ventilation must not be blocked, including air vents and chimneys, as adequate airflow is important for preventing damp and maintaining good indoor air quality.

Draught-proofing can be a relatively inexpensive way to make a home feel warmer, but it is not a replacement for proper insulation. The Energy Saving Trust says insulating a property is a more effective way to reduce heat loss.

News.title: Drivers warned rats likely to nest in cars and garages this winter - how to stop them
News.content:
Drivers warned rats likely to nest in cars and garages this winter - how to stop them

Rodents are increasingly finding their way into parked cars and garages across the UK as temperatures plummet

View 2 Images Keeping on top of the tasks can help keep them at bay (Image: Getty )

Motorists throughout the UK are being alerted to an increase in rat infestations affecting their vehicles and garages this winter as temperatures drop. Car insurance experts have shared their best advice to help drivers understand why rodents are drawn to cars and garages during cold spells, and how to stop them from secretly setting up home.

‌



‌



"Rats and mice are increasingly finding their way into parked cars, especially over winter," Yvonne Gosney, Senior Trading Manager at Lancaster Insurance, said. She explained that this is because "vehicles offer warmth, shelter and plenty of hidden spaces to nest."

‌



Once they've gained entry, these pests can inflict severe and expensive damage - gnawing through wiring, upholstery, air filters and even plastic panels. The consequences can include electrical faults, steering failures, engine damage and a revolting accumulation of nesting materials, droppings and foul smells.

‌



Rodents may also make their way into garages as temperatures fall, as these spaces provide even greater warmth and protection. With many Brits choosing to store or park their cars in garages throughout winter, this creates ideal conditions for infestations to take hold, reports the Express.

View 2 Images There are certain tasks motorists can do to avoid the problem (Image: Getty)

Why are rats and mice living in your car a big problem?

Rats and mice often seek refuge in cars when temperatures plummet, and their diminutive size and stealthy movements can make their presence difficult to detect. Parked vehicles provide warmth, protection from the elements, and a safe haven from predators.

‌



Cars that have been driven recently and still have warm engines are particularly appealing to rodents, which can easily wriggle through tiny gaps around air vents, steering columns, pedal shafts, or openings beneath the chassis. Once inside, they tend to make themselves at home in engine bays, air filters, behind the glove compartment, or under the seats.

While out of sight, these unwanted visitors pose a serious threat to both your car and your wellbeing. As rodents need to gnaw constantly to keep their teeth worn down, they frequently chew through critical components such as electrical wiring, brake or fuel hoses, and upholstery, potentially causing costly mechanical damage. They also leave behind droppings, urine, unpleasant smells, and nesting debris throughout the vehicle.

‌



Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

24p item keeps rats and mice away

‌



How can motorists stop rats and mice from secretly nesting in their cars?

"Prevention is far better than the cure," Yvonne said. She has outlined four essential steps drivers should take if they wish to steer clear of this headache.

First, given that rodents are drawn to leftover food, she recommends keeping both the car and garage clear of any rubbish. "Vacuum regularly to remove crumbs," she said.

‌



Secondly, as there can be dozens of potential entry points for rodents to access your car - from air vents and wheel wells to gaps in bodywork or pipes - Yvonne says: "It's a good idea to seal what you can with steel wool."

Rats and mice love to hide away, as it gives them the confidence to settle in and nest. And once they've made their nest, the problem will only spiral, she warned.

‌



Thirdly, Yvonne highlights the significance of maintaining a clutter-free environment. She advises clearing away cardboard boxes, old clothing and other such materials.

‌



She also warned: "Avoid covering your vehicle with a sheet". Elaborating on her reasoning, she explained that "[It] can create more opportunities for rodents to nest."

Her fourth tip involves using particular aromas to repel the creatures. "Strong scents such as peppermint oil, dryer sheets or certain soaps may also help keep them at bay," Yvonne said.

Article continues below

Her final piece of advice is one she considers to be the "most important". She said: "Drive the car regularly.

"Movement and noise are often enough to deter rodents before they settle in. A few simple precautions can save you from extensive damage and a very unpleasant cleanup."

News.title: Mounjaro and Wegovy dosage warning as users told 'speak to your prescriber'
News.content:
Mounjaro and Wegovy dosage warning as users told 'speak to your prescriber'

A health expert said to check the rules for your particular treatment as they can differ

View 2 Images People on weight loss treatments like Wegovy or Mounjaro may need to talk to their prescriber (stock image) (Image: Getty)

People taking weight loss treatments, including Wegovy and Mounjaro, have been urged to check the instructions. The rules can differ depending on what you are on, and you may need to talk to your prescriber in certain situations.

‌



‌



Dr Kate Bunyan, medical director at heart health check provider PocDoc, warns: "Weight loss medications have specific instructions around dosing, and these can differ depending on which treatment you're taking." She went on to explain how the guidance differs when comparing Mounjaro and Wegovy.

‌



The health expert said: "For example, Mounjaro and Wegovy injections are both taken once a week, but the rules for a missed dose differ. With Mounjaro, a missed dose can be taken up to four days late, whereas with Wegovy, the window is five days. Always refer to the instructions provided with your medication."

‌



View 2 Images A health expert has spoken about the different rules that can apply for weight loss treatments (Image: Getty)

Three-day rule

She said it's important to be consistent with the interval between when you take your doses: "Keeping enough days between doses is important—at least three days for both—whether you're moving your day on purpose or catching up on a late dose. If you're late with a dose, you can take it and make that your new weekly day."

But if you keep missing your dose, you may need to speak with your medication provider. Dr Bunyan explained: "However, if you've missed more than one dose, speak to your prescriber before restarting, as you may need to go back to a lower dose.

‌



Ensure our latest health headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

"Never take a double dose to make up for one you've missed." She said the key principle when starting on your medication again is that the doses are "increased gradually over time".

‌



Getting the dose right

There are important reasons for this: "This allows the body to adjust to treatment, and patients shouldn't increase their dose ahead of the recommended schedule, even if they're keen to see results more quickly. The other side of this is that patients don't have to increase their dose.

Woman credits routine with 7st weight loss but some say it's 'unhinged'

‌



"You should always take the lowest dose that gives you the right balance between side effects you can tolerate and progress towards your treatment goals."

Dr Bunyan also reminded users that these treatments are meant to go alongside other changes in your life. She said: "These medications are intended to work alongside healthy lifestyle changes, including a balanced diet and regular physical activity.

Article continues below

"They can offer significant benefits for eligible patients, but following the prescribed treatment plan and staying in regular contact with a healthcare professional are important parts of getting the best possible outcomes."

News.title: 'I run a toy swap charity to help parents afford Christmas presents — families are struggling now more than ever’
News.content:
'I run a toy swap charity to help parents afford Christmas presents — families are struggling now more than ever’

A mum's toy swap scheme is going nationwide to help parents facing hefty Christmas costs. The scheme gives parents the chance to pick up second-hand presents while reducing waste

View 3 Images Families can give unwanted toys a new home and pick up Christmas presents (Image: Instagram/ @no.crap.parties)

As the festive season approaches and families feel the financial squeeze, one woman is bringing hope through a toy swap charity.

‌



‌



Charlotte Mason-Curl set up the Big Toy Swap to encourage parents to give their children second-hand gifts rather than fork out on brand new items. The organisation has been running for five years, with more parents attending each Christmas in a bid to save money.

‌



One in four British adults (27%), equivalent to around 14.3 million people, will struggle to afford Christmas, according to StepChange Debt Charity. This is set to be the worst period for living standards since 1961, according to Joseph Rowntree Foundation.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Charlotte's book Elf Chloe's Surprise follows a mission to repair and rehome toys (Image: Cover Images)

NHS list of supplies to stock up on before temperatures plummet READ MORE :

This year marks five years since Charlotte created the Big Toy Swap in Kendal, Cumbria. Now, with backing from the National Lottery, it is going nationwide, with 68 swaps on the map across the UK.

‌



Charlotte said: “The goal is to help people save money at Christmas, but also encourage less waste. You can get really amazing things secondhand and really cheap – and that doesn’t mean it’s any less of a decent item.”

She added: “People have been coming back every year and we also get new people each year too. I just think there is a lot of chat about the cost of living and financial pressure. A lot of people are getting into debt. Parents always want to be extravagant for Christmas and birthdays, but in this day and age a lot of families are struggling.”

‌



With listings on Vinted surging by more than a third last year, Charlotte has noticed people becoming more accustomed to pre-loved items.

She said: “People are more open-minded to secondhand, but there is a mismatch where people are happy to receive secondhand gifts but they worry about giving them. There’s a slight stigma attached as you don’t want to seem stingy, as well as the idea that secondhand is second best.”

‌



At the swaps, families donate toys their children no longer need and take home others to give as presents. Charlotte says the general motto is “bring what you can, take what you need.”

View 3 Images National Lottery backing has helped the scheme expand across the UK (Image: Cover Images)

‌



The events run from mid-October to early December, with venues stretching from the South Coast to Scotland. Church halls, synagogues, women’s centres and libraries are among the places opening their doors to help toys find new homes before Christmas. Each swap is run independently, and Charlotte says the rules vary slightly depending on the community and venue. Most are free, although some ask for donations or a small contribution towards venue costs.

Charlotte said: “People are struggling even just to make ends meet day to day. So the stress of thinking you’ve got to spend hundreds on your kids’ Christmas gifts is crazy, and you can get amazing things for your children."

‌



“I am not against giving gifts, I think giving and receiving them is a lovely thing to do and lovely to teach children, but there also needs to be a balance between doing it and what we’re teaching them.

"Christmas and birthdays have become a real focus on presents – but is that really what we want to be teaching our children? We’re all trapped in the social norms where we feel like we need to have this enormous pile of brand new presents.”

‌



Charlotte’s idea grew from her own experience of becoming a parent. When she and her partner welcomed their daughter in 2021, they were inundated with gifts. Alongside the gratitude she felt a sense of guilt about the waste, inspiring her to set up her business, No Crap Parties.

“When my children were quite small, I was hearing so many parents moaning about birthday parties. We’d be going to a party every weekend and would have to buy a present and then come home with a party bag of plastic tat.”

Article continues below

Charlotte now has more than 28,000 followers on her Instagram page @no.crap.parties. She uses it to encourage parents to feel comfortable giving pre-loved, handmade or sustainable presents, rather than buying new every festive occasion. She has also written a children’s book called Elf Chloe’s Surprise, which follows an elf and Mrs Claus on a mission as they set out to repair and rehome toys to reduce waste.

News.title: Boss of British Gas owner Centrica 'hugely concerned' over impact of soaring energy bills
News.content:
The boss of British Gas owner Centrica says he is "hugely concerned" about the impact the expected jump in energy bills in January will have on consumers.

Chris O'Shea told the BBC he thought the number of people unable or unwilling to pay their energy bills would rise when prices go up in the new year.

The new energy price cap to take effect from January will be announced on Wednesday and consultancy Cornwall Insight has forecast it will jump by Â£443 a year for a typical household.

The government has said some households will get Â£100 to help with energy bills, but Citizens Advice said it was a "drop in the ocean" while one pressure group called for action on "inflated energy firm profits".

Speaking to the Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme, O'Shea said the predictions for a "substantial increase" in bills from January were "materially correct", adding that the first quarter of the year was the time when most energy was consumed.

"That's right at the point where people will be paying for Christmas and the like. So I am hugely concerned," he said.

O'Shea added there was a "massive problem" with people not paying their bills in the UK, with some not able to pay their bills and an "increasing number of people that are choosing not to pay their bills".

He said the collective impact of that was that "every single electricity consumer, is paying about Â£1.50, Â£1.60 a week to cover the cost of people that are not paying their bills, and it's just going to get worse when bills go up".

The amount owed to energy suppliers by households hit Â£5bn in the April to June period, according to energy regulator Ofgem.

News.title: Theresa May 'aghast' at Burnham's EU plans and says 'Brexit is done'
News.content:
Former Prime Minister Theresa May has warned Andy Burnham he should "move on" from Brexit, telling the BBC she is "aghast" the prime minister could be considering rejoining the EU.

At the Brussels summit this week the PM said he wanted to "brainstorm" options for the future relationship between Britain and the trading bloc.

In an exclusive interview with the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Baroness May, who spent three years negotiating an EU exit deal, said: "Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on."

May claimed Burnham "wants to pat people on the head" by suggesting: "Remember that vote? Well, you got it wrong, didn't you. So have another go and come out with the right answer."

May, who was prime minister between 2016 and 2019 urged Burnham to "just get on with" today's challenges rather than re-opening the conversation around being in the European Union.

Before becoming PM she had campaigned to stay in the EU, but when in No 10 she presided over three years of tortuous negotiations.

The deal she concluded was rejected by MPs. She was forced to quit and was replaced by Boris Johnson in 2019.

Telling Burnham to "move on", she said: "What I saw was that the extent of those negotiations, the hours that have to be put in - it's across the whole of government.

"It's not just prime ministerial time, cabinet ministers' time, officials' time, to-ing and fro-ing on those negotiations. Because you have to negotiate hard in order to make sure that you're getting out what you want.

"And that's one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU. And also we, as a country, we voted for Brexit.

"When I was prime minister I was very clear, we should deliver on that vote. So I'm afraid my message to him really is, you know, people voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on."

Warning against another vote, May told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "I almost think this is what Andy Burnham is saying to the British people, sort of patting them on the head.

"He wants to pat them on their head and say, you know what, remember that vote? Well, you got it wrong, didn't you? So have another go and come out with the right answer.

"Or what he thinks is the right answer. But as I say, let's just get on with making sure the UK is as strong economically, in security terms, and in terms of opportunities for people as it can be."

Speaking to the BBC back in 2023, she said the UK "would have been better off if MPs had backed her deal to leave the European Union".

Her deal had included the prospect of a vote on holding a second referendum, and a vote on a temporary customs union, as well as promises on workers' rights and environmental protection.

May claimed her plan was thwarted by "hardline" Brexit-supporting MPs and those who wanted to remain in the EU.

News.title: RAF's next fighter jet could be last crewed combat plane, air chief says
News.content:
Britain's next-generation fighter jet could be the last crewed combat aircraft the UK builds, the head of the RAF has said.

Air Chief Marshal Sir Harv Smyth, said Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled, uncrewed aircraft would "transform military aviation".

His comments refer to the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), a partnership between the UK, Italy and Japan to develop a sixth-generation fighter jet, expected to enter service by 2035.

The aircraft, commonly known as Tempest, is expected to provide speed stealth, use advanced sensors and even AI to assist the human pilot when they are overwhelmed, or under extreme stress.

Writing in the Telegraph, external, Sir Harv said the GCAP aircraft was "perhaps the last crewed fighter we will ever build", not because people would become less important, but because advances in technology were changing the nature of air combat.

He said AI and machines would take on "the most dangerous tasks instead of humans", while stressing that technology should enhance human judgement and "not replace accountability". He added: "Uncrewed fighter jets will start flying in UK airspace next year. This is exciting and necessary in equal measure."

Sir Harv also said the RAF of the future would combine Typhoons and F-35s with autonomous systems.

The programme was announced in 2022 by the UK, Italy and Japan, which are jointly developing the aircraft. In July, the three countries signed a Â£4.6bn contract covering the next phase of its design through industry joint venture Edgewing.

According to GCAP, the aircraft will be powered by advanced data processing and artificial intelligence, while also featuring enhanced stealth technology. The UK government says the project already supports 3,500 jobs and 1,000 apprenticeships.

Canada was granted "observer nation" status in July, giving it privileged access to the programme without a decision-making role.

In October, Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, said the UK government would "seek to progress" Germany joining GCAP. He said the partnership could also support cooperation on issues including "countering hybrid attacks" and "countering interference in our democratic processes".

News.title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row
News.content:
The wife of disgraced comedian Russell Brand says she will "honour" the rules of his prison, a week after she read a message from her husband proclaiming his innocence.

Laura Brand, 39, drew criticism from ministers after reading out the message from inside HMP Littlehey last week, prompting the government to seek to have the episode removed from social media platforms.

She said on Sunday that she would continue to defend her family and herself over her portrayal in the media during the couple's weekly podcast, which she now presents alone.

Russell Brand, 51, is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

"Last week's episode drew a considerable amount of attention," Laura Brand said during this week's episode of Sunday Service.

"Now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant and professional staff at HMP Littlehey, I will absolutely honour that."

In the relayed message last week, Russell Brand had said he was "not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for".

Laura Brand said she had spoken to him at the Cambridgeshire prison and said he was "OK".

Russell Brand was found guilty of raping a woman at his home in 2009, as well as three counts of sexual assault against three other women.

Further allegations have since been reported about him and some have called for consent laws to be revised.

His conviction has renewed conversation about safeguarding in the media industry, and whether some celebrities are still able to use their fame to prey on women and then silence them.

Ministers have pointed out that inmates are prohibited from making statements that are likely to cause their victims distress and have said Brand's message was being investigated.

A woman who alleges she was raped by Brand when she was 16, but who was not among the women whose accusations led to his conviction, said his prison message was "upsetting" and "really shocking".

The government attempted to have the podcast removed from YouTube, but this was refused by its owner Google. Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged social media companies to "show some decency and take these videos down".

On Sunday, Laura Brand also said that Sunday Service would be a place where she would "continue to be proud to be a wife, a mother and a woman defending her family at a time when the media's image of what kind of a woman I am is under so much scrutiny".

She expressed feeling a mixture of "grief", "absence", "desolation" and "loneliness" since her husband's imprisonment.
