News.title: How a teen gamer and his mother helped rescue a missing girl
News.content:
The Colorado mother knew things were serious when she read the missing persons articles. Jenny knew she was in Oregon and gave the name of a city, but she didn't know where she was being held exactly. Khristina knew she needed more. She told Jenny to find a piece of mail or another document in the house that had a full name on it, which the girl did.

"That's when I went to work," Khristina says, delving into tax and property records.

Khristina narrowed down addresses, then searched them on a real estate site to find pictures. She showed the photos to Jenny, who confirmed that the second one was where she was being held.

The "next thing she asked me was to please not tell anyone until [her captor] was gone - that he did have weapons in the house and she was very scared," Khristina said.

Jenny promised Khristina she'd call her back through the game platform when he left the next morning, and in the meantime Khristina began looking for the law enforcement agency that had been assigned to the missing teen's case. She contacted Jenny's mother on social media, spoke briefly to her on the phone and then got a call from an FBI agent.

"Have you seen her alive?'" the agent asked Khristina.

"And I said: 'I have; I video chatted with her, I've seen her, and she goes 'Oh my God, I cannot believe any of this'," Khristina recalled.

When Jenny called Khristina back after her alleged captor left home, the FBI monitored their conversation. According to the criminal complaint's record of the conversation, Jenny explained how she'd met Adam Hunter Harmel on social media in May 2025.

He'd told her he was disabled and his hips were "messed up," offering Jenny money if she'd help get him to Oregon.

After he picked her up in Utah, however, Harmel threw her phone into a river, drove her to Oregon and kept her in the basement. He forced her to sleep against the wall in his bed, with a knife under his pillow, to prevent her from escaping. He gave Jenny a cell phone with no ability to make calls, but it could connect to wifi, which is how she played the online game.

The 39-year-old "would become violent and aggressive", the document says, which included hitting her and sexually assaulting her.

He also allegedly forced Jenny to remove her braces with pliers so she wouldn't be identifiable.

News.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix as Ferraris collide
News.content:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front.

The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli.

But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team.

And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap.

The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight.

And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin.

Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc.

It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year.

But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world.

The key stories of an engrossing race were:

News.title: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
News.content:
She said Morando had got down on one knee for the proposal during a trip to Asia.

"I am not easy to surprise because I love to control every situation and I had completely surrendered and I'm telling you, I was so, so, so surprised," she said.

During an interview with Wonderland, Morando said he "had to be really sneaky" to keep his proposal plans a secret.

"We went to Tokyo first for a couple days, and then on to Kyoto. I think she had a sense that it was coming, so I was waiting until the very last moment of the very last day to throw her off the scent as much as I could," he said.

Cyrus, 33, had previously been married to Australian actor Liam Hemsworth but the couple separated in 2019.

The singer, whose hits include Flowers and Party in the U.S.A, married Hunger Games star Hemsworth in 2018 after the couple were in a relationship for a decade.

Speaking to British Vogue in 2023, Cyrus said she and 28-year-old Morando met after being "put on a blind date".

Morando is a drummer with LA-based band Liily. The band participated in NBC's Miley's New Year's Eve Party - hosted by Cyrus - in 2022, alongside musicians including Cyrus's late godmother Dolly Parton and David Byrne.

News.title: Tories would scrap Burnham's deal with EU, deputy leader says
News.content:
Conservative deputy leader Alex Burghart has said his party would scrap the deal agreed between the UK and the European Union on Friday, if the Tories win the next general election.

The agreement signed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham covers a youth travel scheme, emissions trading and British food exports.

The government has argued scrapping most checks on British food exports will cut costs for businesses and could bring down prices for shoppers.

Burghart told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme the deal was "a dog's dinner", which would not lead to lower prices in the shops and would mean the UK "gives up our ability to set our own rules".

Under the agreement, the UK will also have to follow some EU regulations.

Burghart acknowledged the deal would reduce some trade "friction" but he said it would put a "massive additional burden on the 90% of farmers that don't do any trade with the EU".

Pressed over whether the Conservatives were committed to scrapping the deal if the party wins the next general election, Burghart said: "I don't think that there will be positive outcomes, and yes, we would scrap it."

He added: "I also don't think it is a good idea for a country like Britain to hand over control of its rules to another power and have no say over how those rules are created right into the future."

Food retailers have welcomed the deal, saying it will cut costs, reduce bureaucracy and remove barriers to trade.

However, they have not committed to cutting prices as a direct result of the changes.

The British Retail Consortium has said it does not expect prices on supermarket shelves to fall in response to the deal.

It has said upward pressures on prices remain and will not be alleviated by the agreement.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband insisted the deal "reduces pressure on trading costs", adding: "They're the things that go into prices."

"It will reduce the costs that the retailers face, all of that Brexit red tape, millions of forms that they were having to fill in, frankly pointlessly, as a result of the bad deal that we had," he told the BBC.

Challenged that the UK was also giving up some powers to set regulations itself, Miliband argued businesses were already "rule takers" from Brussels if they wanted to sell into the European market.

"So they have to abide by the rules of the European Union. But at the same time, because we are not integrated into that market for food and agricultural products, they have to fill in a whole bunch of forms... to confirm that they're observing the right standards, which is frankly crackers," he said.

Under the deal, he said the UK would "be able to shape decisions" for the first time.

News.title: BBC apologises for 'any offence caused' by Strictly noise disruption
News.content:
The BBC has apologised "for any offence caused" after lewd audio was heard during the live broadcast of Strictly Come Dancing.

A recording of sex noises appeared to be playing from the audience in Blackpool's Tower Ballroom as judge Motsi Mabuse gave feedback early in Saturday's episode. She paused before joking: "It's not me."

At the end of the programme, presenter Emma Willis apologised to viewers "if you heard any audio disruptions". A BBC spokesperson also issued an apology and said it was "investigating how this happened".

Lancashire police said it was assessing whether any criminal offences may have taken place, after receiving a formal complaint and a mobile phone being seized.

The moment was streamed on social media by content creator Daniel Jarvis, whose videos include pranks. He appeared to place a phone call before the audio began playing in the ballroom, and suggested he was trying to target judge Craig Revel Horwood for his "bullying".

Jarvis has previously claimed he was responsible for sex noises disrupting Match of the Day in 2023.

Willis told viewers: "Before we see the judges' leaderboard, we'd like to apologise if you heard any audio disruptions earlier in tonight's show and for any offence caused."

News.title: Widow fears losing home built by husband after support payments end
News.content:
Every room in Lauren's family home reminds her of her late husband.

A self-employed builder, Andy carried out much of the work on the property himself, helping create the house where the couple raised their four children.

Now, more than two years after his death from cancer, Lauren fears she may struggle to keep it.

The financial support that helped her cover mortgage payments and household bills has ended, leaving her facing uncertainty as she prepares to remortgage the property.

"I don't want to uproot my children," she said. "They've already been through too much the last two and a half years."

News.title: Man dies in M42 crash near Birmingham Airport
News.content:
A man died in a serious crash on the M42 near Birmingham Airport, police said.

The crash, involving a van and a lorry, happened on the northbound carriageway of the motorway between junction 5a and junction six on Saturday, just after 12:30 GMT.

The van driver, a man in his 40s, died at the scene, West Midlands Police said.

The carriageway remained closed for several hours but was fully reopened to traffic earlier on Sunday morning.

Motorists caught in standstill traffic described seeing a "huge fire" after the crash, while West Midlands Police urged motorists to avoid the area.

The driver of the lorry remained at the scene and was helping officers with their investigation as inquiries remained ongoing, a spokesperson added.

News.title: Village vote 'sent powerful message', say politicians
News.content:
No-one was surprised by the outcome of the poll which saw 257 people vote for the village ''to become an independent self-governing Crown dependency'' and just 16 vote against the idea. One ballot was spoiled.

The result has no legal basis, but there were warnings from local politicians for ministers not to ignore the result.

"It sends a powerful message that it is a completely unsuitable site.

"I hope just for once that the government will actually listen to local people," said Tim Passmore the Conservative Police and Crime Commissioner for Suffolk.

"That is what Andy Burnham said he would do, now it's time for action."

Terry Jermy is the Labour MP for Thetford, which is just two miles away from the base.

He said: "The people of Barnham have done a really good job in raising awareness of the issue and demonstrating the strength of feeling against these plans.

"The message to the government is that this MoD site is not suitable."

While Michael Hadwen, the Reform UK leader of Suffolk County council, said: "This is a clear demonstration of democracy at work.

"Barnham has said loud and clear that that the government cannot impose this base upon them and the government should start to listen because when things like this start to get ignored that's when society starts to collapse."

The estimated turnout of around 70% was lower than campaigners had been hoping for.

When a similar referendum was held in the Oxfordshire village of Piddington 89% of locals took part.

The chair of the residents association in Barnham said some people had decided not to vote after seeing the government ignore the result in Piddington and give planning permission for a nearby military base to be used for asylum seekers.

News.title: Joanna Page says she nearly messed up Gavin and Stacey audition
News.content:
Joanna Page has said she nearly messed up her Gavin And Stacey audition after failing to do a Cardiff accent.

The 49-year-old rose to fame after starring as Stacey in the BBC comedy opposite creators James Corden and Ruth Jones.

Page, from Swansea, told campmates on ITV's I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here! that she had initially read some scenes for Jones using her actual accent.

She recounted that she was then asked to do it in a Cardiff accent, as that was where her character was supposed to be from, but Jones told her it sounded "awful" and to "just be you".

Speaking about her preparations for the life-changing audition, she said: "I remember reading the script, Ruth and James had written it and I remember thinking, 'This is me, she is me, I can do this'."

Page said she got the offer for the part in the Bafta-winning sitcom two weeks after being rejected from a West End show.

She said: "I was working in a shoe shop in East Dulwich and I'd just missed out on getting the part in Dirty Dancing The Musical.

"And so if I'd have got that, I never, ever would have done it."

Page also recalled her first impression of Mathew Horne - who played Gavin in the series - during their chemistry read and said "he seemed really cool, and I thought I'm not cool and I'm just a nerd".

The hit series aired for three seasons from 2007 until 2009 followed by Christmas specials including the series finale in 2024.

News.title: Rare Titanic items sell for record-breaking sums
News.content:
Rare items belonging to passengers of the Titanic have been sold at auction for record-breaking sums.

The highest selling artefacts were a pocket watch from third-class passenger Mary Mangan, which fetched Â£250,000, and a diamond ring worn by famous passenger Lady Duff Gordon, which was bought for Â£140,000.

Another item was a detailed, water-stained letter recovered from the body of its writer, first-class passenger Ramon Artagaveytia Gomez, which was auctioned for Â£80,000.

Auctioneer Andrew Aldridge from Henry Aldridge and Son in Devizes, Wiltshire, said the "epic sale" was evidence of the lasting global interest in the tragic story.

News.title: Man charged with attempted murder after Bradford councillor stabbed
News.content:
A man has appeared in court charged with attempted murder after a Bradford councillor was seriously injured in a stabbing.

Councillor Ibrar Ali was attacked at about 11:00 GMT on Thursday on Thornbury Avenue, before being driven to nearby Manse Street, according to West Yorkshire Police.

Arfan Ali, 32, of Thornbury Avenue, is also charged with assault and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place. At Leeds Magistrates' Court earlier, he was remanded into custody until he appears at Bradford Crown Court on 21 December.

Councillor Ali remains in hospital in a serious but stable condition, police said.

Councillor Ali is a Your Bradford Independent Group representative for Bradford Moor ward and was first elected in May.

He works as a community development manager at charity The Leap, and was one of the founders of Leeds Road Festival.

Speaking after Thursday's incident, his family thanked police, paramedics and members of the public who "courageously provided first aid and assistance at the scene" and asked people to "keep him and his family in your duas [prayers]".

News.title: Tottenham stun Man City to end 17-match winning WSL run
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Manchester City’s long winning home run in the Women’s Super League came to an end as they were stunned by Tottenham.

Khadija Shaw put City ahead with only 10 minutes gone but Cathinka Tandberg levelled late in the first half and goals from Matilda Vinberg and Jess Naz secured a 3-1 victory for the visitors.

City had been on a 17-match winning run at home in the WSL, with their last defeat coming back in March 2025 against Chelsea.

open image in gallery Tottenham players celebrate at the final whistle after overcoming Man City ( PA )

The result means City stay two points behind leaders Chelsea, while Tottenham are now only five points further back in fifth.

Arsenal remain without a win at Emirates Stadium this season after they were held to a goalless draw by West Ham.

Days after a home loss to Lyon in the Champions League, Renee Slegers watched her side endure more struggles in front of their own fans.

Boos greeted the full-time whistle after Arsenal were held to a sixth consecutive home league draw to further pile the pressure on Slegers.

Spurs remain a point adrift of Manchester United, who left it very late to claim a 2-1 victory over Birmingham.

Lee Geum-min put struggling Birmingham in front in only the fourth minute and United struggled to create clear-cut chances, while Phallon Tullis-Joyce made a couple of crucial saves.

open image in gallery Man United scored two late goals to earn victory at Birmingham ( PA )

The visitors finally found the breakthrough 10 minutes from time through Elisabeth Terland, and Simi Awujo broke Birmingham hearts with a header four minutes into added time.

Bottom side Charlton claimed their first point of the season at the 11th time of asking with a 1-1 draw against Aston Villa.

Keira Flannery put Charlton ahead with a first-half penalty but Lucy Parker pulled Villa level 19 minutes from time.

An early own goal scored by Maz Pacheco saw struggling Everton fall to a 1-0 defeat at home to Brighton.

News.title: Interim Blackburn boss reveals Tony Mowbray message to players before derby
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Blackburn’s players followed Tony Mowbray’s pre-match instructions to ensure they earned a 2-2 Championship draw at neighbours Burnley, assistant head coach Damien Johnson said.

Johnson and fellow coach Mike Dodds have taken charge of the team after Mowbray announced he was stepping back from his duties on Tuesday because of health issues.

Mowbray, appointed head coach in June, has been in contact with club staff since the announcement.

He missed the trip to Turf Moor, on his 63rd birthday, for what would have been his 900th match in management.

Without him, Blackburn came back from behind twice – with Andri Gudjohnsen’s 12th goal of the season and Todd Cantwell’s 74th-minute penalty cancelling out goals from Largie Ramazani and Jaydon Banel.

Johnson said it had been a huge surprise when Mowbray had announced the need to take a step back.

He said: “Tony’s had a huge impact on the club. And that’s with the staff, the players, everyone. He had a close connection with us all really. And so it was a shock and a concern.

“He felt he had to take a step back and so we respect that and we want what’s best for him. And he sent some messages and had been in contact and he wanted us just to knuckle down, prepare for the game properly. And I felt the players did that.

“They’ve been terrific all week and I thought they took that into the game today in what was in these circumstances.”

Blackburn warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message ‘We’re with you, Tony’, with Gudjohnsen grabbing one from a pitchside photographer to hold up for the cameras after his 31st-minute goal.

They had a testing afternoon on the field, having to deal with the early loss of defender Tom Atcheson, who was concussed after receiving a boot to the face.

“Taking the week into consideration, it’s not been an easy one, but the reaction from the players after the initial announcement was terrific and we knew this would be a difficult game,” Johnson added.

“All in all, I’m really proud of the players and the effort and the character they’ve shown this week and in the game this afternoon. And so while we’d have loved to have won it, I think, all in all, we’ll take a point.”

News.title: Arsenal’s Lisa Baum stretchered off after on-pitch collapse
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Arsenal winger Lisa Baum was stretchered off while receiving oxygen after collapsing off the ball in her side’s WSL match with West Ham.

The 19-year-old hit the deck while the ball was out of play close to the half-hour mark, with Arsenal’s medical team rushing onto the pitch in her aid.

She required lengthy treatment with oxygen being used, before she was carried off on a stretcher in the 34th minute. She was replaced by Caitlin Foord.

Arsenal have since issued an update Baum’s wellbeing, stating that she was suffering from breathlessness but is now recovering.

This was reiterated by Gunners manager Renee Slegers, who said: "She was short of breath on the pitch. All I heard which is very good, cause it was a concerning situation, she’s in a stable condition which is good."

open image in gallery Lisa Baum was stretchered off after collapsing against West Ham ( PA )

Baum joined Arsenal in the summer from RB Leipzig and the German international has shown promise since her arrival, scoring in Arsenal’s opening-day win over Brighton in September.

She has two goals and one assist to her name across all competitions this season.

Arsenal have struggled for form this season and are still yet to win at home in the league.

They were again frustrated in a goalless draw with West Ham and Mariona Caldentey recognised the team’s difficulties in front of their home support in a half-time interview.

"We are conscious about that and feel sad about it, the fans are always on our side and we want to give back what they give to us,” she said. “Everyone cares so much, and we are trying. We are trying to change the dynamic quickly.

"Individually and collectively, we are a really good team, we need to have confidence and belief in ourselves. When you are in a hard moment it's hard to change the dynamic and you get frustrated; you put in a lot of hard work and effort but it's not working.”

News.title: Gerwyn Price swats off Kevin Doets – and wasp – to seal Grand Slam of Darts final spot
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Gerwyn Price overcame the irritation of a wasp to book his place in the final of the Grand Slam of Darts.

The Welshman was attacked by a flying insect midway through his semi-final with Dutchman Kevin Doets, but swatted it away on his way to a 16-13 victory.

Last year’s World Championship was dogged by the ‘Ally Pally wasp’ and another was out of hibernation early in Wolverhampton.

But it was Price who was buzzing to overcome Doets and reach his fourth major final of the season.

There was nearly a sting in the tale, though, as Doets rallied back from 10-6 down to make it 11-9.

Price got the job done to set up a final showdown with Gian van Veen.

“I’m into another final and I’m not playing that great,” he said.

“I’ve played all right in patches in this tournament. I’m in another final and I’m happy.

“It’s probably going to jinx me now. I’ve probably been the most consistent player this season where majors are concerned. I’m in another final, I don’t care.”

Van Veen is in his first major final since the World Championship after ending compatriot Michael van Gerwen’s run in a tense semi-final, which he won 16-11.

News.title: Howard Lutnick was on the chopping block until he made a massive donation to Trump’s presidential library: report
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick was on the chopping block — until he made an eight-figure donation to President Donald Trump’s planned library, according to a new report.

Trump had been on the cusp of firing Lutnick after he acknowledged during congressional testimony in February that he had visited Jeffrey Epstein’s private island more than a decade earlier.

But after Lutnick contributed $25 million to Trump’s planned presidential library in Florida, “Trump stopped talking about replacing” him, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

Lutnick, a billionaire who has known Trump for more than two decades, has held on to his post despite clashes with senior administration officials and scrutiny over his former Wall Street firm and his role in the Nvidia controversy. The Journal dubbed him the “ultimate survivor.”

“One thing that I find both admirable and vexing about the president is his loyalty to past friends,” outgoing North Carolina Senator Thom Tillis, a frequent Trump critic, told the outlet.

open image in gallery Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick was on the chopping block until he donated $25 million to Donald Trump’s planned presidential library, according to a new report ( Getty Images )

Former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles often clashed with Lutnick and held him on a “tight leash.”

So, when Trump announced that Wiles would step down and be replaced by her deputy Stephen Miller earlier this month, Lutnick felt unshackled, telling people: “I’m not going anywhere.”

The commerce secretary came under renewed pressure last week after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed the department for delaying export restrictions on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm under investigation for allegedly diverting advanced Nvidia AI chips to China. Bessent and Lutnick had previously clashed over a Ukraine minerals deal, according to the book Regime Change.

Amid the fallout from the Nvidia scandal, White House officials privately signaled that Secretary of State Marco Rubio would be put in charge of the export-control process.

open image in gallery Former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles often clashed with Lutnick and held him on a ‘tight leash’ ( Getty Images )

Senior White House officials also debated removing Lutnick from office in the wake of the controversy, which centered on allegations that co-founder Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, Reuters reported this month.

A White House official, however, said the president has total confidence in Lutnick. And the president publicly praised him Friday, telling reporters he’s doing a “very good job.”

Lutnick also faced scrutiny over his ties to Cantor Fitzgerald, the Wall Street firm he led before handing control to his sons when he joined the Trump administration.

open image in gallery The commerce secretary came under renewed pressure last week after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed the department for delaying export restrictions on a firm tied to the Nvidia scandal ( Getty Images )

“Some of the president’s senior advisers have looked at whether Lutnick’s moves as Commerce secretary benefit the firm’s investments, an issue that the president has himself raised at times,” the newspaper reported. The firm has denied there is any conflict of interest.

Emboldened by their midterm victories, Democrats have signaled plans for investigations targeting Trump administration officials and members of the president’s family, including his eldest sons, Stephen Miller and Attorney General Todd Blanche.

Lutnick and Cantor Fitzgerald, which has done business with artificial intelligence companies in Asia, are among their potential targets.

The Independent has contacted the Commerce Department for comment.

News.title: Issue with automation system causes Delta flight delays in Atlanta
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

An issue with Delta Air Lines' weight and balance automation system was causing flight delays Sunday at its hub in Atlanta and nationwide.

The Federal Aviation Administration said on X on Sunday that the airline was working to resolve the issues, and that the delays weren't related to any FAA air traffic systems.

Delta said in a statement Sunday that its teams were using manual workarounds to get flights off the ground while they continued to work to restore automation.

The airline's hub is Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport.

The delays come as Americans begin traveling for the Thanksgiving holiday this week.

News.title: Liverpool v Man United LIVE: Mauricio Pochettino off to worst possible start as United manager
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first Manchester United game and is thrown straight into the deep end as he faces fierce Premier League rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

It’s been a whirlwind week for Pochettino since arriving back in England but the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has outlined his plan to bring success back to Old Trafford after a turbulent spell and alarming dip of results under Michael Carrick.

United enter the weekend in the relegation zone, with Liverpool having the opportunity to pile more misery on their rivals and continue their progress under Andoni Iraola. The Reds will also be out for revenge after losing both games against United last season, including a 2-1 defeat at Anfield.

No game against Liverpool is a considered a free-hit for a United manager but for Pochettino, ending the club’s nine-match winless run with a first victory away from home this season would be some start.

Follow updates from Liverpool v Man United, below:

News.title: Why was Leny Yoro sent off against Liverpool?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Life at Manchester United got off to a nightmare start for Mauricio Pochettino as his side was reduced to 10 men inside eight minutes in his managerial bow against Liverpool.

Liverpool started brightly and fashioned a chance out of nothing when Ronald Araujo’s hooked clearance left Matthijs de Ligt - making his first league start in a year - in no man’s land.

Alexander Isak latched onto the ball but was clattered into last man Leny Yoro just outside the box, prompting referee Sam Barrett to reach into his pocket and show the Frenchman a red card.

Yoro stood little chance of a VAR review overturning his red card, even though Isak’s touch past him was heavy.

open image in gallery Leny Yoro saw red in the early stages of Man United’s clash with Liverpool ( PA )

"Michael Carrick will be looking at this saying: I was dealing with this two weeks ago,” Gary Neville said on Sky Sports commentary.

"It is as bad as it gets from two centre-defenders that.

"For United to be beaten like that by one pass, it is shocking. It is basic positional play.”

Things then went from bad to worse for United as Dominik Szoboszlai stepped up to the free-kick and fired past Senne Lammens into the bottom-left corner, ensuring Yoro’s blunder was fully punished.

Liverpool doubled their lead just three minutes later, with Florian Wirtz volleying high into the goal as Pochettino’s side rapidly unravelled.

Liverpool’s outright domination of the opening stages, combined with losing a defender, sparked Pochettino into making an early change, replacing forward Bryan Mbeumo with centre-back Harry Maguire in the 22nd minute.

News.title: What type of Black Friday shopper are you?
News.content:
Now that you know your Black Friday shopping style, here are the best sales for your personality type.

JUMP TO:

Your favourite mantra is “buy cheap, buy twice” and you’d rather spend more money on fewer quality items.

In our survey with 820 Telegraph readers, 70 per cent of respondents said that when shopping in a sales event, product quality and durability matters the most, while 56 per cent also prioritise brand reputation and trust.

It’s therefore unsurprising that John Lewis emerged as the most popular brand to shop for homeware and kitchenware during November and December, followed by Dunelm and Marks & Spencer. John Lewis was also the second most popular place to shop for electronics and technology (Amazon pipped it to the post). British staple Marks & Spencer was the top choice for clothing and footwear.

Meanwhile, Boots is the most popular brand for buying Christmas beauty and wellness products, but luxury legacy fasion and beauty houses like Chanel, Clarins, Clinique, Dior and Estée Lauder were also dominant in the responses.

High quality sings through all of your choices, so here are some Black Friday sales to shop to match your shopping style.

News.title: Verstappen mocks ‘absolute joke’ Russell after thrilling Las Vegas win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, coming to you from very early on a Sunday morning (if you are in the eastern hemisphere) and very late on a Sunday night (if you are in the western hemisphere).

It is a strange race in a strange place, but this is now the fourth edition of the race and it looks to be here to stay for all its strangeness. It does present the teams with problems and problems are there to be solved or negotiated as well as can be in F1. That is the name of the game.

In qualifying yesterday the world champion, Kimi Antonelli, did that expertly, sneaking in at the end to finish fastest. He does, however, take a five-place grid penalty, so will be starting in sixth. Taking first place on the grid will be the in-form Max Verstappen, followed by George Russell, who could do with a strong finish to the season.

Russell seemed miffed about missing out on pole position, particularly with how Mercedes managed the qualifying situation, particularly with how the tow was managed. Antonelli was always going to take a grid penalty, so why give him the tow, was Russell’s reasoning.

In any case, Russell has a good chance to take his third victory this season. At least on paper. Russell’s qualifying has probably been his strongest suit this season, but race days have let him down. Let us not forget that Lando Norris, who won last time out in Brazil, starts third.

There could be a bit of aggro on the first lap, given Russell and Verstappen’s “disagreement” yesterday, but let’s see. It may end up being a clean race.

It all starts in about an hour and we will be here for all the updates and reaction from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

News.title: Wales ‘frustrated’ after being brought back down to earth by Wallabies
News.content:
Wales have a spring in their step coming into their game tonight as they host Australia at the Principality Stadium. Wales pulled off one of their best wins in recent memory last weekend, ending an over 70-year with for a victory over New Zealand. Despite pulling off that shock victory, Wales sit down in fifth in the northern hemisphere standings coming into this final round of fixtures. In all likelihood, they can only improve one spot. They have made four changes from the historic win over the All Blacks, with the likes of Josh Adams and Aaron Wainwright coming in.

“We were all immensely proud to make history last week,” Wales head coach Steve Tandy said. “There is a new opportunity and challenge for us against Australia and we are looking to back up our performance this weekend. It is our last home game of this competition. The support that fans give to the players and staff has been incredible and we cannot wait to get back out at Principality Stadium.

“We made nearly 350 tackles, the ball in play time was one of the highest in Test rugby in the last three years and we have got competition. The plan was always to freshen up and we are likely to do similar for the week after, because we need to find out about players. We have fresh and hungry players coming in, which will add the energy that we need at the weekend. The training environment is getting more competitive in certain positions we have the ability to put people in and feel confident about performance.”

News.title: Whiff of arrogance as Arsenal unexpectedly implode
News.content:
Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “My feeling is that we lost two points today. I think we were exceptional in the first half. At every level. Our intensity, the clarity that we have, how to attack the jumps of Newcastle every time they wanted to go man-to-man, the composure that we have, the way we use our relationship to break their press. And it should have been 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0 up, clear.

“But it wasn’t. And when it wasn’t, then we expected in the second half that we have to again raise the level because the opponent is going to have a reaction. And the opponent did have a reaction and we were very below the level that is required to stretch the gap in a game like this in this stadium. And then we gave them belief.

“And I say we give them belief because we give them a goal, we give them a throw-in that we just give them the ball. We have no structure to control the opposite winger. We concede a goal and it’s game on. And from that it became a very chaotic game. Every set-piece, we know that they are exceptional at it and we concede from a set piece.

“And then you have to react. And then we went back to the team that the exceptional team that we were in the first half again for another 25 minutes and we scored a great goal. We create infinity of openings to create and score the third goal, but we lack some time or to be precise, to make that count.”

News.title: ‘Remarkable’ Ireland deliver perfect riposte to Erasmus mind games
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Ireland vs South Africa from the Nations Championship in Dublin, with both teams harbouring hopes of finishing the day at the top of their respective tables.

Ireland and South Africa have both won four of their five games in the group phase of this year’s inaugural Nations Championship, and come into their last match before next weekend’s finals still in contention for the overall title.

Andy Farrell’s men begin the afternoon in third in the Northern Hemisphere table, but level on points with second-placed England, who are currently hosting New Zealand, and just one point behind leaders France, who take on Argentina this evening.

The reigning world champions, meanwhile, are guaranteed to at least remain in second in the Southern Hemisphere table, but are just one point behind the All Blacks at the top of the group, so will be hoping for a favour from Steve Borthwick’s men at Twickenham.

The Springboks will be without head coach Rassie Erasmus for today’s contest in the Irish capital, with the 54-year-old facing a six-match ban because of his criticism of officials following his team’s narrow defeat by France last weekend, including asking whether they were “match-fixing”.

“He’s been hands-on with our team, and we’re in a good space,” assistant coach Mzwandile Stick said of Erasmus on Friday. “Irrespective of what has happened, we love him, we appreciate him, and no one is going to break us. I can tell you that for sure.”

In the same press conference, Erasmus predicted that Sam Prendergast would be cleared to play after being cited for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji. The Ireland fly-half escaped punishment from the independent panel and starts for Farrell’s side this afternoon.

News.title: Alonso heckled as Chelsea are humiliated by Leeds
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to coverage from the Premier League as domestic football returns after an international break.

We have five matches to bring you, including Chelsea vs Leeds, Aston Villa vs Sunderland and Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side needs to learn to deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again today.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Chelsea’s goal output has been dramatically reduced and they have dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games.

“(We need) the whole team for that,” said Alonso. “It’s not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

“It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an important player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

“We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.”

Tottenham will not have their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, on the touchline after receiving three yellow cards this season.

Gary O’Neil is targeting a “special” result at Tottenham, but promised Ipswich will not make any drastic changes after a four-match winless run.

Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the two-week break, which followed draws with Hull and Nottingham Forest along with a narrow defeat at Manchester City, but O’Neil is happy with his new-look group.

“There won’t be any drastic changes. The odd personnel change, (but) I don’t think it’s going to be a big shift for us,” O’Neil told a press conference.

“It’s a very well-balanced squad. There’s going to be no massive uplifts or downgrades when we have to change players within this group.”

Aston Villa will have Johan Manzambi available for the visit of Sunderland.

The midfielder did not feature for Switzerland during the recent international break because of a calf injury but he has trained with the rest of the squad and can feature today.

Villa can also call on right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka after a muscle injury ruled him out for six matches. His return is timely as Matty Cash is unavailable.

Cash was suspended for Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United before the international break but suffered a concussion while away with Poland.

News.title: England obliterate All Blacks in record win
News.content:
A nearly perfect half for England was ruined just two minutes before half-time when Ben Earl gave up a penalty from the restart, immediately after scoring the home side’s third try. New Zealand kicked to the corner and Ethan de Groot plunged over to give the All Blacks a lifeline they scarcely deserve.

Until that point, this was as dominant a half against top-tier opposition that we have ever seen from Steve Borthwick’s team. Much like they did against Australia, England have strangled the life out of New Zealand and have enjoyed a preposterous 78 per cent territory.

They have also repeatedly cut New Zealand open in midfield. The interplay between Fin Smith, Seb Atkinson and the regal George Furbank has been sumptuous to watch. England have struggled to break New Zealand down in the red zone but still have three tries to show for their efforts. Smith’s cute little poke through was grounded by Henry Slade after five minutes and then scrum half Jack van Poortvliet did his best Superman impression by diving over the top of a ruck for England’s second try.

Earl also went route one, picking off the back of a scrum and through Cam Roigard’s tackle to put England in dreamland. Not every department has functioned perfectly. New Zealand have been on top of the scrum and have stopped the English maul in its tracks, but the All Blacks have been dominated physically. When was the last time we said that about an England team?

The De Groot try has taken the wind out of England’s sails a little but a similar setback took place in the Australia game just before half-time and Borthwick’s team responded with an emphatic second-half performance.

England need to see this out too, otherwise they’ll be kicking themselves all the way through to the World Cup.

News.title: England lose to ‘Australia B team’ in thriller
News.content:
England’s white-ball tour of Australia continues as a five-match T20 series between kicks off in Melbourne at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground, with the sandpapergate saga rumbling on. The first part of the tour went England’s way, as they came from 1-0 down to win the ODI series 2-1, following wins in Adelaide and Hobart. All of that action on the field has taken place whilst there has been plenty of “he said, she said” as some, like Cameron Bancroft, David Warner and Usman Khawaja say that everyone knew about the use of sandpaper whilst Pat Cummins has categorically denied that.

The last time these sides met in a T20 series back in September 2024, the three-match series ended in a 1-1 draw, with the final match abandoned. England won the last series played down under in October 2022, claiming a 2-0 series victory. Therefore, England are unbeaten in their past three bilateral mens’s T20I series against Australia. England are currently top of the ICC T20 rankings, with Australia third.

England were last in T20 action back in September, when they beat Sri Lanka 3-0. They have won all but two completed T20Is in 2026, with their last defeat coming in the World Cup semi-finals against India in March. They have decided to rest a number of the seamers who played in the ODI series including Jofra Archer and Gus Atkinson, whilst Josh Tongue is out injured. With those seamers absent, it will likely present opportunities for Henry Crocombe and Eddie Jack. Jacob Bethell remains out with a knee injury that he is still struggling with whilst Jos Buttler continues to recover from an hamstring injury.

Australia bombed out of the T20 World Cup in the group stages earlier this year, the first time that has happened since 2009. They did though win their most recent T20 series, beating Bangladesh 3-0 in June. Australia’s fast-bowling trio of Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood have all been rested for England’s white-ball tour, something that was planned long before the 2018 sandpapergate was reignited. Not only are that trio not involved but the likes of Nathan Ellis and Xavier Bartlett will also not play, therefore it will be a relatively inexperienced bowling attack for the hosts.

They will give a debut to wicketkeeper Sam Harper, who was named player of the tournament in the most recent edition of the Big Bash with the Melbourne Stars, with Josh Inglis being rested ahead of Australia’s upcoming busy Test schedule. Inglis is not the only player to sit out this series having played in the ODIs, with the likes of Travis Head, Matt Renshaw, Cameron Green and Cooper Connolly also not participating.

Play from the MCG gets under way from 8.15am GMT.

Sports.title: Hull 2 Brighton 0: Oli McBurnie scores dramatic injury-time double in blow to Seagulls’ Premier League title dream
Sports.content:
Next

BRIGHTON are about to enjoy the best season in their history and they still look certain to finish in a Champions League spot.

But sadly, certainly for those who want to see a title challenge as Manchester City are blowing up, Fabian Hurzeler’s fine football team are not going to win the Premier League.



And here was the reason why.

Somehow, against all the odds, they lost this game. Not just by one goal but two which was properly taking the pee.



After battering Hull for the entire game, having 15 shots and forcing seven saves from keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, they ended up with nowt.

Incredibly, Ollie McBurnie scored twice in injury-time with the home fans not believing what they were seeing.



Brighton looked set for a point until Joao Costinha was sent off near the end for a second booking – and it all went wrong.

McBurnie struck in the second minute of stoppage time as he fell to the ground and then had a tap-in right at the end.

Despite sticking to their principles and refusing to panic, Brighton could still be playing for the next 24 hours and they would have failed to score.

The fact Arsenal, despite their draw on Saturday, are six points clear with approaching a third of the season gone tells you who will be champions in May.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Hull, despite struggling for most of the game, should get some credit for their bloody-minded determination.

Yes, they had dipped since the start of the season.

But as they also proved in the 1-0 loss at Arsenal a couple of weeks ago, they are no pushovers and it is lazy to assume they will definitely be relegated.



Yes, it will be close but there is enough dross down at the bottom of the Premier League for all three promoted teams to scramble to safety.

Certainly if Hull hang in there like they did here, they will be staying up.

Brighton, of course, have no such worries and they are reaching for the stars.

On Thursday, Brighton will once again be back in Europe, at home to Romanian SuperLiga leaders Craiova and they will want to get this game out of their system.

Their only defeats had been a chaotic 4-3 loss at Chelsea and 2-0 defeat at Liverpool but this one will hurt.



Brighton were wasteful even though the Hull keeper, a £20million summer signing from Olympiacos, was outstanding.



Diego Gomez should have scored but he stuck a shot straight at Tzolakis while Brighton defender Joao Costinha crouched down and put both hands on his head in embarrassment when he should have least managed to get the shot on target.

Tzolakis then made two saves from Georginio Rutter and the second was a cracker as he rushed off his line and made himself big with his left arm keeping the ball out.

That moment came just seconds after Ayari sent an effort thundering against the bar and on the stroke of half-time, Tzolakis stuck out his right boot to somehow keep out a strike from Gomez although once again, he really should have scored.

Despite barely getting a kick in the first 45 minutes, Hull still had a couple of chances but Bart Verbruggen kept out a flick from Matt Crooks and a decent free-kick by Mohamed Belloumi.



Hull manager Sergej Jakirovic was forced into a change before half-time when Tim Iroegbunam injured himself tackling Chema Andres.

Yet after the break, Brighton carried on being denied by Tzolakis who made saves from Gross and Lewis Dunk while Gomez blasted a half volley wide from the side of the six-yard box.

Because they had spent most of the game watching Brighton waste good chances, Hull started doing the same.



Belloumi dragged a shot wide when he looked certain to give his team an unlikely lead while Sorba Thomas’ cross hit the woodwork.

Finally, the Brighton sub lifted the ball over the Hull keeper yet Regan Slater bailed out his team with a goal-line clearance.

Near the end, a frustrating afternoon became too much for Costinha who pushed Thomas to the floor and he picked up his second booking.

Yet worse was to follow in injury time.

And unbelievably, as Brighton pushed forward Belloumi beat Maxim De Cuyper and he squared for McBurnie.

LISA BAUM was stretchered off while wearing an oxygen mask after going down off the ball during Arsenal Women’s stalemate with West Ham.

The winger, 19, hit the deck and medical staff rushed onto the pitch as the Women’s Super League clash neared the half hour mark.



Baum was seen dropping to the turf after West Ham top scorer Viviane Asseyi sent a long range shot high and wide.

Arsenal team-mates, including Lionesses icon Georgia Stanway, showed concern before it was quickly signalled that a substitution needed to be made.



Baum was eventually stretchered off after receiving treatment for close to five minutes.

And the one-cap Germany international, who was applauded off the pitch by those in the Emirates stands, was replaced by Caitlin Foord.



Arsenal released an update early in the second half which read: “After suffering from shortness of breath, Lisa Baum is now stable and responding well.”

But the Gunners could not go on to grab all three points as they were held to a goalless draw by West Ham.

The stalemate left Arsenal closer to the drop zone than table-topping Chelsea.

Renee Slegers’ side are just nine points better off than Birmingham, who are in the relegation play-off spot.



Chelsea, who have still not been defeated in the Women’s Super League this term, are 12 points clear of Arsenal.

Baum joined the Gunners during the summer and has already made an impressive start to the campaign.

She found the net in Arsenal’s season-opening win over Brighton in September.



Baum wears a bandage on her right wrist in memory of her brother Dennis, who tragically died in a car accident at the age of 17 in 2022.

Baum told The Guardian: “The next time I was on the field, I felt like I wanted to do that.

“I feel like it’s given me a different kind of strength and confidence. Sometimes I don’t write anything, but it’s about just having the physical feeling that he is with me.”

Bruno Fernandes insists that he won't down tools and see out his contract at Manchester United - like he's seen some of his teammates do.

‌



‌



Fernandes, 32, recently turned down a second offer of a new deal with the Red Devils, with his current terms expiring at the end of this season.

‌



But the United captain says that he'll make a decision on his future before then or accept being sold in January. Fernandes has played with multiple big names who've opted to run down their contracts at Old Trafford before leaving on a free transfer, meaning that the club have missed out on a fee.

‌



Some players have left much more amicably at the end of their deals and Fernandes wants to be in the latter camp if this proves to his final campaign in Manchester. "I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on," the Portugal international told Sky Sports.

"I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United. They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, 'Bruno, it's time to part ways', I'm going to be the first one walking out the door."

A handful of players were banned in the aftermath, including Paredes, who was given a 10-match suspension and fined $90,000. This ban applies to senior international fixtures, so Paredes has remained eligible to captain and play for Boca throughout the current season.

Article continues below

The former PSG and Juventus player appealed the ban, but FIFA's Appeal Committee rejected the appeal this month.

The Argentine Football Association announced it would take Paredes' case to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) following the committee's ruling.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes opens up on Arsenal frustration after being booed on Newcastle return
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes opens up on Arsenal frustration after being booed on Newcastle return

Bruno Guimaraes returned to St James' Park for the first time since his summer move from Newcastle to Arsenal, where he was given a hostile reception

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes during Arsenal's draw with Newcastle at St James' Park (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes admitted he was left frustrated after Arsenal failed to win all three points on his Newcastle return.

‌



‌



The Brazilian was given a hostile reception as he made his first appearance at St James' Park since leaving the club in a contentious and drawn-out £75million switch to Arsenal in the summer.

‌



Guimaraes told the Magpies that he no longer wanted to play for them after four and a half years on Tyneside, during which he twice helped the club secure Champions League qualification and became the first Newcastle captain in 56 years to lift silverware.

‌



His contributions at the club left many fans with mixed feelings ahead of his return, but inside St James' Park the reaction was crystal clear, with the midfielder roundly booed and jeered every time he touched the ball.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Guimaraes appeared visibly affected by the reception. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta had been expected to keep the player on the bench following his international commitments with Brazil and he eventually hauled the midfielder off for Myles Lewis-Skelly after 70 minutes, reports Chronicle Live.

In the aftermath, Guimaraes took to social media to voice his frustration and anguish over how the night had unfolded, with his side being held to a 2-2 draw by the battling Magpies.

‌



"A different experience for me today, returning to a place where I've shared so many happy memories over the past five years," he wrote.

View 2 Images Guimaraes was frustrated to not win on his Tyneside return (Image: Lee Parker - CameraSport, CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



"A game of two very different halves, and the frustration of not being able to take all three points at a place where it's always tough to play.

"There's still a lot ahead of us. We keep moving forward together, always!".

‌



Guimaraes had an excellent opportunity to break the deadlock in the opening period, arriving late into the box to connect with a Noni Madueke delivery but could only direct his effort wide of the upright.

Following the final whistle, the Brazilian remained on the turf and received a somewhat warmer welcome from the Newcastle supporters who stayed in the stadium as he clapped and acknowledged them, though a handful of jeers could still be heard.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino makes instant changes to Man Utd training with warning to players
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino makes instant changes to Man Utd training with warning to players

Mauricio Pochettino has only been in post at Manchester United for a matter of days, but the new Red Devils boss hasn't wasted time in making changes behind the scenes

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino will lay down the law at Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United's players have been warned that new manager Mauricio Pochettino is only just getting started with his high-octane training sessions. Pochettino, 54, has been brought in to arrest United's problems following a dire start to the season, leaving them in the relegation zone ahead of his first game away to Liverpool on Sunday.

‌



‌



Going into this weekend, the Red Devils were 19th for total distance covered in the Premier League this season, 17th for high-speed running and 19th for average maximum speed. Pochettino stressed in Friday's press conference that 'data is about context', but the statistics certainly make for worrying reading.

‌



The Argentine has overseen three days of training so far, with each session described as 'harder' and lasting longer than under Michael Carrick. But the real work starts after the trip to Liverpool.

‌



A source told the Sun: "Poch has immediately brought an increase in tempo and intensity to everything. The players have been training harder and for longer and have already noticed the difference.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"But his main aim has been to get some of his tactics into the team ahead of the game. So while they have felt an increase in workload and demands, the message is that he’s not even got going yet.

"It will be interesting to see what happens - either the players are going to embrace it and go with it, or they're not and it's going to be another disaster."

‌



United's players will need to be ready to get a sweat on under Pochettino, who demands that his players run hard. The ex-USA head coach won't have much time on the training ground, though, with five matches in the next 21 days.

Will Manchester United beat Liverpool? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino has been focussed on facing Liverpool (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Still, Pochettino will do what he can to get his squad fit as fire. "If you don't put context on the data, I think it's very dangerous to talk and I think that it's easy to manipulate the data," he explained in his press conference.

‌



"But it's true that I need to be honest. That sometimes data shows something that you can see after on the field. But we are going to be very focused and try to improve our data, our numbers in every single area of the field.

"And, of course, we are here not to denounce things. We are here to build something with our players and with the club and try to perform and win games."

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes breaks silence on Man Utd future after double contract rejection
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes breaks silence on Man Utd future after double contract rejection

Bruno Fernandes has entered the final year of his deal at Manchester United and has reportedly turned down two offers of a new contract, plunging his future into doubt

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes provided an update on his future (Image: Sky Sports)

Bruno Fernandes has confirmed that he's been offered a new contract by Manchester United - but says that negotiations are on hold. Fernandes, 32, is approaching the final six months of his current deal and has reportedly turned down two proposals to stay at Old Trafford.

‌



But the United captain's future is uncertain following a dismal start to the season and a change of manager. Mauricio Pochettino has replaced Michael Carrick, who Fernandes insists there was no fallout with, despite being dropped from the starting XI last month.

Pochettino's arrival has brought the Portuguese's future back into the spotlight, as he could be sold in the January transfer window if United want to avoid losing him for nothing next summer. Fernandes insists that he wouldn't stand in the club's way if they decided to sell him, but rejected claims that he wants more money or a longer deal.

"No, there's no negotiations ongoing," Fernandes told Sky Sports. "But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

"And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United.

Should Bruno Fernandes leave Manchester United? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes says that he didn't fall out with Michael Carrick (Image: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

"They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, 'Bruno, it's time to part ways', I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

"Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on.

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes has put contract negotiations on pause (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Fernandes maintains that his ambition remains to win the Premier League and Champions League with United, but concedes that their present target is to finish inside the 'top four'. The midfielder is excited to work with Pochettino, who tried to sign him at Tottenham in 2019.

"He's someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, said it straight away that he won't allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player," Fernandes, speaking ahead of Sunday's clash with Liverpool, added.

"He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that's pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve."

Sports.title: McBurnie's late double stuns 10-man Brighton after Tzolakis heroics
Sports.content:
A Konstantinos Tzolakis goalkeeping masterclass teed up Oli McBurnie to score two late goals as Hull stunned dominant Brighton in a smash-and-grab 2-0 win at the MKM Stadium.

Like the legendary Greek mythological king, Tzolakis had the Midas touch throughout for the Tigers, making five first-half saves - the most by any goalkeeper all season - before McBurnie netted twice in added time to snatch a victory which had looked beyond Hull for so long.

High-fying Brighton had racked up an xG of 2.24 and five presentable chances but were denied by a combination of the goalkeeper's fine form and some wasteful finishing, and ultimately missed the chance to move three points off leaders Arsenal.

Tzolakis' highlight was a stunning one-handed stop to keep out Diego Gomez's 15th-minute effort, which set the tone for a perfect performance to frustrate the visitors.

He was also at his best to deny Georginio Rutter, after Yasin Ayari's shot had rebounded off the crossbar, before a superb stop with his trailing leg frustrated Gomez again moments before the interval.

"We can be critical of some of the misses but the goalkeeper has been fantastic," said Sky Sports' Roy Keane at the break. "He's man of the match already for me."

With the one-way traffic unabated after the restart, Tzolakis owed some credit to midfielder Regan Slater for keeping his clean sheet intact, nodding off the line when substitute Charalampos Kostoulas lifted the ball over the goalkeeper after he had given the ball away cheaply himself.

The hosts did threaten an unlikely victory with Mohamed Belloumi twice cutting in off the right before wasting good positions, and Sorba Thomas almost netting a fortuitous goal when his cross bounced back off the crossbar.

But after Brighton's Costinha was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge late on, Hull saw their moment to strike, with McBurnie scrambling in an opener following a counter-attack before tapping home a second with Brighton pushing to equalise.

The key moments from the MKM Stadium

15: ONCE... Tzolakis begins his afternoon heroics by getting down low to keep out Gomez's effort.

19: MISS! Costinha should put Brighton ahead but fires wide from close range.

37: TWICE... Ayari's effort crashes off the bar before Rutter is again denied by Tzolakis on the follow-up.

45+3: THREE TIMES A 'KEEPER! Tzolakis keeps out another Gomez effort thanks to a superb stop with his trailing leg.

52: CLOSE! Gomez brings down a cross with a world-class first touch before lashing inches wide of the far post.

65: CLOSE! Against the run of play, Belloumi fires wide after leaving Olivier Boscagli on his backside.

79: OFF THE LINE! Kostoulas races through to latch onto Slater's backpass but the midfielder recovers to clear his chip off the line.

89: RED CARD! Costinha sees red for a clumsy lunge on Thomas, which earns him a second yellow card.

90+1: GOAL! McBurnie turns home an unlikely opener on the counter-attack to stun Brighton before...

90+4: GOAL! ...He adds a second from Belloumi's square ball to seal victory and send the MKM Stadium wild.

Sports.title: Final Demand battles back to win Punchestown thriller
Sports.content:
Final Demand emerged best of the army of returning Willie Mullins stars on show after a thrilling finish to the John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase.

With Henry de Bromhead's mare The Big Westerner a non-runner due to unsuitable ground, the champion trainer saddled each of the nine remaining runners, with last year's winner and subsequent Cheltenham Gold Cup hero Gaelic Warrior the 10/11 favourite in the hands of Paul Townend.

Kitzbuhel and Daniel King took the field along for much of the two-and-a-half-mile journey, closely pursued by 8/1 shot Final Demand and Patrick Mullins, with Fact To File and Gaelic Warrior next in line.

With the latter unable to quicken sufficiently to get himself into a challenge position, it was the 2024 winner and last year's runner-up Fact To File who looked most likely to prevail when taking over the lead on the run-in, but Final Demand battled bravely to get back up by a neck.

"It was a fantastic race. Very few of my horses were disappointing, they all ran well enough and I was happy with them," said Mullins.

"What a result, for the Mullins family, not just Closutton. To see Patrick riding a Grade One winner and dare I say it, maybe outriding Harry Cobden from the last home.

"Patrick said he thought he had the race won but he just missed the last and he had to win it a second time. So that just shows how much this horse has improved from last year.

"In against those top-class horses, he was good the whole way around. I was amazed at what turn of foot he showed from the last home. I thought when he made that little error that was enough and Fact To File would go on and win. He got down and ground it out. For a second season novice, that's a huge result."

Bookmakers cut Final Demand's Cheltenham Gold Cup odds to 7/1 from 14/1, while easing Gaelic Warrior to 5/2 from 13/8.

Gaelic Warrior's owner Rich Ricci was not too disappointed with the defeat of his star chaser.

He said: "Paul was happy enough, he obviously needed the run. He said he blew up a couple of times and got boxed in a little bit, but couldn't go fast enough to keep with them.

"He rides like more of a three miler these days, but Paul was very positive and said he wouldn't swap him for anything yet. Let's see how it goes.

"For him it's all about the spring, I think. Last year he won here, lost at Christmas, lost at the Dublin Racing Festival and then won the last two at Cheltenham and Punchestown, so hopefully he can repeat his spring successes."

Sports.title: Burnley’s wait for a home win goes on as Blackburn twice hit back in derby
Sports.content:
Todd Cantwell's penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since head coach Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues.

In a gripping, physical east Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani's rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel's steered finish after the break.

But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn's first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted.

Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. They have dropped 25 points from winning positions in the Sky Bet Championship this season.

Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was set to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back.

Their players warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message 'We're with you, Tony' on the back and the number 900 on the front.

Coaches Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have taken charge in Mowbray's absence and had to reshuffle the defence when Tom Atcheson was concussed after receiving a boot to the face in the third minute.

Stand-in goalkeeper Aynsley Pears, playing after Balazs Toth suffered a broken hand on international duty with Hungary, pushed over a fierce deflected shot from Banel, but was at fault when Ramazani gave Burnley a 27th-minute lead.

The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react.

But Gudjohnsen equalised four minutes later, racing on to a Harry Pickering long ball that drifted over Burnley centre-back Max Alleyne, and steering a sweet shot beyond goalkeeper Max Weiss for his 12th goal of the season. The Icelander celebrated by grabbing a t-shirt paying tribute to Mowbray from a photographer and displaying it for the cameras.

Blackburn finished the first half strongly, with Cantwell firing over a good chance, before Banel restored Burnley's lead six minutes into the second half, running unchallenged to place a shot into the far corner as defender Hayden Carter backed off.

The home side were fortunate to escape a strong penalty appeal just before the hour mark as Cantwell burst into the penalty area and saw two attempted crosses both strike the arm of Igor Julio.

Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker's leg. Cantwell drove the penalty straight down the middle to make it 2-2.

Gudjohnsen thought he had given Blackburn the lead two minutes later, when he controlled and drove a low shot against the base of the post with Weiss a spectator, but neither side could find a winner.
