Sports.title: BEN YOUNGS: Why James Bond and Eddie Jones inspired England's fast start against the All Blacks... and watching Lewis Moody step out with the boys was one of the most powerful things I've ever seen at Twickenham
Sports.content:
I’ll never forget sitting in an England team meeting in 2018 when Eddie Jones suddenly put a James Bond film on the big screen. As our assistant coach at the time, Steve Borthwick was in the room, too, taking notes as he always does.

It was the opening scene from Quantum of Solace, with Daniel Craig caught up in a high-speed car chase around Lake Garda in his Aston Martin. Engines roaring, bullets flying, windscreens smashed, flying around corners on the edge of a cliff.

Funnily enough, Daniel Craig came into the dressing room a couple of times after our matches. He filled the changing room with champagne bottles during the 2013 Lions tour of Australia. He played a little bit of rugby in the Wirral before his acting career took off.

It felt like one of those lessons at school where you get to watch a movie instead of working! I loved it. But after a couple of minutes, Eddie stopped the film and asked everyone a question.

‘Right boys, what have you just watched? What’s the common theme in a James Bond film?’

I hadn’t worked it out. I was just enjoying the car chase. But Eddie wanted to make a point about fast starts. James Bond films don’t waste 20 minutes getting going. They explode into action from the opening scene, grabbing your attention immediately.

Henry Slade scored early on for England as they made yet another brilliant start to a match

That’s exactly what Eddie wanted from England.

Now Borthwick is instilling a similar mentality. England keep big databases of GPS data and training history and that will have helped Borthwick fix his team’s slow starts. Don’t forget that England were 12-0 down after 19 minutes when they played the All Blacks last year.

Their hard work is clearly paying dividends. They have started fast in their victories over Fiji, Argentina, Japan and Australia and we saw the same philosophy against New Zealand. Maybe they should invite Robert Pattinson, the new 007, into camp!

There are different ways of approaching those opening 20 minutes. You can decide to manage the game, kick long, play territory and minimise risk. A lot of teams do that. It might be effective, but it can also mean half your players spend the first quarter chasing kicks without ever feeling involved.

As a scrum-half, I know how frustrating that can be. You can spend 15 minutes running around without getting your hands on the ball or making a meaningful contribution. England’s approach is completely different now.

They’re holding onto possession, moving the ball and dictating the tempo. It’s got Lee Blackett’s fingerprints all over it. Suddenly everyone is involved. Forwards are carrying, backs are getting touches and players are making tackles and clearing rucks.

That gives the whole team a foothold in the game.

Henry Slade scored a peach of a try after five minutes on Saturday. England spotted the opportunity, with Cam Roigard and Beauden Barrett in New Zealand’s defensive line. It was brilliant space ID.

Seb Atkinson is growing into the No 12 shirt and adding refined touches to his game

England’s start was aggressive, accurate and relentless. New Zealand barely had a chance to breathe. Slade was part of that squad in 2018 so he knows all about Eddie’s methods.

That all comes back to your preparations in the week. Under Eddie, we’d do our warm ups and activations on the 4G pitch but the intensity would go through the roof the moment we stepped onto the grass. There was no mucking around. You were down on your chest, doing these horrible shuttle runs, until everyone was gasping for air.

Then, with no chance to recover, we’d go straight into a game Eddie called ‘ruck and run’. It was 12 against 12, using the full length of the pitch. Five-man lineouts, quick ball and absolutely no standing around. If the ball was too slow, Eddie would kick it behind you and suddenly the opposition were attacking. It was relentless.

The idea was to fly straight into a training session that was more intense than anything we’d experience on a Saturday. It tuned your body as well as your mind to fire from the moment the game kicks off. Sometimes we would even train in full England kit. It was smart coaching.

Borthwick helped drive those sessions. He understood that starting fast wasn’t simply about running around with steam coming out of your ears. There had to be accuracy and calmness alongside the intensity. That’s what impressed me most about England’s performance against New Zealand. Fin Smith’s thinking was crystal clear when he kicked the ball through for Slade’s opening try.

A fast start isn’t necessarily about scoring a try in the opening five minutes – but that’s definitely a bonus. It’s about building pressure. It’s seeing Alex Coles, Maro Itoje and Ollie Chessum steaming down at Roigard’s kicking foot at the very first box kick. It’s about intent.

Once again, their breakdown work was excellent, their exits were efficient and they barely allowed New Zealand into their half. England had 74 percent of the territory and 65 percent of the possession against a team which usually prides itself on building pressure with its phase play. It was really pleasing to see George Furbank running the ball back – with guys like Ben Earl on his shoulder – rather than kicking it back for guys like Barrett to run from deep.

I was concerned England might revert to a more conservative approach against the All Blacks. It’s one thing throwing the ball around against Japan, but quite another doing it against New Zealand.

One moment just before half-time summed up the change in mentality. England were leading 19-5 when New Zealand chipped the ball away and England regained possession. There was an easy option to kick the ball into touch and head for the dressing room with a comfortable lead.

During the Six Nations, England would probably have done exactly that. Instead, they went through four or five phases, looking for another opportunity to attack. Only when they realised there was nothing on did they kick the ball out. Fin Smith would always look to play at Northampton and now he’s getting to show more of his true self in England colours.

England hammered the All Blacks at Twickenham and are developing into a top side

It’s a mindset shift from survival to dominance. They’re playing a style of rugby that suits the players they’ve got. A lot of teams run a pod of three forwards off the scrum half. England are now running their pod of three forwards off the fly-half, which cuts out a couple of defenders and helps you reach a wider reference point on the pitch much earlier. It allowed them to really manipulate the defence and they dominated every attacking statistic.

England’s strike plays from the lineout were very sharp, too. New Zealand were using Will Jordan as the first defender off lineouts and England were targeting that channel with the likes of Earl and Seb Atkinson.

Atkinson is growing into the No 12 shirt. Every time I watch him, I see more little touches that I like. He offers England a really effective combination of power, intelligence and distribution alongside Smith.

Then you look at the firepower they can bring off the bench.

Ellis Genge, George Martin, Luke Cowan-Dickie, Will Stuart and Greg Fisilau are serious reinforcements. Throw Henry Pollock into the equation and suddenly you’ve got a team whose power actually increases towards the end of matches.

You can never underestimate the importance of the gainline in international rugby.

England now have the ability to dominate it for 80 minutes.

I was also really impressed by Cadan Murley. It hasn’t quite happened for him on the international stage until now, but he delivered a really eye-catching performance.

He wasn’t necessarily expecting to play and Will Joseph had been outstanding against Japan the previous week. With Tommy Freeman unavailable, Murley stepped in and took his opportunity.

England are developing genuine depth. Watching the match, I found myself asking a question I don’t think I’ve ever asked before. How many of those New Zealand players would I actually put into this England team? There weren’t many. England look fresh, energised and full of confidence. New Zealand, by contrast, looked like a team crawling towards the finish line.

Cadan Murley came in for Tommy Freeman and produced one of his best displays

RASSIE'S WEIRD WATCHALONG

I had a quick look at the Rassie Erasmus watch-along of South Africa’s defeat by Ireland. It was one of the weirdest things I’ve seen in a long time, with the bottle of brandy in the background!

We all want to uphold rugby values and Erasmus deserves his ban for kicking off at the match officials. We all know the rules. Richard Cockerill coached me for years and he faced the odd suspension for similar offences.

Coaches are often entitled to be frustrated about refereeing. The big takeaway from this is there have got to be better channels to effectively feedback your thoughts without doing it in public. It’s clearly not quite working.

MOVING MOODY

Watching my old mate Lewis Moody step out with the boys for the haka was incredibly moving. In fact, it was one of the most powerful things I’ve ever seen at Twickenham.

I played a lot of rugby with Lewis for Leicester and England. Seeing him walk onto the pitch with Maro Itoje was overwhelming.

Lewis was one of the most inspirational team-mates you could ever have. He had an almost complete disregard for his own body. He was relentless in his pursuit of the ball and would put himself on the line for the team every single time.

Those bonds you form through rugby don’t disappear when you stop playing, no matter whether you’re playing for England or Holt RFC. Lewis is one of ours and everyone wanted him to know that.

There is no doubt that it helped energise England in the first few minutes of the game.

How you respond to the haka is always a big talking point. We got it right before we played New Zealand in the 2019 World Cup semi-final.

It was incredibly moving to see Lewis Moody join the England team for the Haka

Eddie told the leadership group we should do something to welcome the challenge, but left it up to us to decide what. We settled on the V formation and explained the plan to the players at our Friday-night meeting.

Everyone seemed to understand until Luke Cowan-Dickie put his hand up.

‘I don’t quite understand what I need to do.’

We ended up drawing a giant V on a board with little crosses representing the players.

Luke looked at it and asked: ‘So which one am I?’

We told him: ‘Dickie, it doesn’t matter, mate. Just stand somewhere. It’ll be obvious!’

Thankfully, it worked out!

Sports.title: Sol Campbell puts his stunning £13.5million country pile up for sale (...huge portrait of his face above the dining room mantelpiece not included)
Sports.content:
Sol Campbell has put his magnificent £13.5million country pile up for sale - but it's not the heated swimming pool, full-size tennis court or private cinema that has people talking.

Instead, prospective house-hunters have been left amused that the ex-England defender has decorated the walls of his lavish Berkshire mansion with giant portraits of... himself.

Campbell, 52, has offered prospective buyers a glimpse inside his sprawling 23-acre estate which he shares with his interior designer wife Fiona Barratt-Campbell, 46.

And while Grade II-listed Forbury House boasts all the trappings of a millionaire ex-footballer's dream home, it is the larger-than-life wall art that has raised eyebrows.

In one particularly striking photograph shown on Rightmove, a giant image of the no-nonsense centre-half dominates the wall above a dining room fireplace

The imposing picture shows Campbell staring straight ahead, keeping a watchful eye over guests as they tuck into dinner.

Sol Campbell, 52, is hoping to secure the £13.5million sale of his sprawling Grade II-listed Forbury House near Hungerford in Berkshire

But it's not the heated swimming pool, full-size tennis court or private cinema that has people talking - it's the fact that the listing includes a giant portrait of the star on the dining room wall

Campbell also appears in a second huge portrait hanging on the wall in a thoroughfare to the boot room, looking every inch the country gent with a rifle and noise mufflers in the picture

The first portrait has previous featured in a Channel 4 show about the England star's former home in Northumberland, the property he owned when he played for Newcastle United

Sol married his wife Fiona Barratt-Campbell, 46, in July 2010 at St Andrew's Church in Corbridge, Northumberland, after the couple had been together around four years

It is likely to be the same portrait which previously took pride of place at Hallington Hall; the couple's former £5.9m mansion in Northumberland, where visitors were also greeted by framed football shirts collected during his illustrious playing career.

Another wall-sized portrait in a boot room shows Campbell in profile as the country man, wearing ear defenders and appearing to be carrying a shotgun.

The enormous portraits have not gone unnoticed among eagle-eyed house viewers online, who were quick to poke fun at the former footballer's rather unusual choice of art.

One amused Reddit user said of the 16,400 sq ft, seven-bedroom estate: 'Wow that's actually pretty tasteful, except for all the blown up Sol Campbell photos.'

Another admitted: 'I'd be so embarrassed to have huge pictures of myself hanging above the fireplace. But the house is just (sigh) absolutely gorgeous.'

And a third said: 'I could do without the...massive pictures of Sol, but that's lovely.'

Sol, who has three children with Fiona, granddaughter of Sir Lawrie Barratt, multi-millionaire founder of Barratt Homes, posts pictures of the Berkshire home he is trying to sell - like this one of a dog overlooking the full size tennis court in the 23 acres of grounds

The star's social media also shows off the garden in all of its glory on a hazy summer's day

Whoever has pockets deep enough to buy the stunning home will get use of the heated swimming pool within a secluded walled garden - and a pool house for entertaining

Forbury House, near Kintbury, sits among rolling Berkshire countryside and includes a heated outdoor swimming pool within a secluded walled garden, alongside a pool house.

There is also a tennis court, lake, greenhouse and kitchen garden.

Campbell, 52, earned a fortune from football, most notably from the bumper four-year £20m contract he got when he moved to Arsenal from bitter rivals Spurs in 2001.

He and wife Fiona, an interior designer and granddaughter of Sir Lawrie Barratt, founder of Barratt Homes, have three children.

The couple have reportedly built up a property empire worth £50million through the years including a west London home worth £25m. They also own a high-end furniture company together.

Sports.title: Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapses during post-match interview as journalist tries to break his fall after he 'felt dizzy' at the end of the first half of Boca Juniors' cup glory
Sports.content:
Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapsed during a live interview immediately after winning a trophy with his Boca Juniors side.

The 32-year-old was one of the focal points of a World Cup side that reached the final last summer, and went on to win the Copa Sudamericana on Saturday evening after beating Brazil's Atletico Mineiro 2-0 in Barranquilla.

But amid the thick humidity and Colombian heat, Paredes became overwhelmed moments after lifting the trophy.

After giving a brief interview, Paredes was captured closing his eyes, before falling towards the interviewer, who attempted to break his fall.

Instead, the former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder hit the ground, with attendants rushing to help him after his collapse.

Paredes had been taken off in the second-half after suffering from heat-related dizziness, with humidity at 80 per cent heading into the match, and 32-degree-temperatures.

Leandro Parades collapsed to the floor during a post-match interview after winning the Copa Sudamericana with Boca Juniors

The interviewer attempted to break his fall as the former PSG crumpled to the turf

'He felt dizzy towards the end of the first-half,' his manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena explained of the substitution. 'He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second-half, you could see he was struggling.'

Fortunately, Paredes was revived quickly and treated in the treatment room, before re-joining his team's celebrations after claiming the South American trophy.

The star shared a brief statement on social media confirming he was fine after the interview aired.

'We're fine,' Paredes confirmed with a picture taken during treatment, before adding in a separate caption: 'Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just a dizziness from so many turns together'.

Paredes' triumph for his club side comes months after agonising defeat to Spain in New York at the World Cup final in July.

Argentina were felled by a solitary goal from Ferran Torres to end their reign as world champions, before the match descended into petty scraps - with Paredes at the heart of the bad behaviour.

Paredes furiously shoved Spain substitute Gavi to the floor after the final whistle blew, earning himself a punchy 10-match suspension from FIFA.

He faced three assault charges, while teammate Nahuel Molina faced two, and both players were also fined $90,000 (£66,000).

Paredes himself admitted that the length of the ban had put his international future under consideration.

'It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team,' Paredes told the media in September. 'Because of the suspension as well, because of (Lionel Messi) Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

'I haven't discussed it with the coach (Lionel Scaloni) yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make.'

Paredes' announcement came just days after Messi decided to hang up his international boots, with the talismanic Argentina superstar treated to a magnificent send-off during the early Autumn international break.

'Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled,' Paredes added.

Paredes updated fans after the incident to confirm he was okay before rejoining the festivities with his team-mates (Source: Instagram/Leandro Parades)

'We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us.'

Although unable to compete alongside him in their country's colours for one last time, Paredes joined Messi on the pitch in Buenos Aires for his final farewell, and shared an emotional tribute post to his former captain.

'THANK YOU FOR ABSOLUTELY EVERYTHING CAPTAIN,' he captioned a carousel of photos of himself and Messi.

'It was a dream to be able to have achieved everything we achieved together and to have defended this shirt and our country with you, I'm leaving and we'll miss you always.

'It was a pleasure to be one of your soldiers for all these years and I will be forever! I love you buddy.'

Sports.title: The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star eyes new lucrative deal with clubs circling, writes MATT BARLOW
Sports.content:
The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star eyes new lucrative deal with clubs circling, writes MATT BARLOW

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

Williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old said he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

This is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Similarities are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No.10 position.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals

He does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

His brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Here, they rose to salute a new talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

The Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' said De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

Spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Currently under contract until 2028, the 18-year-old has rival clubs circling if Spurs cannot pin him down

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side

Williams-Barnett is under contract until 2028 but is understood to be closing in on a lucrative new deal to tie him down because others have been circling.

It is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping issues but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

Although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' said De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and said it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

There was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'Mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

The pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

Sports.title: Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Big Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters
Sports.content:
Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Big Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

To use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Big Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

So why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic big boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the issues we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

City had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

Iraola is aware of all this and said on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month

‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a big game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’

Asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – said: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’

In Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

Against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

In both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

To take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's big boys

And that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their new manager in a few weeks.’

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

But Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

Isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the big boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

Iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

‘I said at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Big Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

But a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

Sports.title: Ange Postecoglou bites back at Sadio Mane question after ex-Liverpool star misses match
Sports.content:
Ange Postecoglou bites back at Sadio Mane question after ex-Liverpool star misses match

Ex-Liverpool star Sadio Mane was absent for Al-Nassr's 3-1 defeat to Al-Ahli in the Saudi Pro League on Friday, having chosen to attend the birth of his first child with his wife

View 2 Images Ange Postecoglou snapped at a journalist (Image: Thmanyah Sports)

Ange Postecoglou took a reporter to task after they questioned why Sadio Mane missed Al-Nassr's game for the birth of his second child. Former Liverpool star Mane was absent as his team-mates were beaten 3-1 away to Al-Ahli in the Saudi Pro League.

‌



‌



Cristiano Ronaldo had given Al-Nassr an early lead before missing a penalty. Al-Ahli capitalised and staged a comeback, with England international Ivan Toney among the goalscorers.

‌



Post-match, a journalist asked Postecoglou whether Mane's decision to be with wife Aisha Tamba showed a lack of commitment to the club. "Are you a father? Do you have children?" the ex-Tottenham boss snapped.

‌



The reporter replied 'no', to which Postecoglou said: "That's probably why you ask the question. Because when you do, you'll realise it's the most important thing, the biggest blessing you can have.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"[Mane] is with his wife while she is having a baby, okay? Nothing is more important in life. Yes he had my permission, my blessing, and Sadio Mane is one of the best people in this world, mate. Never question him or his commitment to this football club."

Postecoglou is no stranger to a fiery or tense interview, having become renowned for them during his time in the Premier League. The 61-year-old regularly had awkward conversations with journalists while in charge of Tottenham and briefly Nottingham Forest.

‌



After Al-Nassr lost 4-0 to Al-Ain in the Asian Champions League in September, Postecoglou told a reporter who'd claimed that Ronaldo had done 'nothing' in the match: "You're watching a different game to me."

Friday's loss was only Al-Nassr's third since Postecoglou took over in the summer. But they remain third in the league table, two points behind Al-Hilal, who have a game in hand.

‌



View 2 Images Sadio Mane married Aisha Tamba in 2024 (Image: magvision_evens_officiel/Instagram)

Mane has scored three goals and provided eight assists in 15 appearances this season. The winger joined Al-Nassr in the summer of 2023 following a year at Bayern Munich.

‌



That came after spending six trophy-laden seasons at Anfield, helping Liverpool win both the Premier League and Champions League. Mane burst onto the scene in English football across two years at Southampton.

Away from the pitch, Mane married Tamba in 2024. The couple, who can count on Mane's eye-watering £650,000 per week contract, welcomed a baby girl last year.

Sports.title: Inside Mauricio Pochettino's huge fortune and private family life as he joins Man Utd
Sports.content:
Inside Mauricio Pochettino's huge fortune and private family life as he joins Man Utd

Mauricio Pochettino has taken charge at Manchester United and will no doubt face scrutiny - but his wife has long been his most candid critic

View 4 Images Mauricio Pochettino has the support of his close-knit family (Image: Getty)

Mauricio Pochettino is taking on one of football's most intensely examined roles as Manchester United's new manager. However, nobody will scrutinise the Argentine quite like his cherished partner.

‌



‌



There's been a major shake-up at Old Trafford. With Michael Carrick shown the door, it's Pochettino who's now in the hot seat. The ex-Tottenham and Chelsea boss has signed a contract running until 2028 and faces his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday.

‌



The 54-year-old has departed his position with the USMNT for this fresh challenge and backing him as he attempts to lift United clear of the drop zone are his beloved wife Karina and sons Maurizio and Sebastiano - the latter being a sports scientist who's joined the coaching setup at Carrington.

‌



Pochettino will likely face unprecedented scrutiny as United boss, so Mirror Football examines his private life beyond the touchline, including an in-depth look at his family circumstances and his remarkable net worth.

Second Man Utd rule change as Mauricio Pochettino makes offer to players ahead of Liverpool READ MORE :

Mauricio Pochettino sends Pep Guardiola two-word message over becoming USA boss READ MORE :

Who is Mauricio Pochettino's wife?

Pochettino initially encountered his partner, Karina, at a nightclub in Rosario back in 1991 and the pair connected instantly. The Argentine had recently established himself in the Newell's Old Boys senior squad.

View 4 Images Pochettino has been married to Karina for over three decades (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The couple wed in 1994 and have stayed together ever since, with Karina following Pochettino to Barcelona when he joined Espanyol as a player that same year, before he subsequently returned to manage the club in 2009. She has been his "rock" throughout his stints as a manager in the Premier League, at Paris Saint-Germain and in the United States.

‌



Karina is renowned for keeping an extremely low profile. She has no public social media presence and seldom gives interviews or attends matches. Nevertheless, Pochettino has offered insight into her influence on his life.

In 2018, during his time at Spurs, Pochettino was quizzed on whether his wife ever criticises him. He said: "Many things. Many, many times. It's more than 25 years now she's been next to me and in the last few years the one thing that she criticises most is my press conferences.

‌



"Because she is very focused, 'Why you say that', 'You need to say to, not for', 'That is why, not because.' She is fixing me after every press conference and criticises me a lot. But it is part of it to improve, no?"

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



What is Mauricio Pochettino's net worth?

Despite his modest upbringing, having grown up on a farm in the province of Santa Fe, Argentina, Pochettino has accumulated a staggering fortune through his years as one of the world's most sought-after managers. According to The Sun, Pochettino is worth £40million.

View 4 Images The Argentine has amassed a stellar fortune (Image: Getty)

‌



This wealth has been accumulated through his 17-year playing career and several lucrative managerial positions. When he was dismissed by Tottenham in 2019, a reported £12.5m severance package was paid to him and his coaching team.

When Pochettino departed PSG three years later, another £8.5m compensation was provided. He was also earning £10m per season at Chelsea and his yearly salary with the US was £4.6m.

‌



His financial position has enabled Pochettino to maintain properties in Barcelona and London. It remains unknown where he will reside during his spell with United.

Who are Mauricio Pochettino's sons?

Pochettino has two sons: Maurizio and Sebastiano. The younger Maurizio, who is 25, is currently forging a career as a professional footballer. He developed his abilities in both Southampton and Tottenham's youth systems before signing for Watford in 2021.

‌



He featured in Championship matches at Vicarage Road before transferring to Spain with Gimnastic Tarragona and subsequently Ibiza IP. Maurizio now represents Andorran club Inter Club d'Escaldes.

Sebastiano, meanwhile, is an accomplished sports scientist and fitness coach. He is already at Carrington, having arrived early as part of his father's new backroom team.

‌



View 4 Images Sebastiano now works for United (Image: Getty)

The 31-year-old studied sports science in England while his dad managed Southampton. Sebastiano worked alongside Pochettino at Tottenham, PSG, Chelsea and with the US.

Article continues below

He will spearhead Pochettino's rigorous fitness approach at United, which places emphasis on recovery methods and stamina assessment.

This is arguably the most significant transformation Pochettino will introduce to United and whether he succeeds or fails, his family will always stand behind him.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino left key player out of starting XI and gave blunt explanation
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino left key player out of starting XI and gave blunt explanation

Mauricio Pochettino froze out Christian Pulisic in his former job as USA boss,

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino has shown he's prepared to make big decisions (Image: Getty)

Mauricio Pochettino has previously taken a tough stance when naming a starting XI, with the new Manchester United boss set to pick his very first Red Devils team.

‌



‌



Pochettino has inherited something of a mess at Old Trafford, and one of his toughest jobs will be keeping the big egos in check. Deciding who to play and who to bench can create divisions in a squad, but the Argentine has shown in the past he's not one to be challenged in this area.

‌



In his former job as USA boss, Pochettino froze out Christian Pulisic after the AC Milan forward requested to play in two friendlies, but be rested for the Gold Cup.

‌



Pochettino didn't take kindly to the request, and instead left Pulisic out of the matches against Turkey and Switzerland. He said: "Players [do] not need to understand or not understand.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"Players need to listen and to stick with our plan. They cannot dictate the plan. The most important thing is that we explained why we decided not to include [him] in the two friendly games. Then if you have some problems, no, that is not my problem to understand. I am the head coach; I am not a mannequin."

Pulisic discussed the fallout on CBS Sports, saying he "respected" Pochettino's decision but "didn't understand it". He added that those questioning his commitment to the USA team were "way out of line".

‌



Pochettino will pick his first Man United team this Sunday as the Red Devils take on bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

View 2 Images Christian Pulisic wasn't happy with Mauricio Pochettino (Image: John Dorton/USSF, Getty Images)

‌



Ahead of the game, he said: "We are so excited to be here, and I think it's an amazing club. We are happy, but at the same time, so busy. I think it's a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool.

"We arrive with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy with the way we love to work. We have found supportive people in the club.

‌



"But at the same time, we need to improve our players and find a way to perform. The identity and the culture of the club are very clear; it's a historic club with years as one of the best in the world."

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes shows true colours with behaviour at full-time after brutal Newcastle boos
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes shows true colours with behaviour at full-time after brutal Newcastle boos

Arsenal star Bruno Guimaraes left Newcastle United in the summer and was playing at St James' Park for the first time since his exit as the Gunners were held to a draw

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes was booed on his return to St James' Park (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

There was no hero's welcome for Arsenal star Bruno Guimaraes as he returned to Newcastle for the first time since his summer transfer. The Magpies held the Premier League leaders to a draw at St James' Park on an occasion when the Toon Army expressed exactly how they felt.

‌



‌



Guimaraes was booed on his way into the ground, when he warmed up and during the match, but nevertheless took the time to complete a lap of the ground, waving to the crowd, following the full-time whistle. The midfielder received a few rounds of applause but was still met with a negative response from many of those remaining in the ground in the North East.

‌



Such was the sustained hostility, Guimaraes could only show a glum expression as he made his way back to the tunnel to head towards the dressing room. The 29-year-old, who captained Newcastle to their first domestic trophy in 70 years, was, however, offered a warmer greeting by his former teammates.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Guimaraes was embraced by figures such as Malick Thiaw and Tino Livramento as he was crowded in the centre of the field following the game. The Brazilian could be seen having positive interactions with members of Newcastle's backroom team too.

‌



The former Newcastle star could not help his new team to three points on his old stomping ground. The Gunners took the lead in a commanding first-half performance when Eberechi Eze opened the scoring.

Matthias Jaissle's side fought back after the break as Harvey Barnes and Thiaw turned the game on its head. David Raya was forced off the field with an injury, while Guimaraes was replaced by Myles Lewis-Skelly as Mikel Arteta attempted to get his side back in the clash.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes applauds the Newcastle United fans (Image: Lee Parker - CameraSport via Getty Images)

View 3 Images Arsenal player Bruno Guimaraes with Malick Thiaw (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

‌

Noni Madueke scored the crucial goal to equalise after 78 minutes, and neither side found a further breakthrough. Newcastle boss Jaissle was pleased with the atmosphere that pushed his side on in the second half.

‌



"That helps," he said. "If you find that synergy between the players and the fans, then our playing style then you can build something successful.

"We're at the stage of the season where we need to be humble and realistic. A point against the best team in the Premier League is something we can build on."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta issues David Raya update after injury that 'could change everything' for Arsenal
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta issues David Raya update after injury that 'could change everything' for Arsenal

David Raya suffered a worrying injury during the second half of Arsenal's draw with Newcastle, with the Gunners goalkeeper forced to leave the game at St James' Park

View 3 Images David Raya of Arsenal is helped to his feet after suffering an injury vs Newcastle

Mikel Arteta has confirmed David Raya will undergo an MRI after the goalkeeper was forced off during the clash with Newcastle United.

‌



‌



The Gunners moved six points clear at the top of the Premier League table after settling for a point following a thrilling encounter at St James' Park. Arsenal took the lead through Eberechi Eze, before a quickfire double from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw put the Magpies in front.

‌



But Noni Madueke scored the all-important equaliser to ensure the shares were spoiled. That goal came after worrying scenes for the Gunners with Raya leaving the game following a worrying looking injury.

‌



Raya received lengthy treatment, before leaving the pitch holding his arm and clearly in pain. Speaking after the game, Arsenal boss Arteta said: "Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news. He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don't know."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Kepa Arrizabalaga came off the bench and helped the Gunners to their point, but Sky Sports pundit Jamie Redknapp warned a significant injury could have major ramifications to Arsenal's title challenge.

"Arsenal's squad, they have two players in every position. The fact that their goalkeeper David Raya walked off that pitch, he looked like he was in severe pain. That is the one player that is irreplaceable in that team.

‌



"Kepa is not up to the level of him. I actually think he struggles in the Premier League. Obviously we've seen him in the Carabao Cup last year in the final.

View 3 Images Raya pointed to his shoulder before receiving treatment

‌



"He's now going to have to play some games and that's going to be difficult for him and that will change everything for Arsenal for a while.

"So that's a massive blow depending on how long David Raya is out because he is, as I say, irreplaceable - probably the best goalkeeper in the Premier League, if not one of the best in the world."

‌



Following Manchester City's draw with Fulham, Arsenal had the chance to build a commanding eight-point lead at the top, but failed to capitalise after a dominant first-half performance.

And goalscorer Madueke pulled no punches with his verdict on their struggles after the break, suggesting his teammates may have been too relaxed.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal moved six points clear at the top after drawing with Newcastle

He said: "The second half, we weren't at our standard in the first 20 minutes and when you give this crowd and team belief it's difficult. In the end I think 2-2 is a fair result.

Article continues below

"You know what to expect form Newcastle at home. The first 20 minutes of the second half is us not sticking by our own principles. I don't know if we were too relaxed after our first-half performance."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta has given Man Utd the perfect blueprint - but INEOS have to completely change
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has given Man Utd the perfect blueprint - but INEOS have to completely change

Mauricio Pochettino has now started work at Manchester United and if he's in need of any inspiration when it comes to turning a club's fortunes around, he should look no further than his old PSG team-mate Mikel Arteta

View 3 Images

Anfield feels an entirely fitting venue to uncover the size of the task Mauricio Pochettino has on his hands. It's a bear pit at the best of times - not least when there's an opportunity to inflict early misery upon a brand-new Manchester United manager.

‌



‌



For Liverpool, chances as good as this do not come around often. Sleep-deprived Poch heads to Merseyside with a blank canvas for a match poised to underline the importance of patience.

‌



Just ask the 54-year-old's former Paris Saint-Germain team-mate, Mikel Arteta. The Spaniard recently masterminded Arsenal's first Premier League victory at Anfield since 2012, when he was a player.

‌



However, it was also a landmark triumph that stretched far beyond three crucial and priceless top-flight points. That's because it also symbolised the Gunners' growth and ascension into a red-hot, rock-solid established force.

The champions are not everyone's cup of tea but under Arteta they have gone from a laughing stock to a serious outfit, capable of going toe-to-toe with just about any team on the planet.

They were thrashed 7-1 on aggregate across his first two league visits to Liverpool as Arsenal manager but after three defeats and three draws, Arsenal finally silenced The Kop on November 1 - without conceding a single shot on target.

‌



Some 25 years ago - during an 18-month loan spell with PSG - fresh-faced teenager Arteta did everything within his power to learn from Pochettino in the French capital.

Now the tables have turned because despite his respectable coaching pedigree, Poch simply has to try and emulate what Arteta has created, sculpted and gradually built at the Emirates - which has not happened overnight.

‌



It won't be a universally popular take, but the Basque is currently the gold-standard Premier League coach.

Having tinkered, controlled and overseen the seismic transformation of a big prestigious football club - while regularly competing with iconic managerial juggernauts such as Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp - Arteta has undeniably set the benchmark where rebuilds are concerned.

‌



View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has worked wonders at Arsenal but he needed significant backing from upstairs to turn the club's fortunes around (Image: Pavel Lebeda/Soccrates/Getty Images)

The great irony of it all is that Arsenal genuinely gave some consideration to offering Pochettino the job, ahead of Arteta, back in 2019.

‌



Whether he would have taken it, on the back of his love affair with Tottenham, is a question we will never truly know the answer to but ultimately, there is no guarantee he would have had the same level of success as the title-winning Men's Coach of the Year nominee.

Equally, Arteta couldn't have done it without significant backing. He flirted with the sack in August 2021 following a 5-0 drubbing at Manchester City but dared to be great by slowly discarding the club's top-earners such as Mesut Ozil and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, respectively.

‌



Pochettino, who has long been eyeing the keys to the kingdom at Old Trafford, knows a thing or two about squad-building having fired Spurs to the Champions League final seven-and-a-half years ago.

The United is an entirely different beast, however. In many respects, it has been a poisoned chalice since the departure of Sir Alex Ferguson back in 2013.

‌



The Argentine needs time to implement his ideas but with INEOS under greater scrutiny than ever following a series of high-profile mistakes, he's entering a pressure-cooker environment that has eaten up so many of his predecessors.

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first Manchester United match this weekend (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Given United are currently languishing in the relegation zone, swift results also feel somewhat imperative because commercially, the club needs Champions League football to flex their muscles in the transfer market.

Then there's an entirely separate argument that Pochettino is already handicapped by the faulty regime working above him.

‌



It's been claimed the Glazers overruled Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada in signing off the hire. Should that be true, the lack of alignment is a huge issue in itself while player recruitment under director of football Wilcox has been dismal.

On the back of a top-five finish under Michael Carrick, United needed to be efficient and clinical in the market. Instead, they burned cash and the team regressed.

‌



Pochettino is also the fourth head coach in situ in the past three years under Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

There is still no identity, no direction - it's chalk and cheese when compared with Arteta's working conditions at Arsenal - and until bold changes are made, the same problems will remain.

Sports.title: Newcastle and Arsenal play out thrilling draw as new Gunners concern emerges
Sports.content:
Newcastle United and Arsenal both had to settle for a point after a rollercoaster Premier League clash ended 2-2.

Eberechi Eze put the Gunners in front, before Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw turned the game on its head after the break. But Noni Madueke's goal was enough to secure Arsenal the point which moved them six clear at the top.

The Gunners quickly assumed control in front of a Newcastle crowd which was struggling to warm to new manager Matthias Jaissle.

After a tepid opening 45, Jaissle made a triple change and that sparked an immediate transformation with Barnes scoring the equaliser, before Thiaw put them in front just after the hour mark.

‌



Arsenal suffer brutal injury blow as David Raya leaves the pitch in agony vs Newcastle READ MORE :

Arsenal and Newcastle given detested new kick-off time for Premier League clash READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The visitors' night got even worse when David Raya was forced to leave the pitch with a worrying injury to his shoulder. But with Newcastle in the ascendancy, Arsenal showed their resilience to restore parity through Madueke.

Both sides pushed for a winner, but even with nine minutes added on, neither side were able to nick all three points.. Here's what we learned from an enthralling tie at St James' Park.

ARSENAL MISS THEIR CHANCE

Nobody of an Arsenal persuasion wanted to admit it, but when they were leading, dominating and about to go eight points clear at the top, they must have thought it. Could we be heading towards a title procession?

‌



Manchester City - ignoring the obvious elephant in the courtroom - look miles off the pace, while Liverpool have their own issues. Brighton are a good story and have looked brilliant, but it still feels unlikely they can match Arsenal over a 38-game season.

And while they still have a very healthy lead, this is a slight dent to the feeling of inevitability that would have accompanied a sixth straight win.

BRUNO'S UNHAPPY RETURN

Newcastle fans started their Premier League season by giving Alexander Isak an exceptionally hostile return to St James’ Park. That was to be expected, given the manner of the Swede’s exit and his antics before sealing a move to Liverpool.

‌



Bruno Guimaraes may have been hoping for a more pleasant reunion with the supporters that once adored him. After all, as recently as September, the Brazilian goaded Sunderland following his winning goal on Wearside

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes returned to Newcastle for the first time since his move to Arsenal

But if that was an attempt to curry favour with the Toon Army, it didn’t have much impact. He was roundly booed as he came off the Arsenal bus, but that was nothing compared to the reception each and every time he touched the ball.

The cauldron created for Isak’s return helped the home team get a result and while not as vitriolic as that afternoon, the atmosphere played a huge part again.

‌



Guimaraes didn't have his best evening in an Arsenal shirt and Arteta’s decision to withdraw the midfielder as they chased an equaliser brought a cheer as loud as either goal.

SEASON-DEFINING CHANGE

Jaissle needed something. While it hasn’t been a disastrous start to his tenure in the Toon dugout, supporters remained firmly unconvinced.

After watching back-to-back home defeats, a lifeless first half did little to win over any doubters. But the 15 minutes following the first 45 could be the period that completely changes the narrative on Tyneside.

View 4 Images Matthias Jaissle got the reaction he wanted after ringing the changes at half time

‌



For just the second time this season a Premier League manager made three changes at the break, such was the level of their first-half display. Fair to say it had an impact.

The comeback didn’t appear on the cards. Until it was. Newcastle looked like a team reborn in the second half and although it was only good enough for a point, the comeback offered a glimpse of what Jaissle’s team could really become.

RAYA CONCERN

The sight of David Raya going down in the Arsenal penalty area isn't an uncommon one. After shaking off a collision to the head, when he went down holding his shoulder many assumed the Spaniard had gone down for tactical reasons rather than anything more serious.

View 4 Images David Raya left the game with an injury

‌



But after lengthy treatment, Raya trudged off the pitch in agony with what appeared to be a shoulder injury. It can't be emphasised enough just how important the World Cup winner is to Arsenal's mean defence.

Kepa is a capable deputy, but a long period without their number one, after finally seeing William Saliba return to fitness would be a bitter blow for Arteta to swallow.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso speaks out as Chelsea fans turn on manager after Leeds thrashing
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso speaks out as Chelsea fans turn on manager after Leeds thrashing

Chelsea were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, with Xabi Alonso already under pressure just 11 games into his tenure as manager

View 2 Images Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso during his side's 4-1 defeat to Leeds

Xabi Alonso admits his Chelsea side are struggling in all aspects of the game after their painful home defeat to Leeds.

‌



After taking the lead through Emmanuel Emegha, Chelsea capitulated, eventually losing 4-1 to Daniel Farke’s impressive Leeds side.

Chelsea - who have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches - were loudly booed off by the home fans who have now seen home defeats to Tottenham and Leeds in the last month.

A section of the Stamford Bridge crowd turned on Alonso, chanting ‘you don’t know what you’re doing’ during the Leeds onslaught in the second half.

And Alonso accepts that there are serious issues with his side, claiming there is a fragility which is impacting everything else.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"We are disappointed and sad. It was tough to deal with the defeat and we're in a fragile moment,” he told BBC Sport.

"We have lost a bit of the confidence which we were playing with. It's a delicate moment but we have to go through it together and find solutions.

"The first half an hour was good but we conceded the equaliser and weren't too comfortable and lost some momentum. We could have done more in the second half but we didn't regain the confidence to have a real go and couldn't push hard enough to score one goal, which would have changed the momentum."

View 2 Images Leeds ran riot at Stamford Bridge to beat Chelsea

Asked to pinpoint Chelsea’s biggest issue, Alonso added: "Everything is related. It's the confidence, this fragility at the moment, the demand of the game, the physicality - everything is related."

It was a different story for Farke, who masterminded Leeds’ first win at Stamford Bridge since 1999 to move his charges just one point off the top four.

"We came here to win the game. We spoke the whole week about this and wanted to make this our game where we play on the front foot. We didn't want to allow Chelsea to control the mood,” Farke explained.

"We need to have good fitness levels and I have smart players who understand how we want to press and play. We have to be more concentrated to execute what we want to do. Desire is second to none, and we are competitive in the best league in the world."
