Ghana News.title: Prof. Francis Kwaw Andoh inducted as Principal of Enchi College of Education
Ghana News.content:
Prof. Francis Kwaw Andoh, an alumnus of Enchi College of Education, has been formally inducted as the new Principal of the institution in the Western North Region.

His investiture took place on November 20, 2026, at the college's auditorium, bringing together political leaders, traditional authorities, educationists, businesspeople, family members, colleagues, lecturers and students.

He succeeds Professor Philip Ntaah, who led the college from 2019 to 2025.

Among the dignitaries present were the Omanhene of the Aowin Traditional Area, Beyeman Tano Kwaw Benbuin III; Director-General of the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC), Professor Ahmed Jinapor Abdulai; and Chairman of the college's Governing Council, Dr Frank Kwekucher Ackah.

Professor Andoh is an economist, researcher and academic whose career spans classroom teaching, university administration, research and international development consultancy.

He began his professional career as a classroom teacher at Dadieso Primary School in Suaman, where he worked from 1997 to 1999. He later taught at Nkoranza Senior High/Technical School between 2002 and 2005 and Efutu Senior High/Technical School in 2006.

He obtained a bachelor's degree in Economics from the University of Cape Coast (UCC) in 2002, followed by an MPhil in Economics from the same university in 2008.

In 2010, he earned a Certificate in Cost Analysis in Education from UNESCO's International Institute for Educational Planning in Paris.

He subsequently received an international scholarship from the African Economic Research Consortium, sponsored by the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the Canadian Government, to pursue a PhD in Economics at the University of Dar es Salaam in Tanzania. He completed the programme in 2017.

His academic career at UCC began in 2007 as a Senior Research Assistant. He later became a Principal Research Assistant before moving into lecturing in 2010. He was promoted to Senior Lecturer in 2020 and appointed Associate Professor in February 2024.

At UCC, he also held several administrative positions, including Hall Tutor, Senior Hall Tutor and Hall Master of Atlantic Hall. He further served as Dean of the School of Economics before taking up his new role at Enchi College of Education.

Beyond academia, Professor Andoh has undertaken consultancy assignments for international organisations, including the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation, United Nations Population Fund, International Labour Organisation, Copenhagen Consensus Centre, Solidaridad West Africa and SNV Netherlands Development Organisation.

In 2019, he was appointed a Visiting Scholar at the IMF in Washington, DC, where he participated in research and academic discussions on fiscal and economic policy issues.

His research interests include macroeconomics, public finance, public policy and health economics, with particular focus on fiscal policy, public debt, healthcare financing, health insurance, foreign direct investment, inequality and multidimensional poverty.

He has also supervised and co-supervised doctoral and master's students, many of whom have gone on to occupy professional positions in Ghana and abroad.

Speaking after his induction, Professor Andoh said he would draw on his academic experience, professional networks and leadership skills to strengthen the college and advance teacher education in Ghana.

He called on staff to support his administration and work collectively towards the development of the institution and the training of teachers.

Professor Ahmed Jinapor Abdulai, in his remarks, commended the college for its recent performance and urged the lecturers, Governing Council and staff to rally behind the new Principal to drive further progress.

He also assured the institution that GTEC would collaborate with the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund) to facilitate the completion of abandoned projects on campus and the renovation of the college's auditorium.

Professor Andoh's appointment brings to Enchi College of Education an academic with experience in teaching, research, institutional administration and international development work.

Ghana News.title: I wanted a 5% fare increment, but transport operators are strong negotiators – Transport Minister
Ghana News.content:
Transport Minister Joseph Bukari Nikpe has disclosed that he initially proposed a 5% increase in public transport fares, but the negotiations with transport operators resulted in an 8% adjustment.

According to him, the proposed 5% increase contributed to a week-long negotiation with transport unions, who pushed for a higher adjustment before the final rate was agreed.

“Actually, I wanted 5%, and that delayed the one-week negotiation we were having. But you know they are also strong negotiators, so they were able to move to the 8%,” he stated on TV3's Hot Issues, Sunday, November 22.

GPRTU increased transport fares by 8%, effective Saturday, September 26, 2026.

The Deputy Public Relations Officer (PRO) of the GPRTU, Samuel Amoah, said the decision was reached after a final meeting with the Ministry of Transport on Tuesday, September 22, to discuss the proposed adjustment in fares.

According to him, the Union initially pushed for a 30% increase, arguing that failing to adjust fares would negatively affect drivers and transport operators.

“We were pushing for 30% and not coming down. But then during the meeting, the Minister also said that the President has given some directive and that hopefully we will have some more reduction on petroleum products."

The Minister explained that although there were discussions about maintaining the existing fares, the Union insisted that some adjustment was necessary to sustain operations.

Ghana News.title: Asante Kotoko suffer defeat against Bechem United on Stanley Menzo’s debut
Ghana News.content:
Bechem United claimed a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Asante Kotoko in Ghana Premier League Matchday 12, with Isaac Korankye scoring the decisive goal at the Nana Fosu Gyeabour Park.

Korankye, making his first start of the season, headed home in the 63rd minute to hand the Hunters all three points and spoil Stanley Menzo's first match in charge of the Porcupine Warriors.

Menzo, who was appointed head coach for the remainder of the 2026/27 campaign just three days before the encounter, was tasked with reviving Kotoko's struggling league campaign following a disappointing run of results under interim coach Hamza Obeng.

The visitors started brightly, with Hubert Gyau winning a free-kick in the Bechem half in the fifth minute. Emmanuel Sanja delivered the set-piece and found Richard Boadu, but the midfielder failed to make proper contact with the ball.

Kotoko continued to search for an opening, with Lawson Kyei Manu setting up Eric Gbetta in the penalty area in the 23rd minute, only for his effort to be blocked.

Bechem also threatened, and Samuel Okai came close to breaking the deadlock in the 30th minute when his effort flashed narrowly wide of the post.

The first half, which also saw Bechem's Baba Moro Abdulai and Kotoko's Umar Ali receive yellow cards, ended goalless despite promising moments from both sides.

Menzo introduced Opoku Agyemang at the break in place of Emmanuel Mamah as Kotoko looked to add more attacking threat.

However, the visitors struggled to turn their possession into clear-cut opportunities. A promising opening came in the 52nd minute when Umar Ali released Opoku inside the box, but the substitute's left-footed effort lacked the power to trouble Bechem goalkeeper Benjamin Asiedu.

The breakthrough arrived in the 63rd minute when Korankye rose highest to power a header into the net and give the hosts the lead.

Bechem nearly doubled their advantage four minutes later, but Kotoko goalkeeper Aziz Dari Haruna produced an excellent save to prevent the Hunters from extending their lead.

Kotoko made further changes in an attempt to rescue the game, introducing Derrick Anthony Duah, Seth Kwadwo and Solomon Asaah, while Bechem also made substitutions to protect their advantage.

Asante Kotoko pushed for an equaliser in the closing stages, with Asaah directing a header towards goal in the 86th minute, but the Bechem goalkeeper was equal to the task.

The hosts' resolve was tested further in stoppage time when Afranie Mensah was sent off for a foul on Asaah, leaving Bechem with 10 men for the closing moments.

Despite the numerical disadvantage, the Hunters defended resolutely to preserve their slender lead and secure a memorable victory.

The result represents a disappointing start to Menzo's tenure as head coach, with Kotoko missing the opportunity to improve their position in the league standings as they continue their pursuit of the leading sides.

Ghana News.title: GPL 2026/27: Berekum Chelsea beat Young Apsotles to move up on league table
Ghana News.content:
Berekum Chelsea bounced back to winning ways in the Ghana Premier League following their 2-1 victory over Young Apostles on Sunday afternoon.

The Berekum-based side claimed all three points on matchday 12 to move up thhe league table.

Chelsea came into the weekend in 10th position after picking up 15 points from their opening 11 games of the Premier League campaign, while Young Apostles had managed eight from the same period and were languishing in the 18th position on the league log.

It was more of a precautionary start for the two teams, as neither Chelsea nor Apostles wanted to leave spaces in behind their defence, keeping a cagey contest for the opening 30 minutes.

However, the home side found a way to unsettle the visitors.

Seidu Abubakari shot Chelsea into the lead after 34 minutes, breaking the deadlock to put them ahead against Young Apostles.

Six minutes into the second half, Jonah Attuquaye doubled the lead, putting the game beyond the reach of the visitors.

Despite conceding two goals, Young Apostles continued to search for a way back into the game and found one through Samuel Prempeh, who scored in the 67th minute to reduce the deficit.

The result lifts Chelsea three places to seventh in the league table after Basake Holy Stars, Swedru All Blacks and Aduana Football Club all failed to pick up maximum points.

Ghana News.title: Asikuma Inland Port to ease Tema Port congestion and create jobs in Asuogyaman – Mahama
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama says the construction of the Asikuma Inland Port will help ease congestion at the Tema Port while creating jobs and opening up economic opportunities for residents of Asuogyaman.

He says the facility, sponsored by LMI and financed by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), will serve as the southern terminal of the Volta Lake transport system when completed.

Speaking at the Odwira Akyi Akwasidae Kese and the 15th anniversary of the enstoolment of Odeneho Kwafo Akoto III as Akwamuhene, President Mahama said the project will be supported by an extension of the railway line from Mpakadan to Asikuma.

He explained that containers and other imports will be transported by rail from Tema to Asikuma, where they will be loaded onto barges and moved along the Volta River to Debre in the northern part of Ghana.

According to the President, the arrangement will provide a more seamless transportation route for Ghana's northern neighbours in the Sahel, particularly Burkina Faso, allowing them to move goods without having to travel all the way to Tema.

President Mahama said the development will not only reduce pressure on the Tema Port but also create opportunities for tourism and business through plans to establish a modern marina at Mpakadan.

"All these investments are going to create jobs for the young people of Asuogyaman," he said.

The President said the government will work closely with traditional authorities, the District Assembly, investors and local communities to ensure residents benefit directly from the development projects.

He stressed that development must translate into tangible benefits for the communities where such investments are undertaken.

"Development must not simply happen in our communities; it must happen for our communities," President Mahama stated.

He said his vision is to see Akwamu preserve its traditional heritage while embracing modern economic opportunities, adding that prosperity must be shared across all regions and communities.

Congratulating Odeneho Kwafo Akoto III on 15 years of leadership, the President wished him good health and wisdom, urging the current generation to build on the legacy of their forebears.

"Our ancestors built a kingdom of influence. Our generation must build an economy of opportunity," he said.

Ghana News.title: Gizella Tetteh-Agbotui condemns unfair hostel fee hikes, assures students of gov’t action
Ghana News.content:
The Deputy Minister for Works and Housing, Gizella Tetteh-Agbotui, has condemned reported arbitrary increases in hostel fees by some operators, warning that students must not be made to bear the cost of exploitative practices while living in substandard conditions.

She gave the assurance during a working visit to the headquarters of the Rent Control Department in Accra on Saturday, November 21, where she engaged the Ag. Rent Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, and management over complaints of rising hostel charges and poor accommodation conditions affecting tertiary students.

The Deputy Minister said the government was concerned about reports that some university-affiliated and privately operated hostels had increased their charges by as much as 110 per cent without the required statutory assessment.

Briefing her on the situation, Mr Opoku presented inspection findings which also highlighted poor ventilation, broken facilities and inadequate sanitation in some hostels, despite the significant increases in fees.

He further disclosed that the Department had issued summons to managers of facilities found to be non-compliant following petitions from students.

The Department has also sought guidance from the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources on the matter.

Ms Tetteh-Agbotui condemned the reported practices and reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to strengthening the Rent Control Department’s regulatory functions to protect tenants and ensure compliance with the law.

Speaking on behalf of the sector Minister, Ahmed Ibrahim, she assured students, parents, tenants and the general public that the concerns raised would receive attention through immediate, short-, medium- and long-term interventions.

She said the Ministry welcomes the concerns and remains committed to working with relevant institutions to address the challenges confronting hostel residents.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: ‘Disappointing’: Delegates react after COP31 climate talks end without deal
World.content:
Draft text considered too weak to deal with climate change after oil-producing countries oppose the term ‘fossil fuels’.

United Nations climate talks have failed to secure a deal on how to deal with climate change, prompting UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to express “a very profound frustration”.

Multiple countries and negotiating blocs said on Sunday that the final draft, presented by COP31 presidents Turkiye and Australia, was too weak to fight global warming.

If the text had been approved, it would have acknowledged for the first time that global warming is on course to exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) threshold that countries had sought to preserve from the 2015 Paris Agreement.

The talks had extended into overtime after key oil- and gas-producing countries opposed mentions of “fossil fuels” in the final text. The revised text also dropped a $120bn target for funds to help poorer countries adapt to climate change.

The last time the annual UN climate talks failed to end in an agreement was in Copenhagen in 2009.

Here’s how countries and key parties reacted to the deal’s failure:

UN chief Guterres

“I am deeply disappointed that COP31 has ended without consensus on ⁠an overarching outcome. I share the very profound frustration of ⁠all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” Guterres said.

The UN chief criticised powerful fossil fuel interests for obstructing climate action, accusing them of distorting scientific evidence, delaying policies and prioritising profits.

EU delegation

The European Union said it will not endorse a deal that “does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate ‌‌change, ‌‌and we will not accept negotiating backward in time, and we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel”.



A spokesman added that the draft deal “does not begin to address the climate emergency that we face”.

Denmark’s climate minister

Samira Nawa said the EU was willing to accept clauses on adaptation finance but argued that the text did not go far enough.

“This is about the mitigation. It’s about the ⁠⁠fossil fuels not being mentioned. It’s the language on science not being strong enough.”

United Kingdom lead climate negotiator

Kate Hughes said the draft text “moves us backwards on the science” and does not acknowledge the urgency or scale of the climate crisis.

“It should have been instead presenting bold, collective ambition on climate action.”

Least Developed Countries group

The Least Developed Countries group said: “We struggled to find meaningful outcomes that respond to the ⁠⁠priorities of the most vulnerable countries like us. … We cannot afford to see backsliding.”

The group is composed of 44 countries that are the most vulnerable to climate change and have contributed relatively little in carbon emissions.

They represent more than 1 billion people and include Pacific island nations, such as Tuvalu and Kiribati, as well as other countries most at risk to the effects of climate change, such as Bangladesh, Nepal and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Marshall Islands delegation

“We have been let down on all sides,” the Marshall Islands said. “We were presented with the worst possible response to overshoot, a response to enhance oil and gas. We will not be forced to accept false solutions. We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests. We will not accept an outcome that undermines our security and threatens our future.”

Vanuatu delegation

The delegation for the Pacific island nation said: “This text falls short of what international law requires, what science demands and what our vulnerable communities urgently need.”

It called it “unacceptable” that the text was “silent” on fossil fuels.

Kenya delegation

Kenya’s delegation complained that the deal did not specifically mention Africa and did not take into account “Africa’s special needs and circumstances”.

“Those who took the lead in emissions cuts take the lead in support.”

Iraq delegation

The Iraq delegation expressed its “deep concern with some pathways that were taken to divert ⁠⁠from [the] Paris Agreement”.

Russia delegation

Sergei Kononuchenko, a Russian delegate, argued that if oil and gas supplies shrink, it would lead to a “switch to dirtier types of fuel and energy poverty, … and the first to suffer would be the poorest”.



“For that reason, we cannot agree to any formulation on fossil fuel.”

Saudi Arabia delegation

The Saudi delegation said it believed “climate change requires all solutions on the table” and it made no sense for “concrete solutions” to be “taken off the table”.

COP31 president

Murat Kurum, Turkiye’s minister of environment, urbanisation and climate change, said: “We did everything we could. You should not hurt people in the world who really expect something out of this by just being hung up on one word or phrase. … There is no benefit for anyone in a system where you go into negotiations with no result.”

“There will be ‌‌no new text from now on. We will not be carrying out work on a new text in an environment where there is no consensus. We will implement existing decisions.”

COP31 president of negotiations

Chris Bowen, Australia’s minister of climate change and energy, called the collapse of the talks “very disappointing”.

“A lot of good things happened this COP, a ⁠⁠lot of events which told the clean energy story, a lot of commitments made – like the more than 90 countries that signed the electrification pledge, for example. And all that is good work and a great thing but not enough when it comes to climate action,” he said.

“An obvious issue is the transition away from fossil ⁠⁠fuels, where some parties insisted that must be mentioned. Other parties insisted that if it was mentioned, they would veto.”

World.title: Can we build a more ethical AI future?
World.content:
Marc Lamont Hill speaks with tech entrepreneur Anil Dash about AI’s risks and the fight for ethical technology.

The artificial intelligence boom is transforming the global economy and concentrating enormous power in the hands of a few technology companies. But a series of developments is raising new questions about the industry’s stability and accountability from the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy to a wave of technology outages affecting the US government, major banks, companies and aviation systems alongside reports of hacked refrigerators across Europe. Concerns are mounting over the economic risks, mass layoffs, privacy and environmental impact of AI. And as AI company Anthropic began trading publicly, reaching a $2 trillion valuation, questions are mounting over whether the extraordinary levels of AI investment are sustainable. Is there a future where AI can be used for the collective good?

This week on UpFront, Marc Lamont Hill speaks with Anil Dash, former adviser to the White House Office of Digital Strategy in former United States President Barack Obama’s administration, about the risks of the AI boom, Silicon Valley’s growing political influence and the urgent need for greater accountability.

World.title: Drone attacks kill four near Sudan’s capital, damage UN building
World.content:
The Rapid Support Forces are blamed as drones reportedly hit United Nations and government buildings, as well as Khartoum’s airport.

Drone attacks blamed on Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have killed four people in and around the capital, Khartoum, and damaged a United Nations building, according to local reports and UN officials.

The attacks early on Sunday struck residential areas as Sudanese air defences responded to drones reportedly targeting government buildings and Khartoum’s airport.

The strikes have raised fresh concerns about the growing danger to civilians and aid workers as Sudan‘s war increasingly relies on drones.

Explosions were heard across the capital between approximately 2am (00:00 GMT) and 4:30am (02:30 GMT), according to witnesses cited by the AFP news agency, as the army attempted to intercept the drones.

Al Jazeera’s AlMigdad Alruhaid reported from the city of Omdurman, across the Nile from Khartoum, that three people were killed and nine wounded when a drone struck a home in northern Omdurman.

A child was also killed in a separate attack south of the capital.

In the village of Jebel Aulia, about 45km (28 miles) south of Khartoum, a witness told AFP that a drone hit the home of a mosque official who calls worshippers to prayer. Residents searched the wreckage for trapped relatives.

The UN’s humanitarian coordinator in Sudan, Denise Brown, said on Sunday that one of its buildings had been damaged while staff were inside.

The UN’s humanitarian office, which coordinates emergency relief, condemned the danger to its personnel in a civilian neighbourhood, calling it “unacceptable”.



A Sudanese army source told AFP on Sunday that the drones had been launched from neighbouring Ethiopia’s Bahir Dar airport. The allegation could not be independently verified.

Ethiopia has previously denied Sudanese accusations that it allows the RSF to carry out attacks from its territory.

Sudan has also lodged complaints with the UN Security Council, the body responsible for international peace and security, and the African Union, a continental organisation, over alleged drone operations originating in Ethiopia.

Soldiers executed

Separately on Sunday, Sudan’s government accused RSF fighters of executing captured soldiers in southeastern Blue Nile state, near the Ethiopian border.

The government condemned the alleged killings as violations of international humanitarian law. The accusation has not been independently verified.

Both the RSF and the Sudanese army are relying more frequently on drones to hit enemy targets. More than 1,100 were killed by drones in the first half of this year, according to the United Nations.

The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has said that drone attacks account for about two-thirds of children killed or injured in Sudan from the period of January to September.

The war in Sudan between the army and the RSF began in April 2023. It has led to one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises, with 13 million people displaced and some regions facing famine.

World.title: The Drugs Don’t Work
World.content:
A look at how antibiotic overuse could fuel superbugs, killing eight million people annually by 2050.

The challenges posed by antimicrobial resistance show where its impact is most acutely and tragically manifested: infant mortality in the developing world, specifically in sub-Saharan Africa. This film shows what these bland statistics mean in real terms to the health workers and families affected, following them as they struggle to fight this battle with low-tech solutions.

The Drugs Don’t Work follows the battle to the United Kingdom and examines how and why penicillin, the world’s most successful antibiotic, was invented. It then examines why pharmaceutical companies like GlaxoSmithKline are struggling to produce novel solutions to the problem of antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

The film also explores the cutting edge of academic research at British universities and hospitals supported by the power of the UK-based tech company DeepMind, and features academics and advocates who are devoting their lives to solving the problem. Returning to Africa, it shows how local innovation and the tools offered by the developed world are now saving lives and contributing to the global battle against AMR – an effort that could ultimately save millions of lives.

World.title: Zelenskyy urges US to release Patriot missiles as Russia kills 5 in Ukraine
World.content:
Two Russian attacks kill at least four people near Kyiv as Russian shelling kills one in Zaporizhzhia.

Share Zelenskyy urges US to release Patriot missiles as Russia kills 5 in Ukraine on social media

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has urged the United States to approve the delivery of Patriot interceptor missiles after a week of Russian attacks across 20 regions of the country with the latest ones killing five near Kyiv and in Zaporizhzhia.

In a post on Telegram on Sunday, Zelenskyy said Russia launched about 2,700 attack drones, nearly 1,460 guided aerial bombs and 165 missiles over the past week. A significant share of the missiles were ballistic, he said, including some supplied by North Korea.

“Against this backdrop, it is particularly difficult to understand the delays in the delivery of antiballistic systems to Ukraine,” Zelenskyy said.

Ukraine is short of US-made Patriot interceptors, which can shoot down ballistic missiles.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s partners had already paid for the missiles through a NATO-coordinated programme that funds purchases of US weapons for Kyiv. However, their delivery is still awaiting Washington’s approval.

Rescuers search rubble near Kyiv

One of the latest Russian attacks hit a five-storey apartment building early on Sunday in the village of Dymer, north of Kyiv, causing part of it to collapse.

Rescuers later recovered three bodies as emergency crews searched for 10 people, including two children, who were missing, according to Russia’s Interfax news agency, citing Radio Liberty.

Later ⁠on Sunday, one person was ⁠killed when a Russian drone struck a grocery store in Vyshneve, southwest of Kyiv, the local governor said on Telegram, adding that three ⁠people were injured.



Mykhailo Semikin, the acting head of the Zaporizhia regional military administration, also said a man was killed in Russian shelling in the city of Zaporizhzhia.

Moscow says it hits cargo ship and power facilities

Also on Sunday, Russia’s Ministry of Defence said its forces struck a cargo ship northeast of Ukraine’s Black Sea port city of Odesa overnight.

The ministry said Russian drones struck the Pravoberezhna electricity facility in Zaporizhzhia, which it said supplied power to Ukrainian arms manufacturers. It reported further strikes on an oil refinery, electrical substations and a data centre operated by MKM Telecom.

In its battlefield update, the ministry claimed Russian forces had taken control of the Ukrainian village of Sosnovyi Bir in the northeastern Kharkiv region and destroyed a launcher for Ukraine’s Neptune coastal missile system.

It also said it struck energy and transport facilities it described as serving Ukraine’s military. The Russian claims could not be independently verified.

World.title: Why Bangladesh descended into violence ahead of Hasina’s planned return
World.content:
Supporters of the ousted PM, who lives in self-imposed exile in India, have protested against rejection of her return.

Bangladesh has deployed paramilitary troops to help contain a wave of violence that erupted after supporters of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina staged protests against the government’s rejection of the ousted leader’s planned return to the country.

At least four people have been killed and police stations, banks and even the ancestral home of the former interim leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner, Muhammad Yunus, have been attacked in a week of violence.

Violence erupted after supporters of Hasina’s now-banned Awami League party took to the streets as part of weeklong protests that overlapped with the anniversary of the former leader’s death sentence last year. Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for crimes against humanity related to the 2024 student-led protests.

Earlier this month, Hasina requested a new passport and identity card to allow her to return to Bangladesh. She has been living in self-imposed exile in India after fleeing the country in the wake of the July 2024 student-led uprising.

But the Bangladesh government, led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, says she is a convicted criminal, and she can only return under the extradition treaty with India.

Rahman has blamed India for the unrest. “It is not only that; they have not looked at the interests of Bangladesh and its people. At the same time, the country across the border, where they have fled to, is their master… To satisfy those masters, they have again started conspiring against Bangladesh and its people,” Rahman said in parliament on Friday.



So why does Hasina still want to return to the country, and are the recent protests spontaneous or orchestrated?

Here’s what we know:

What do we know about the deadly protests?

Since mid-November, arson attacks and violence have been reported across 28 districts of Bangladesh.

At least four people have been killed in the political violence since November 14, including three political activists and a bus worker who died when his vehicle was torched, according to local media reports.

Two men from the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) were killed in the Narail district, according to the AFP news agency. In retaliation, BNP supporters set ablaze more than a dozen homes belonging to Awami League supporters in the district.

A Narail resident, who asked not to be identified for fear of reprisals, said as many as 50 houses had been damaged in the district.

“We are terrified by the clashes,” he told AFP. “We have asked our women and children to stay inside unless it is absolutely necessary.”

Late Wednesday, police said the ancestral home of Yunus was set on fire in the port city of Chittagong. It was not immediately clear who was behind the blaze.

“Criminals set fire to the eastern side of the house. The area was being used as a storeroom,” Chittagong Metropolitan Police spokesman Aminur Rashid said, adding there were no casualties.

Yunus, who was targeted by Hasina during her term in power, has faced hostility from her supporters. Grameen Bank, set up by Yunus, said 22 of its branches were subject to arson attacks.

State news agency BSS reported that 90 additional platoons of the paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) had been deployed nationwide.

National police chief Md Ali Hossain Fakir told BSS that security had been restored in Gopalganj, Hasina’s hometown and a longstanding stronghold of her party.

“I urge the peace-loving people of this area to stand against those involved in sabotage and disorder,” he added.

Khandakar Tahmid Rejwan, lecturer of global studies and governance at the Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB) and contributing analyst at the United States defence think tank Jamestown Foundation, told Al Jazeera that the protests do not appear to be entirely spontaneous in nature.

“If they were genuinely organic and spontaneous, one would arguably expect to see broader public mobilisation and participation across different parts of the country. Instead, what we are witnessing is a concentration of protest activity in areas such as Gopalganj, Faridpur, and Madaripur, which have traditionally served as strongholds of the Awami League’s support base,” he said.



He noted that while sporadic protests and demonstrations have also been reported in other parts of the country, their scale and geographical spread, at least so far, suggest localised unrest rather than a nationwide mobilisation.

“Although these incidents are concerning from the perspective of public order and political stability, the available pattern of mobilisation does not, at this stage, indicate a level of nationwide momentum that could fundamentally challenge the incumbent government’s position,” he added.

What triggered the violence?

The recent protests began soon after the government rejected Hasina’s request for her passport and identity card on November 9. Hasina served as prime minister from 1996 to 2001, and again from 2009 to 2024, but her nearly 15 years of iron-fist rule have been slammed by human rights organisations.

She was sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over her deadly crackdown on the student-led protests in 2024. As many as 1,400 people may have been killed in the violence, according to United Nations estimates.

Hasina has, however, denied these charges and told the Reuters news agency on November 9 that she intended to return to Bangladesh and surrender before a court. Her aides added the date would be announced once various formalities were completed.

But her request has been denied by the current government.

“Bangladesh does not give passports to terrorists who kill thousands of people and flee. It will work under the current extradition arrangements with India to pursue and get the terrorist Hasina handed over,” State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said earlier this month.

The Bangladeshi prosecutor Md Aminul Islam, who secured the death sentence for Hasina at the Dhaka-based International Crimes Tribunal, said she will be executed if she returns home.

“Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict,” Islam told reporters.

Protesters have also been calling for the ban on Hasina’s party to be lifted and detained leaders and supporters of the party to be released from prison.

Why does Hasina want to return to Bangladesh?

Hasina still enjoys support among a section of the population, while many others want to see her hanged.

Her return could also worsen political tensions as Prime Minister Rahman’s government tries to restore ‌‌stability two years on from the 2024 uprising.

But her game plan behind why she wants to return is unclear.

Some analysts have questioned whether Hasina genuinely intends to return to face the law.

Others have questioned whether she is using the promise to revive her political fortunes from self-imposed exile in India. New Delhi, her close ally for decades, has sheltered her since she fled Dhaka in August 2024. But her continued presence has become a point of contention between the two countries.

Rejwan believes there are several interconnected factors behind Hasina’s renewed emphasis on returning to Bangladesh.

“First, there is the domestic political context. It has been nearly 10 months since the incumbent government assumed power, and during this period, it has faced a number of challenges, including inflationary pressures, economic stagnation and a fuel crisis. While these difficulties are not entirely homegrown and are, to a considerable extent, linked to broader geopolitical and global economic developments, it remains difficult to communicate these complexities to the general public. Their everyday consequences inevitably affect public morale and confidence in the government,” he said.



“Secondly, there is the ongoing political debate surrounding whether the Awami League should remain proscribed or be allowed to resume its political activities,” he added.

He noted that several international actors and civil society voices have advocated lifting the temporary ban and allowing the party to return to mainstream political activities, potentially following the prosecution and sentencing of those responsible for the atrocities committed during the July 2024 uprising.

“Thirdly, there is India’s role, which cannot be entirely overlooked. Sheikh Hasina and several Awami League leaders and activists who fled Bangladesh following the collapse of her government in August 2024 have reportedly continued to receive varying degrees of support from India. There have also been discussions and speculation about whether New Delhi has been exploring possibilities for negotiating her safe return to Bangladesh, potentially under arrangements that would ensure her security, including protection under the custody of the Bangladesh Army,” he added.

Mushfiqul Fazal Ansarey, a senior Bangladeshi diplomat, said that Hasina does not intend to return to face her sentence. “In my assessment, her talk of a comeback is intended to rally supporters and destabilise Bangladesh,” he told Al Jazeera.

The violence, Ansarey said, has extended abroad, with Awami League supporters reportedly attacking Nahid Islam’s entourage in Romford, east London. Islam, who was part of the student-led uprising, is a member of parliament.

“Arson, killings and intimidation cannot be presented as political protest. The neighbouring country should ensure that its territory is not used to organise or incite violence against Bangladesh.”

What are the political ramifications of the Awami League protests?

Besides deploying police forces to contain the protests, in an effort to build unity, Prime Minister Rahman has held talks with Shafiqur Rahman, the leader of the opposition party Jamaat-e-Islami.

The Jamaat’s Secretary-General Mia Golam Porwar told the Bangladeshi newspaper The Daily Star that the two leaders viewed the meeting positively and hoped it would strengthen democracy in the country.

“If this initiative is taken with the intention of moving forward with everyone on board, it will be good. We want to view it positively. If the initiative genuinely has good intentions, we want it to succeed,” he said on Sunday.

Rejwan, from the Independent University of Bangladesh, said that from the Awami League’s perspective, one of the most unfavourable political developments would be the possible convergence of political interests between the BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami, particularly if their existing political differences were set aside in the interest of preventing the Awami League from regaining political ground.

“Beyond the Awami League, Jamaat-e-Islami remains one of the few political organisations in Bangladesh with an established grassroots organisational structure, a relatively disciplined cadre base, and extensive networks of political mobilisation. This gives the party a significant organisational capacity to counter the Awami League’s own entrenched political networks and grassroots mobilisation,” he said.

He highlighted that another crucial variable is the extent of residual popular support for the Awami League.

“If Sheikh Hasina were to return to Bangladesh, how would the politically dormant but ideologically sympathetic sections of the population respond? Would her return reactivate sections of the Awami League’s grassroots support base, or would the party’s political isolation and organisational setbacks limit its ability to mobilise them?” he said.



“Ultimately, the sustainability and effectiveness of any BNP–Jamaat political understanding aimed at containing the Awami League’s political resurgence would depend not merely on elite-level negotiations but also on the ability of both parties to manage their competing political interests and respond to the evolving sentiments of the wider electorate,” he said.

World.title: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
World.content:
An explosion has occurred on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base port after a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said.

The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libyan state media reported, citing the eastern government.

It added that the site was secured, and there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment.

Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC, reviewed by BBC Verify, shows a boat on fire at 0547 GMT at the Benghazi port, with a separate image captured several hours later appearing to show the same vessel partially submerged.

Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship engulfed in flames and smoke, while it is still dark.

World.title: South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal
World.content:
"As the minister in charge, I believe I cannot escape criticism that we failed to prepare in advance," Choi was quoted as saying on Sunday by South Korea's Yonhap's news agency.

"Now that the exam has concluded, I feel a deep sense of responsibility and am offering my resignation," the minister added.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung - who has been calling for an overhaul of the current exam system - later accepted Choi's resignation.

The education ministry earlier said 111 candidates had been found with unauthorised smart devices during this year's Suneung, which was taken by about 500,000 students.

Concerns over academic dishonesty during the fiercely competitive exam had been brewing in recent weeks, after reports of candidates cheating with the help of AI devices.

These fears came to a boil last weekend, when Han Won-seok, the top tax accountancy exam scorer in April, admitted to cheating.

His confession came amid speculation over his unusually high score, with just one out of 160 questions wrong.

"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI, then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating," the 34-year-old said in a video message.

This prompted the authorities to introduce urgent measures, with just days ahead of the Suneung.

This included sending nationwide emergency alerts on the exam day.

Three alerts were sent between 08:00 and 15:00 local time on Thursday, causing phones across the country to blare out in unison - even if they were on silent mode, and even if they belonged to tourists using data roaming.

The phones did not ring out if they were switched off or on airplane mode.

It was the first time that South Korea used its national disaster alert system to catch exam cheaters.

Candidates also had to cover up the buttons on their shirts and jackets to block any hidden cameras, and authorities conducted inspections of eyewear.

All this made even honest test takers paranoid.

Ahead of the Suneung, one high school senior told the Korea Times he was worried his horn-rimmed spectacles would be mistaken for smart glasses.

Another told Yonhap he usually wore glasses but made an effort to put on contact lenses for the Suneung to avoid raising suspicions.

World.title: Russia-bound ship still on fire after attack in Gulf of Finland
World.content:
Rescue and firefighting efforts are continuing for a Russian cargo vessel hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, authorities have said.

The ship - the Sparta II - was bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment.

Finland's Border Guard said on Sunday that work was ongoing to make sure the cargo ship did not sink but it was not aware of any danger to surrounding maritime traffic.

Water was still being used to douse the ship on Sunday, and Finland said Estonian and Russian assets were also involved in recovery work.

Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones had been used in the strike, based on preliminary information, and there was "no threat" to the territory's supplies.

"War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."

The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments.

The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.

Finland's coast guard said it had been alerted to the attack at around 08:50 local time (06:50 GMT) on Saturday and that the cargo vessel had been located approximately 50km west of the island of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland.

This prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" around the area, Finnish border officials said.

Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".

A Russian rescue vessel approached the ship and was told by the crew that they did not need to be evacuated, Kaliningrad's governor wrote on Telegram, adding: "The crew is currently carrying out the necessary work and plans to continue on its way."

The Finnish Border Guard later said the crew had been evacuated to another Russian vessel that was now already en route to Russia. The Russian rescue vessel had remained at the location of the stricken ship.

It added that no environmental damage had been detected and that there was no danger to maritime traffic or people.

Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.

World.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
World.content:
A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities.

Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores and seven others were detained by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said.

Seven suspects were killed in the operation, as were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave, the secretariat added.

Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI. The US is seeking his extradition.

Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump since he returned to the White House.

Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, is thought to have been active in the drug trafficking trade since the 1990s but managed to evade authorities till now by maintaining a relatively low profile.

World.title: Three killed and dozens missing after fire at Indonesian factory
World.content:
At least three people have been killed after a fire at a confectionery factory in western Java on Saturday, with the death toll expected to rise.

Firefighters were still tackling some flames on Sunday, while rescuers searched for around 36 missing in parts of the damaged building where workers were believed to be trapped.

Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency said on Sunday 15 survivors had been located, and four others taken to hospital and a local clinic with undisclosed injuries.

Rescuers recovered 24 body bags from the fire as of Sunday evening, as search operations continue to locate missing people.

Banten Governor, Andra Soni, told media about 60 people were believed to be inside the factory when it caught fire on Saturday evening.

The factory is in Serang district, Banten province, about 50km (31km) west of Jakarta. Authorities have not yet determined the fire's cause.

Photos and footage of the scene showed the large factory taken over by flames during the night, firefighters battling the flames, and first responders retrieving at least one body from the wreckage on Sunday morning.

Local media reported that the search had been called off for the night late on Sunday, and would resume on Monday.

World.title: Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89
World.content:
Italian jeweller Paolo Bulgari, who helped turn his family's business into a global luxury brand, has died in Rome aged age 89.

His family announced the news, remembering him as "the greatest jeweller of our time", according to Italian media.

Paolo Bulgari was Chairman of the Bvlgari Group since 1984 and its jewellery pieces have adorned Hollywood stars and royalty including Diana, Princess of Wales.

The company Bvlgari posted an online tribute to the "true creative soul", whose work would "continue to inspire generations to come".

The firm, Bulgari, was set up by his grandfather, Greek silversmith Sotirios Voulgaris, in Rome in the late 19th century - who later adapted his name to Bulgari in Italian.

Originally from Paramythia, a mountain village in the Epirus region of northwestern Greece renowned for its silver jewellery, Voulgaris fled Ottoman rule and settled in Naples before opening a shop in Rome.

Paolo Bulgari joined the company shortly after leaving school, becoming an expert in gemstones - eventually leading the business and overseeing international growth.

World.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
World.content:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media reports, citing two people briefed on the issue.

The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks.

It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US. The agency did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

When asked about the breach in a Fox News interview on Saturday, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the hack. "I will say that it's not good. I don't like that," he said.

"But maybe we'll learn things that we would've never learned otherwise," Trump added.

This apparent breach of FBI database comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors in the US last week. Officials have said they were not caused by cyber-attacks, but the blackouts have sparked scrutiny from lawmakers.

White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired this week, with Trump saying he was not good enough.

Dan Lorhmann, a former analyst for the National Security Agency (NSA), told the BBC News Channel that the NCIC's data included "critical information relating to nationwide criminal activity" and needed to be protected.

He added that while US security agencies including the FBI have "an amazing ability" to keep such information safe" and are "globally respected", the level of cyber-attacks is rising globally.

"There's a lot of different reasons why that's happening but I do have faith in our experts in government," Lorhmann said.

In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber-crime group ShinyHunters, which claimed it had stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff - around 38,000 people.

After that hack, one former FBI agent told the BBC he feared for the safety of current employees, whose personal information could soon become available online to criminals and hostile nation-state hackers.

In a separate development, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture (USDA).

Employees were informed on Thursday that its farm payment system had been targeted, NBC said.

The USDA has not publicly commented on the issue.

World.title: Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has justified Kyiv's repeated attacks on a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, calling it a "fair response" to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate".

He rejected the claim by the Russian president that the bridge - which links Russia to the peninsula it illegally annexed from Ukraine - was "exclusively civilian" in use.

"There are facts, not just the words of Putin. We can see," he said.

The Ukrainian president pointed to images online of tanks and other Russian military hardware using the route from Russia into occupied Crimea as a supply line and for logistics.

"If Putin used the internet, he could see that."

The Ukrainian president added that Russia had carried out attacks with missiles and drones on bridges in Ukraine.

This week's combined missile-and-drone strikes by Ukrainian forces destroyed the central road section of the Crimean Bridge, collapsing part of it together with one of the two support arches into the sea and rendering the structure unusable for road traffic.

Russian attacks on Ukraine continued on Friday evening and overnight: a seven-year-old boy was killed in missile and drone strikes on Zelensky's hometown of Kryvyi Rih in the central Dnipropetrovsk region. Local officials say he had been in a playground at the time.

A 20-year-old female medic was also killed. A local official added that when rescuers rushed to the scene, the same site was targeted again with jet powered drones. Another 58 people were injured in the city.

Ukraine's state emergency service DSNS said 11 people were also injured in the north-eastern Kharkiv region, and one person in Rivne, in the north-west.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

World.title: Lawal distributes motorcycles, tricycles, other empowerment tools to individuals, groups in Zamfara
World.content:
Governor Dauda Lawal said that distributing empowerment assets to beneficiaries shows his administration’s commitment to helping individuals and associations across Zamfara grow their businesses, create jobs, and become self-reliant.

On Saturday, the governor launched the distribution of motorcycles, Keke NAPEP tricycles, Hijet pickups, and three-wheel barrow pickups to Zamfara residents at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, the state capital.

The distribution is the second phase of the state government’s empowerment programme targeting various groups, organisations and associations through the Zamfara State Agency for Poverty Alleviation (ZAPA).

The second phase includes 1,000 motorcycles, 100 tricycles popularly known as Keke NAPEP, 40 Hijet pickup vehicles, 40 three-wheeled pickup vehicles and 40 vehicles.

In his remarks, Governor Lawal reiterated that the initiative offers another opportunity for prospective beneficiaries to expand their economic opportunities and improve their standard of living.

He said, “This gathering is particularly important as it gives me a unique opportunity to formally distribute these vehicles in recognition of the immense contributions of individuals and various organisations to the overall development of our State.

“I wish to commend the Zamfara State Agency for Poverty Alleviation (ZAPA) for its commitment to implementing this laudable initiative.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I also urge all beneficiary associations to regard these assets as valuable economic investments, utilise them strictly for their intended purposes and ensure timely repayment in accordance with the agreed loan arrangements. This will ensure the programme’s sustainability and enable other deserving citizens to benefit.

“Let me remind this gathering that humanitarian services save lives, relieve suffering and protect human dignity during conflicts, natural disasters and health emergencies. They bridge immediate survival needs with long-term community recovery when local systems are overwhelmed.

“My administration will continue to provide empowerment opportunities and livelihood support to individuals, groups and communities to expand opportunities and enhance the well-being of citizens of the State.”

World.title: Tinubu commits ₦450bn to agricultural financing, targets 500,000 farmers – APC campaign Council
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu’s administration has committed ₦450 billion to agricultural financing programmes to strengthen food security, increase domestic food production, and improve the productivity of smallholder farmers across Nigeria.

The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council disclosed this in a statement issued on Sunday by its spokesperson, Dele Alake.

According to the statement, the intervention, implemented through the Bank of Agriculture (BOA), has reached more than 500,000 smallholder farmers across 16 states, including over 70,000 women.

It added that President Tinubu had also approved a ₦1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture to expand access to agricultural financing and support the cultivation of 500,000 hectares of farmland under the Renewed Hope Agenda.

The council said the government’s interventions went beyond providing loans to farmers to include access to quality seeds, fertilisers, mechanisation, irrigation, storage facilities and commodity markets.

It said the Renewed Hope Smallholder Support and Value Chain Fund, valued at ₦250 billion, provides financing through Farmer Aggregation Companies responsible for farmer registration, input distribution, extension services and market linkages.

Under the programme, approximately 2.5 million bags of fertiliser and 300,000 bags of certified seeds have been distributed, while the initiative targets two million farmers and more than 10 million bags of fertiliser.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The statement identified Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, Adamawa, Yobe and Bauchi among the states benefiting from the intervention.

It also said the Bank of Agriculture is implementing a ₦200 billion Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme to protect farmers against market uncertainties and distress sales.

Under the programme, the bank has procured approximately 170,000 metric tonnes of maize, rice, sorghum and cassava to strengthen commodity markets.

On interventions targeting specific agricultural value chains, the council highlighted the Onion Financing Programme, developed in partnership with the National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria (NOPPMAN), which represents more than 11,800 onion farmers.

The scheme is designed to provide farmers with improved seeds and fertilisers, support processors with commodity purchase funds and facilitate the development of storage and solar-powered cooling facilities to reduce post-harvest losses.

Under the financing arrangement, cooperatives will contribute 30 per cent of their input costs, while the Bank of Agriculture will provide the remaining 70 per cent.

On the proposed ₦1.5 trillion recapitalisation, the council said the initiative would strengthen the bank’s capacity to provide affordable financing to farmers, agricultural cooperatives, processors, aggregators and other businesses across the agricultural value chain.

It added that the recapitalisation would enable the bank to support large-scale agricultural investments, expand its reach to underserved farming communities and mobilise additional resources for domestic food production.

The statement also listed other interventions targeting farmers, women and young people, including dry-season farming financing, mechanisation, ginger recovery, women’s cooperative financing and commercial poultry production.
