World.title: America’s outages expose a crisis of trust
World.content:
At a camping and survival store in Los Angeles, customers bought emergency kits and water while talking about Microsoft and grounded flights. It is a long way from being unable to open an email to wondering whether there will be water in the tap tomorrow. This month, some Americans covered that distance in a matter of days.

It felt like the opening of the film “Leave the World Behind.” The lights are still on and the kitchen is stocked but, without a reliable link to the outside world, the people in the house have no idea how far the trouble has spread. As false warnings of a nationwide blackout circulated on social media, some Americans started asking the kind of questions a survival video game puts to its players. How much food do you have? How long will your batteries last? Should you fill the bathtub while the water still runs?

The first major disruption came on Nov. 12, when a Microsoft outage affected Outlook and other services. The next day, a technical failure prompted the Federal Aviation Administration to halt departures nationwide. On Nov. 16, some bank customers struggled to access their accounts and a separate failure delayed United Airlines flights. The day after, a software patch disrupted the National Security Agency’s classified internal communications network. The agency staggered employee arrivals and restricted campus access to essential personnel that evening. The NSA said its critical operations continued.

A scheduled federal emergency alert test went ahead that week. The blackout predicted online never came. At a congressional hearing on Nov. 18, officials including FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia said they had found no evidence that the outages were connected or caused by a coordinated cyberattack. Lawmakers separately asked about reports of possible Iranian-linked plots in the US.

Then news broke that White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross had been fired. For Americans already skeptical of Washington, the timing made it easy to wonder whether officials knew more than they were saying. On Saturday, reports indicated that the FBI was investigating an apparent breach of the National Crime Information Center, a database law enforcement agencies use to share records on fugitives, missing people and stolen property. The scope of the suspected breach was unclear and there was no immediate indication it was linked to the earlier outages.

Before governments put AI to work in public services, they should test what happens when it fails. Dalia Al-Aqidi

By then, the earlier disruptions had already raised a question. How did a few days of outages make a much wider breakdown seem plausible?

Consider what happens when a flight is canceled. The airline sends passengers to its app. The app tells them to wait for an update. Meanwhile, they have to decide whether to stay at the gate, pay for a room or go home. A bank customer staring at a blank screen has to decide whether to resend the rent payment. A system can be down for a few hours and leave people dealing with the consequences long after it comes back.

That uncertainty landed in a country where trust in the federal government had been low for years, under presidents of both parties. In 2024, the Pew Research Center found that 59 percent of Americans trusted Washington to do what is right only some of the time. Another 17 percent said they never did. Over decades of polling, Americans have generally expressed more trust when their own party holds the White House. Elections can change who gets the benefit of the doubt. That leaves every administration facing millions of people who are already skeptical when something goes wrong.

That skepticism matters when rumors move faster than official information. A warning to stock up on food gives people something to do immediately. A statement saying an investigation is underway may be accurate but someone whose flight has been grounded still has to decide whether to leave the airport. Officials can take the time they need to establish a cause and still tell people what is affected, where to get help and when to expect more information.

Technology companies face similar doubts as they ask Americans to rely on artificial intelligence for more of daily life. Even before the outages, Pew found that 67 percent of Americans had little or no confidence in the federal government’s ability to regulate AI effectively. About six in 10 lacked confidence that US companies would develop and use it responsibly.

Before governments put AI to work in public services, they should test what happens when it fails. If an AI booking system goes offline, can a patient still make an appointment? If the software wrongly rejects an application, can the person reach someone with the authority to review and reverse the decision? A company can show how quickly its software works on a good day. The government should test what happens on a bad one, while there is still time to fix it.

Some Americans wondered whether to fill their bathtubs because they were unsure what they could count on if the trouble got worse. That is the question Washington should take seriously. Would officials tell people what they knew, even if the facts were embarrassing? Would they admit what they still could not explain? Those are the things people remember the next time their government asks them to take it at its word.

Dalia Al-Aqidi is Senior Fellow at the Center for Security Policy.

X: @DaliaAlAqidi

World.title: Iran unveils missile launcher as commanders tout capabilities in war with US
World.content:
TEHRAN: Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher as senior military commanders touted the Islamic Republic’s capabilities in defiant messages to the United States.

“A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time,” Iranian state television reported on Saturday.

State television broadcast footage of Revolutionary Guards chief Ahmad Vahidi and the head of the Guards’ aerospace forces, Majid Mousavi, touring an underground missile base.

The two commanders were shown riding atop a vehicle through long tunnels lined with missiles, launchers and other military equipment.

“The damage suffered by our enemy is only the beginning. We shall witness their humiliation,” said Vahidi, whose Revolutionary Guards form the ideological arm of Iran’s military.

“Our capabilities have grown during the last two conflicts, and our high-performance weaponry can intimidate the enemy,” said Mousavi.

The unveiling comes months into the Middle East war, which broke out on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the conflict.

During the war’s most intense phase, US-Israeli strikes targeted Iran’s missile capabilities and again hit its nuclear sites, though the extent of the damage remains unclear.

Earlier this month, Iran unveiled a new underground missile base housing ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as launchers.

World.title: Makeshift cesspits threaten health and safety in Gaza’s displacement camps
World.content:
LONDON: Displaced Palestinians in Gaza are digging makeshift cesspits beside their tents and damaged homes as the destruction of sewage networks by Israel’s onslaught leaves families exposed to untreated wastewater and the risk of falling into poorly covered pits, the Palestinian news agency WAFA reported on Sunday.

The collapse of sanitation services during Israel’s military campaign, which started in October 2023 following a Hamas-led attack, has left stagnant sewage pooling around crowded displacement sites, raising concerns about illness and contamination of groundwater.

Residents told WAFA that the pits fill quickly, are costly to empty and could overflow during winter storms.

“We were forced to dig a cesspit beside our tent because there is no functioning sewage network,” Mahmoud Abdel Nabi told WAFA. “But it fills up quickly, forcing us to dig another one.

“The problem keeps recurring, and we are effectively living above a swamp of sewage, kitchen wastewater and water from washing and bathing.”

Abdel Nabi said his family could not afford to hire a sewage tanker to empty the pits and instead dug new ones whenever the old ones filled. He said family members had developed skin and respiratory problems, which he attributed to the damp, contaminated conditions.

Across displacement sites, wastewater is accumulating faster than the soil can absorb it, leaving pools that produce foul odors and attract insects and rodents.

All five of Gaza’s main wastewater treatment plants have stopped operating, while only 18 of its 74 sewage pumping stations are partially functioning, according to figures from the Palestinian Water Authority.

The authority said more than 80 percent of water infrastructure and about 700 km of sewage networks had been destroyed. The share of the population served by sewage networks has fallen from more than 85 percent to about 45 percent.

About 55,000 cubic meters of untreated wastewater are discharged daily across Gaza, according to the authority. Of that, about 40,000 cubic meters flow into the sea, while the rest enters the surrounding environment through makeshift pits and damaged networks.

The authority warned that more than 320,000 soakaway pits threaten groundwater, while untreated sewage discharged into the sea endangers public health and fish stocks.

For families living beside the pits, the danger is also immediate.

Maher Barhoum told WAFA that children often play near uncovered or poorly secured cesspits because they have few safe places to go. He said children and young people had fallen into the pits, resulting in deaths and injuries.

“The failure to properly cover these pits makes the danger even greater,” he said.

Families often cover the openings with worn metal sheets, wood or plastic, materials that offer little protection and can deteriorate in wet weather, Barhoum said.

Rain also threatens to spread sewage into shelters and nearby water sources.

Thaer Baraka told WAFA that wastewater was leaking into the ground near wells and pumping facilities. Residents pumping groundwater had noticed changes in its color, increased saltiness and visible impurities, he said, raising fears about its safety.

During a recent storm, rainwater mixed with sewage in Gaza City’s Unknown Soldier area and parts of Al-Mawasi in Khan Younis, as well as locations in central and northern Gaza, Baraka said.

He warned that further flooding could send contaminated water into tents, worsening conditions for families already struggling with inadequate shelter.

Emptying the pits has become increasingly expensive because of shortages of sewage tankers, machinery, spare parts and maintenance supplies, WAFA reported, as Israeli authorities continue to restrict the entry of many of those materials.

World.title: Direct flights from Athens to Damascus set to launch next month
World.content:
LONDON: Direct flights between Athens and Damascus will begin next month, as the Syrian Arab Republic seeks to restore international air links and strengthen economic ties with European markets.

Aegean Airlines will begin operating four weekly flights between Greece and Syria, with the first flight scheduled for Dec. 2, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency.

Omar Hosari, head of the General Authority of Civil Aviation, said that aviation authorities are working to reconnect the country’s airports with European capitals and attract more international carriers to operate direct flights to Syria. He added that Aegean Airlines’ route is expected to facilitate passenger travel, support tourism and trade, and contribute to the country’s economic recovery.

On Wednesday, the national flag carrier, Syrian Airlines, launched its first direct flight from Aleppo International Airport to Moscow.

Major international airlines canceled all flights to Syria in the early stages of the Syrian civil war, which lasted from 2011 to 2024, effectively isolating the country from the rest of the world. During the conflict, Syrians who wanted to travel abroad had to travel overland to airports in Lebanon or Jordan.

World.title: US seeks answers on Nvidia’s sale of chips to China, Bessent says
World.content:
WASHINGTON: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that the Trump administration still needs information on Nvidia’s chip sales and ‌will find ‌out who led ‌compliance at the company formerly led by Jensen Huang, who resigned following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

“We’ve ‌been ‌in touch ‌with the temporary ‌management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we ‌do need answers... it behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was,” Bessent told CBS’ “Face the Nation” program.

World.title: UKMTO reports incident involving tanker and military forces in Gulf of Oman
World.content:
The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said it had received ‌a ‌report of ‌an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the ‌Gulf of ‌Oman.

It gave ‌no ‌further details about the ‌incident, adding that authorities were aware and investigations were ongoing.

World.title: Yemeni military reports 639 operations against Houthi positions
World.content:
ADEN: Yemeni Armed Forces said on Sunday they had carried out 639 strikes against Iran-backed Houthi targets across several fronts, killing, wounding or capturing 86 Houthi commanders and fighters.

The operations, backed by the Popular Resistance and aircraft from the Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen, targeted positions, fortifications, weapon emplacements and reinforcements as part of Operation Dawn of Yemen, a military spokesperson said.

The military reported on 560 artillery strikes, 28 rocket-launcher strikes, 27 drone strikes and 24 airstrikes. It said the strikes had destroyed or damaged 64 Houthi vehicles and pieces of equipment.

In Marib and Jouf, troops continued offensive operations and counterattacks while clearing mines and improvised explosive devices from areas the military said it had recaptured.

Farther south, in Taiz, the military said its forces and the Popular Resistance were fighting to break the Houthi siege of the city. They repelled attacks, thwarted infiltration attempts and recaptured several key areas, a statement said.

In neighboring Lahj, troops repelled an attack and an infiltration attempt, inflicting losses on Houthi personnel and equipment.

The military said the campaign would continue until it achieved its objectives, including ending the militia’s threat to Yemen, the region and shipping in the Red Sea and Bab Al-Mandab Strait.

It also pledged to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure in accordance with international humanitarian law.

World.title: Uyun Al-Jiwa festival in Qassim celebrates local heritage
World.content:
UYUN AL-JIWA: A nine-day heritage festival celebrating local traditions, culture and craftsmanship has opened in Uyun Al-Jiwa governorate in the Qassim region.

Organized by Qassim municipality and Uyun Al-Jiwa municipality in cooperation with the governorate’s Local Development Association, the festival seeks to preserve folk traditions, promote community participation and support families engaged in cottage industries and owners of local initiatives.

Falah bin Jabr Al-Jabreen, head of Uyun Al-Jiwa municipality, said heritage events highlighted national identity and celebrated local customs, traditions and authentic values. They also gave younger generations an opportunity to learn about the past.

The festival features the Saudi ardah, a traditional wedding re-enactment, entertainment performances, a children’s stage and family-made products.

The festival aims to preserve folk heritage, encourage community participation and support families involved in cottage industries and owners of local initiatives. (SPA)

Uyun Al-Jiwa combines literary heritage, historical landmarks, traditional architecture and agricultural attractions, offering visitors a range of experiences rooted in local culture. The governorate is associated with the pre-Islamic poet Antarah bin Shaddad, whose celebrated “Mu’allaqa” mentions the area. Local folklore links Antarah and his beloved Abla to Antarah Rock and Al-Naslaa Rock, the latter known for its distinctive cone shape and ancient carvings of ibexes and camels.

The heritage town preserves traditional Najdi architecture, including Uyun Al-Jiwa Mosque, built from mud and stone, and Al-Mashaqiq, a network of ancient rock-cut wells and water channels, some extending more than 100 meters. Historic markets include Souq Al-Majlis and the longstanding Monday market, which attracts visitors from across the region.

The governorate is also known for its date production, particularly sukkari, barhi and wannana varieties, as well as its fruits and vegetables. Other attractions include Mount Al-Marqab, historically used as an observation point, King Salman Park, the public park and Al-Watan Garden.

World.title: Four killed in power plant explosion in southern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – At least four people were killed and 35 others injured on Saturday following a massive gas pipeline explosion and fire at the al-Hartha thermal power station in southern Iraq.

The explosion took place around 6:00 a.m. local time at the Hartha power station, located north of the Basra province.

The Iraqi Ministry of Electricity mentioned that an explosion in a gas pipeline servicing the power plant was the cause of the fire.

According to reports, investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of the pipeline explosion.

Flames spread rapidly from the power plant to nearby trailers and informal homes.

Locals with burns and smoke inhalation make up the majority of the 35 injured, with officials warning that that the death toll may increase.

While Electricity Minister Ali Saadi Waheeb called for an emergency meeting to address facility repairs and power supply interruptions, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi instructed the Health Ministry and the authorities in Basra to mobilize all available medical resources for the victims.

The power plant, which has a capacity of 800 megawatts and was producing about 400 megawatts before the incident, had to shut down entirely.

World.title: Iraq pushes to raise oil output to 10 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Sunday accelerated oilfield operations and extended working hours to advance Iraq’s push to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2032.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting with Meg O’Neill, CEO of British Petroleum (BP), where he emphasized the importance of expanding the recovery of associated gas and ending gas flaring, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The development would bolster Iraq’s energy supplies and meet domestic consumption needs, according to al-Zaidi.

The meeting addressed the development of oil fields and the extension of exploration areas, particularly the Kirkuk field, the Eridu field in Dhi Qar, and the Rumaila field in Basra.

The discussion is part of the Iraqi government’s goal to increase production rates and produce 10 million barrels per day by 2032.

O’Neill affirmed BP’s readiness to expand its operations in Iraq, leveraging its advanced technical and technological expertise to increase production and develop oil fields in line with established plans.

Iraq produces 4.88 million barrels of crude oil per day, according to OPEC data for October 2026, which is based on official Iraqi figures.

BP is involved in projects to develop Iraq’s oil sector; in March 2025, the company signed a deal with the North Oil Company (NOC) and the North Gas Company (NGC) to develop and rehabilitate the Kirkuk fields.

Additionally, BP provides technical support for the development of the Rumaila field in Basra.

BP’s deal in Kirkuk is not limited to developing oil production; it also encompasses the development of gas resources and the establishment of projects to expand infrastructure and processing facilities.

Iraq continues to flare approximately 24 billion cubic meters of gas annually—according to World Bank estimates for 2025—despite its need for gas to provide fuel for power plants and reduce reliance on imports.

World.title: KDP and PUK resume dialogue in Erbil amid disputes over parliament and Sulaymaniyah status
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Efforts to reset relations between the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) have brought fundamental questions over the political trajectory of the Kurdistan Region back to the forefront following a high-level meeting between the two rival parties in Erbil on Saturday, November 21, 2026.

While the talks reopened cautious optimism about breaking the region’s prolonged political deadlock, subsequent statements from Sulaymaniyah revealed persistent disputes over the legitimacy of the Kurdistan Parliament’s recent session, power-sharing mechanisms, and mounting calls for the administrative separation of Sulaymaniyah from Erbil.

The core institutional dispute centers on the legality of the Kurdistan Parliament’s latest session, which the KDP defends as constitutionally sound while the PUK refuses to recognize.

Speaking at a press conference in Sulaymaniyah, KDP 21st Branch official Sattar Awlani asserted that reactivating parliament is a national duty backed by clear attendance figures and legal foundations. Echoing KDP President Masoud Barzani’s call for inclusive dialogue, Awlani stressed that the party’s doors remain open to the PUK and all political forces to form a broad-based regional administration.

On the PUK side, Politburo member Imad Ahmad struck an optimistic yet guarded tone, telling reporters that the Erbil meeting “went well, God willing,” while declining to disclose substantive details of the negotiations.

KDP Central Committee member Sanaw Fereydoun similarly welcomed the resumption of dialogue as a hopeful step, emphasizing that any durable settlement must respect voter mandates and election results, while suggesting that rigid pre-negotiation stances could soften as talks progress.

Complicating the parliamentary impasse are renewed calls advocating the administrative separation of Sulaymaniyah Governorate from Erbil. Awlani flatly rejected such proposals, warning that separating Sulaymaniyah lacks any constitutional or legal basis and is destined to fail, urging all sides to resolve grievances through institutional partnership rather than unilateral moves.

Despite their internal divisions, leaders from both the KDP and PUK closed ranks regarding federal moves by Baghdad to tighten control over oil revenues and combat smuggling—an issue heightened by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi’s recent enforcement campaign in northern Babylon.

Both parties emphasized the Kurdistan Region’s distinct constitutional status. Awlani noted that the region is a legally protected constitutional entity whose authorities must be respected in any federal measures, while Imad Ahmad affirmed that disputes between Baghdad and Erbil must be settled strictly within the framework of the Iraqi Constitution, balancing mutual obligations and rights.

Taking a sharper stance, Sanaw Fereydoun dismissed reports suggesting federal anti-smuggling campaigns could extend into the Kurdistan Region’s border crossings as baseless rumors propagated by hostile actors.

Linking Kurdistan’s internal deadlock to Iraq’s wider political turbulence, political analyst Arslan Mohammed told Shafaq News that the country is navigating a quasi-transitional phase marked by friction between Baghdad and armed factions, oil disputes, economic strain, and rifts within both the Shia and Sunni political houses.

Mohammed warned that persistent KDP-PUK discord compounds public anxiety over political and economic stability, criticizing both parties for keeping citizens in the dark through vague official statements. He urged Kurdish political forces to publicly clarify their intentions, explain sudden unilateral decisions, and clearly delineate between governing partners and opposition actors in order to rebuild public trust in regional institutions.

World.title: Iraqi bodybuilder dies three days after winning Asian championship
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Three days after taking home a gold medal at the Asian Championships in Pattaya, Thailand, Iraqi international bodybuilding champion Sajad Jawad passed away at the age of 30.

Fans, other athletes, and authorities have expressed their sorrow at his unexpected death, which has shocked Iraq’s sports community.

After having previously finished in 11th place in the same event, Jawad reached an important milestone at the Asian Bodybuilding Championships in Thailand by winning first place and securing the continental championship in the 90-kilogram category.

On Thursday, the Iraqi National Federation of Bodybuilding and Fitness announced Jawad’s death through the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Federation President Faiz Abdul-Hassan and board members offered Jawad’s family condolences for his death.

Officials have not revealed the cause of his death. No medical report has been issued to confirm any reasons, despite reports of an unexpected health setback or physical weariness during competition preparation.

Jawad has over 260,000 Instagram followers and represented Iraq in several national and continental contests. His final social media post praising his gold-medal victory received hundreds of condolences after the announcement.

World.title: Al Zaidi to visit Cairo for talks on energy and defense
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi is scheduled to travel to the Egyptian capital, Cairo, on Monday, November 23, 2026, at the head of a high-level government delegation for official talks focused on political coordination, security, economic investment, oil and energy integration, and defense procurement, according to a government source.

During the visit, Al-Zaidi will meet with senior Egyptian officials—including President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi—to advance bilateral ties and expand Egyptian corporate participation in Iraqi infrastructure and reconstruction projects.

The summit builds directly on preparatory talks held in Baghdad on October 18, 2026, when Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty conveyed an official invitation from President el-Sisi and discussed activating the tripartite cooperation mechanism linking Iraq, Egypt, and Jordan, with particular emphasis on regional electrical grid interconnection and oil transport projects.

The Cairo trip marks the latest leg in an intensive regional diplomatic push launched by Al-Zaidi over the past five weeks to strengthen Iraq’s Arab neighborhood ties and energy transit corridors.

His recent regional itinerary began on October 14 with a visit to Saudi Arabia for talks with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, followed by a stop in Jordan on October 26 to meet King Abdullah II.

Two days later, on October 28, Al-Zaidi traveled to Damascus to meet Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, where discussions centered on border security, trade, and the potential rehabilitation of the Iraqi crude oil pipeline running across Syrian territory to the Mediterranean port of Baniyas.

On November 4, he made a landmark visit to Bahrain—the first by an Iraqi prime minister to Manama since 2003—to bolster bilateral economic relations and regional coordination.

Al-Zaidi’s resumption of foreign travel comes immediately after the de-escalation of last week’s security crisis in Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr) in northern Babylon Governorate. On November 17, the Prime Minister had postponed a scheduled official visit to Beirut in order to remain in Baghdad in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces and oversee federal deployments during the standoff with Kata’ib Hezbollah.

World.title: Behind the Jurf al-Sakhar truce: Kata’ib Hezbollah remains in place as Qaani brokers year-long timeline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two days after federal security forces entered Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr) in what Baghdad hailed as its first assertion of state authority over the closed northern Babylon subdistrict in 12 years, local sources and insiders close to Iraqi armed factions have disclosed details contradicting the official narrative, according to a report by Al-Mada newspaper.

While Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi addressed troops from the newly established joint control headquarters on Friday, November 20, declaring that “there are no weapons outside state authority,” sources on the ground indicate that the federal deployment has not displaced Kata’ib Hezbollah.

Instead, incoming Federal Police units were positioned near the town of Musayyib—where most displaced Jurf al-Sakhar residents have lived since 2014—well outside Kata’ib Hezbollah’s core security perimeter, while additional Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF/Hashd al-Shaabi) formations entering the area are described by locals as sympathetic to the faction.

A senior Shia political leader close to the factions told Al-Mada that the recent movements amount to reinforcing Kata’ib Hezbollah’s existing PMF brigades (the 45th, 46th, and 47th Brigades), rotating Federal Police detachments, and deploying Energy Police along pipeline corridors rather than dismantling the group’s military infrastructure.

Even if Kata’ib Hezbollah formally commits to vacating the district, the source estimated that dismantling bases and relocating heavy weaponry would require at least a full year—a timeline extending well beyond Baghdad’s June 30, 2027 deadline for bringing all weapons under state control.

Coordination Framework insiders linked this extended reprieve—and Kata’ib Hezbollah’s abrupt de-escalation after threatening to carry the confrontation into Baghdad’s Green Zone—directly to an eleventh-hour intervention by Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani.

Prior to Friday’s deadline, Qaani met in Baghdad with Kata’ib Hezbollah Secretary-General Abu Hussein Al-Hamidawi, Badr Organization leader Hadi Al-Amiri, and PMF Chairman Falih Al-Fayyadh, prompting Al-Hamidawi to instruct fighters to stand down from high alert and resolve disputes with the government through private channels.

Despite brokering the ceasefire, Iranian officials reportedly expressed sharp dissatisfaction with Kata’ib Hezbollah’s brinkmanship, urging the faction to follow the path of other armed groups that have pivoted toward political integration and state posts.

According to coalition sources, Tehran has spent recent months cultivating more disciplined, tightly controlled armed formations with stronger direct ties to Iran rather than domestic Iraqi politics—a shift coinciding with the sudden emergence of a previously unknown group calling itself “Asa’ib al-Jihad.”

Appearing in a video statement under the banner of the “Islamic Resistance Front in Iraq,” Asa’ib al-Jihad displayed an explosive-laden drone and threatened Shia political parties and factions it accused of abandoning armed resistance in exchange for government positions and financial gain.

Political observers suspect the group represents a hardline splinter faction broken away from Asa’ib Ahl al-Haq following the latter’s decision to comply with weapons-handover initiatives.

As Baghdad sought to project calm in northern Babylon, Al-Zaidi’s government was hit by a major energy security incident in southern Iraq on Saturday, November 21, when an explosion along the gas pipeline feeding the Al-Hartha thermal power station in Basra sparked a deadly blaze that killed and injured dozens and damaged nearby homes. While the government launched an urgent technical probe, political and security circles raised suspicions of a potential drone strike echoing prior attacks on energy infrastructure.

Analyzing the broader political stalemate, academic and political researcher Ghalib Al-Daami argued that the Jurf al-Sakhar compromise underscores the structural constraints placed on Al-Zaidi by the very ruling coalition that brought him to power.

Within Iraq’s consensus system, Al-Daami noted, strengthening sovereign state institutions directly erodes the entrenched economic and security interests of ruling factions—leading influential Coordination Framework actors to impose clear boundaries on how far the Prime Minister can push state consolidation without destabilizing the coalition.

World.title: US dollar dips slightly across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged slightly lower across major domestic parallel markets on Sunday morning, November 22, 2026, with purchasing bids settling below the 170,000-dinar threshold in both Baghdad and Erbil while retail selling rates hovered narrowly above that mark across primary trading hubs.

According to morning market figures, physical banknote rates traded across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra as follows:

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 170,050 IQD against buying offers of 169,500 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks quoted retail selling rates at 170,300 IQD alongside matching purchasing bids of 169,500 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices recorded slightly firmer quotes, with retail selling rates at 170,500 IQD and buying offers holding at 170,000 IQD per $100.

Parallel cash rates continue to trade at a wide spread of roughly 18,050 to 18,500 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

World.title: Iraq qualifies for 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup in Uzbekistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has officially confirmed the final 16-team lineup for the 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup, including Iraq, which topped Group B during the qualifiers in Thailand with 10 points—putting the young Lions of Mesopotamia just three group-stage matches away from securing a berth at the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Under head coach Salam Shaker, Iraq clinched first place in Group B after defeating tournament hosts Thailand 2–1 in their decisive final qualifier in Buriram on Friday, November 20, ending a nine-year continental qualification drought for the national under-17 side.

The finals are scheduled to take place in the Uzbek capital of Tashkent from May 13 to 29, 2027, following the official tournament draw on February 18, 2027.

Per AFC competition regulations, the top eight finishers at the tournament in Uzbekistan—specifically the eight teams that advance out of the group stage into the quarterfinals—will automatically qualify for the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Reaching the World Cup also carries a secondary continental incentive: under AFC rules, all Asian nations that qualify for the global finals earn direct entry into the 2028 AFC U-17 Asian Cup without having to contest the preliminary qualifying rounds.

The 16 participating nations in Tashkent comprise the seven qualifying group winners alongside the nine AFC representatives from the 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup who received automatic entry:

Qualification Route Qualified Nations Qualifying Group Winners Iraq (Group B), Indonesia (Group A), Syria (Group C), Iran (Group D), India (Group E), Yemen (Group F), Lebanon (Group G) Automatic Qualifiers Uzbekistan (Hosts), Australia, China PR, Japan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Tajikistan, Vietnam

Coach Salam Shaker and his squad now shift their focus toward preparing for February’s draw, aiming to replicate the historic success of Iraq’s 2016 U-16 championship generation and re-establish Iraqi youth football on both the Asian and global stages.

World.title: COP31 ends without climate pact as countries fail to reach consensus over fossil fuel omission and empty finance promises
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Countries on Sunday failed to reach an agreement at the 31st session of the UN climate conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey as there was no consensus over the cover decision (overarching political and binding outcome) -- a first such instance since 2009 despite stretching into overtime longer than ever before beyond its schedule time to conclude on Friday -- with some countries and groups including EU, Norway and Panama out-rightly objecting to the final deal for not even mentioning a call to transition away from fossil fuels in the text whereas others criticising it for empty climate finance promise.Incidentally, both Turkey and Australia - twin presidencies of this round of climate conference - are fossil fuel producing nations.

India while intervening on behalf of the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) expressed the group's concerns flagging the "dilution of the historical responsibility and obligations of developed countries" in the text but stopped short of its outright rejection noting that they are "willing to move forward, and continue to engage" for the sake of multilateralism.

"Everyone has worked tirelessly, and despite our discomfort with some elements of the text, are willing to move forward, and continue to engage.



A constructive approach going forward would be to respect the work we have done and move forward. We are committed to multilateralism and the principles of consensus and we invite our partners to join us as well," said India's key negotiator, Amandeep Garg, additional secretary in the environment ministry, in his intervention.

China during the final plenary agreed to what India maintained and even said this in as many words but chose to accept the version of the final text to keep things moving forward.





"I am deeply disappointed that COP31 has ended without consensus on an overarching outcome. I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands," said the UN secretary-general, Antonio Guterres.

The only other time a COP collapsed before 2009 (COP15 in Copenhagen) was COP6 in the Hague in 2000. The COP15 is, however, considered the biggest disappointment in the history of climate negotiations due to its much wider goal where a legally binding climate agreement could not be reached despite much political hype and preparations ahead of it.

Though the COP31 accepted a few decisions and even retained an ambitious '35 by 35' electrification goal as a key takeaway, most of the developing countries expressed strong dissatisfaction over the unresolved amount for the adaptation finance and a move of deploying carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) by 2035 that called for wider deployment of CO2 removal technologies. Many countries argued that the CCUS move raises serious questions about the direction of global mitigation efforts.

Under the '35 by 35' target, electricity would supply 35% of global final energy consumption by 2035. At present, the share of electricity in global energy consumption is 23%. The move recognizes the need for stronger grids, storage, system flexibility and better energy access, but the text mentions no specific financial commitments for this aspiration. It also ignored the firm commitment of renewable-powered electrification.

In India, electricity currently makes up roughly 22% of the countryâs total final energy consumption, with the remainder dominated by oil, coal and natural gas. The country has voluntarily moved quite fast on increasing its renewable footprints, way above many developing countries.

COP31 even failed to bridge the overall adaptation finance gap, leaving many developing countries extremely disappointed. India, on behalf of the LMDC, too flagged it in the plenary.

"... our partners have refused to engage on the issue of climate finance across different negotiating rooms. In fact, we were told that despite the increasing needs of developing countries due to a problem that we have not caused, we should not expect our developed country partners to even engage on the issue of climate finance, since it was 'dead in the water'," Garg told the plenary.

Many experts consider COP31 a big political failure as it happened amid wars, geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainty and mounting climate risks.

Countries across the globe are facing growing pressures over energy security, industrial competitiveness and public finances, while developing nations struggle with rising adaptation costs and increasingly severe climate impacts. They also flagged that the EU failed miserably to take climate leadership in the absence of the USA which under President Donald Trump stepped out from the Paris Agreement.

Developed countries, mainly the EU nations, the UK and Japan resisted measurable commitments to fund climate action while the major fossil fuel producing nations including Saudi Arabia and Russia opposed stronger language on transitioning away from oil, gas and coal.

The result was a text that found space for an electrification goal and CCUS but not for strong anti-fossil fuel commitments or public finance needed by developing nations.

âThe COP 31 outcome reflects an abject lack of political ambition and accountability. Despite negotiations extending till Sunday, countries failed to agree on a meaningful commitment to transition away from fossil fuels or to talk about climate security.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

There is over emphasis on the unknown devil of CCUS which presents a grave concern of untested technology, and serious implications to forest and food security in many parts of the world," said Aarti Khosla, director, Climate Trends.

Harjeet Singh, founding director of the Satat Sampada Climate Foundation, said the COP31 failed the people it was meant to protect. "Rich countries refused to put money on the table to help communities prepare for and recover from climate disasters, and handed polluters a free pass instead. No deal is better than a deal that locks in failure. But this cannot become an excuse for more delay: the money and the plan must now come," he said.

World.title: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri over unsafe packaged drinking water
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (

) on Sunday sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd after a sample of its packaged drinking water was found unsafe.

In a social media post, the food safety regulator said a sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" collected from Bisleri's premises was found to be non-compliant with prescribed safety standards.

"The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," FSSAI said.

The company subsequently appealed against the findings, following which the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory for further analysis.



The laboratory also declared it "unsafe" after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator said.

Based on the laboratory findings, FSSAI concluded that the company had violated provisions relating to unsafe food under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. It has, therefore, sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd under the law.

Apart from Bisleri, the regulator also sanctioned prosecution against several other companies, including Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd, Tit-Bit Foods India Pvt Ltd, Mimansa Industries and Asha Confectionery.





FSSAI also suspended the licences of Urmi Lifesciences LLP and Gaur Ayurvedic Store for non-compliance with food safety rules and regulations, news agency PTI reported.

The latest action comes amid an intensified enforcement drive by FSSAI against food business operators (FBOs) and e-commerce companies during the current calendar year. The regulator has also stepped up scrutiny of energy drink and alcoholic beverage manufacturers.

One of its recent regulatory disputes involves the classification of Red Bull as an "energy drink". In June, FSSAI moved against the use of the label, raising concerns that the high added-sugar content of certain beverages could mislead consumers and encourage excessive consumption.

Red Bull, PepsiCo, Monster Beverage and Reliance Consumer challenged the regulator's order in the Delhi high court, arguing that the restrictions were imposed without giving them prior notice.

Red Bull subsequently secured an interim court injunction allowing it to continue using the "energy drink" label. Its competitors, however, were directed to stop using the classification after exhausting their existing stocks.

FSSAI has challenged the relief granted to Red Bull, arguing that it gives the company "an undue commercial advantage" over its rivals. The matter is scheduled to be heard in January.

World.title: Twenty held in Jammu and Kashmir recruitment board cheating case; ‘no paper leak found’
World.content:
Twenty people of an organised network were held, including government employees, candidates, and intermediaries, for their alleged involvement in “an attempt of unfair means” during the Finance Accounts Assistant examination of the Jammu & Kashmir Services Selection Board (JKSSB) in Jammu on November 14, the police said on Sunday (November 22, 2026).

Meanwhile, the J&K Students Association demanded a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) amid the ongoing protests by aspirants as well as political parties.

“The investigation exposed an organised network involving government employees, candidates and intermediaries, who allegedly planned to facilitate cheating for selected candidates through electronic devices. Twenty people have been arrested so far, including six government employees, and the mastermind,” Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Joginder Singh said.

The details of the JKSSB employees have been shared with the department for action, “as they face criminal proceedings”. The accused had allegedly used electronic devices, including mobile phones and wireless radio sets, to help aspirants qualify for the exam and also earn money by posting papers on a Telegram group. “The accused were asking for money from the candidates,” the police said.

“The malpractice was confined to a particular examination centre. The investigation had not established any paper leak,” Mr. Singh said.

The police said the question paper had allegedly been taken out of the examination centre, photographed, and circulated within the chosen candidates via a Telegram group. The modus operandi suggested that an employee took “selected candidates to a designated room, removed one of the papers and leaked outside”.

“The question paper was intended to reach at least 25 to 26 candidates. Timely police intervention prevented the conspiracy. Two candidates managed to cheat using electronic gadgets, and their details have been shared with the concerned agency for further action,” Mr. Singh said.

The police were piecing together technical details to establish the role of the accused. “Our effort is to take the investigation to such a level, through scientific methods and proper collection of evidence, that when the case goes to trial, the court has sufficient material to punish those responsible,” Mr. Singh said.

On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts. Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K.

Nasir Aslam Wani, advisor to J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, said, “The government won’t allow such things. We will ensure fairness and will restore youths’ confidence.”

The incident triggered widespread protests across J&K, with former MP Aga Syed Ruhullah, aspirants and students holding a day-long sit-in in Srinagar on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

J&K Education Minister Shameema Firdous said that the case on recruitment irregularities fell under the domain of Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha. “The L-G is best placed to decide the further course of action,” Ms. Firdous said.

14 arrested as J&K Police bust exam cheating racket; mobiles, wireless sets seized

Letter to Amit Shah

The J&K Students Association, in a letter to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, sought an independent CBI investigation, postponement of the upcoming J&K Police Sub Inspector and Police Constable examinations. “We demand a comprehensive institutional review of the JKSSB,” the Association said.

“The latest incident must be viewed against the backdrop of recurring recruitment irregularities in J&K since 2020 like the 2022 Police Sub-Inspector examination, the 2022 FAA examination, the Junior Engineer recruitment etc. Repeated scandals, investigations and assurances have failed to restore public confidence,” Nasir Khuehami, national convenor of association, said.

Kashmir’s chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq said the arrest of alleged facilitators in the earlier cases “should have prompted strict action”. “If the system fails students, what should they do?” The government should fix accountability, take strict action against the culprits and announce either a re-examination or cancellation of the recruitment process, depending on the findings of the investigation,” the Mirwaiz said.

World.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah arrives in Delhi for first official visit to India
World.content:
The Prime Minister of Nepal, Balendra Shah, arrived here on Sunday (November 22, 2026) afternoon for his first official visit to India. Sources said that Mr. Shah will inaugurate several projects on Monday and is scheduled to hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

According to sources, Monday’s (November 23, 2026) discussion between the two Prime Ministers will give “political direction” to bilateral relations for the coming years.

On Sunday (November 22, 2026), Mr. Shah was received at the airport by Jitin Prasada, the Minister of State for Commerce and Industry, Electronics and Information Technology. His first formal meeting of the visit took place in the evening, when External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar called on him. After the meeting, Mr. Jaishankar said, “Privileged to call on PM Balen Shah of Nepal on his visit to New Delhi this evening. India cherishes the special friendship with Nepal. Look forward to his engagements with PM Narendra Modi tomorrow.”

Mr. Shah, a rapper and former mayor of Kathmandu, took office as Nepal’s Prime Minister in March after his Rastriya Swatantra Party's (RSP’s) landslide victory in the elections to replace the interim government that was in place following the Gen Z uprising of September 2025. The RSP defeated older political parties like the Nepali Congress and the Maoists, who had dominated the country’s political landscape since the Constituent Assembly elections of 2008.

Mr. Modi had invited Mr. Shah to India soon after the latter was sworn in as Prime Minister. The two leaders have interacted over the telephone and exchanged messages on social media as well as through diplomatic channels, but Monday (November 23, 2026) will be the first time they meet in person.

Major agreements

The Hindu was told that the major agreements between the two sides are expected to be in the areas of development partnership, energy, hydropower, railways, connectivity, climate change, disaster resilience, infrastructure, and technology.

On Saturday (November 21, 2026), The Hindu reported that the Dharchula Bridge, the land port of Banbasa at the India-Nepal border in Uttarakhand, and a train connection between Janakpur and Gorakhpur are expected to be inaugurated on Monday (November 23, 2026) by the two leaders. The two sides are in talks for new railway links between Raxaul and Kathmandu, which would open new freight and passenger connections.

Earlier on Sunday (November 22, 2026), Mr. Shah left Kathmandu on a Nepal Airlines flight, which also carried a 35-member team accompanying him for the engagements in Delhi. Having introduced a no-frills administration, Mr. Shah did not have a ceremonial farewell at the Tribhuvan International Airport, as was the norm during the tenure of previous Prime Ministers of Nepal. Moving away from past tradition, the Nepal Embassy is also not likely to host Mr. Shah for a civic reception, as had been done during similar visits in the past.

The business delegation from Nepal was hosted at an event organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry on Sunday (November 22, 2026) evening, which was attended by the country’s Finance Minister, Swarnim Wagley. Nepal's Foreign Minister, Shisir Khanal, is also accompanying Mr. Shah.

Nepal’s Prime Minister will be given a ceremonial reception at the Rashtrapati Bhavan on Monday (November 23, 2026) morning, following which he will proceed to the memorial of Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat. After this, he will take part in talks with Mr. Modi at Hyderabad House. Subsequently, Mr. Shah will call on President Droupadi Murmu in the afternoon before emplaning for Kathmandu.

World.title: Centre prioritising border villages, 40 seeing reverse migration: Amit Shah in Arunachal Pradesh
World.content:
Describing the development of border villages as a priority of the government, Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday (November 22, 2026) said the upliftment of about 40 villages along the International Border in Arunachal Pradesh, under the Centre’s flagship Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP), ensured that many of those who moved out from these areas were returning.

Launching four major development initiatives worth more than ₹5,610 crore, he said Prime Minister Narendra Modi changed the perception of border villages by describing them as the country's “first villages” and undertaking the VVP to provide such areas with healthcare, electricity, education, and drinking water.

On the last day of his three-day visit to the State, Mr. Shah also inaugurated the 12th battalion campus of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) at Hollongi, near Itanagar, and said the government was following a "zero-casualty" approach to disaster management, under which timely warnings and immediate evacuation measures were being prioritised to protect vulnerable people.

The initiatives launched on Sunday include 199 Vibrant Villages projects worth ₹110.95 crore across 11 border districts; Mission Shikshit Arunachal Phase-II, with an outlay of ₹1,500 crore; and power and rural road development to the tune of ₹2,000 crore each.

“Developing border villages is our government’s priority. If villages are empowered economically, the lifestyle of the people will change, and their happiness will increase,” Mr. Shah said, adding that reverse migration helped repopulate 40 border villages in Arunachal Pradesh.

A lack of jobs and poor quality of life have forced several people in such villages, along Arunachal Pradesh’s borders with Bhutan, China, and Myanmar, to migrate to the State’s urban centres and elsewhere in India over the years. This raised concerns, as the border residents were seen as an important aspect of the country’s first line of defence.

Cooperatives push

The Union Home Minister said personnel of the Indian Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) were helping border villagers increase agricultural production and facilitating the marketing of their locally grown produce.

“As the Army and ITBP personnel are consuming locally produced crops and food items, their emotional bonds with the border villages are becoming stronger,” he said.

Mr. Shah, who also holds the Cooperation portfolio, said Arunachal Pradesh could become self-sufficient in milk, eggs, fish, and meat production through cooperatives, thereby improving the economy of rural and border areas.

He assured the people that if they produced sufficient quantities of milk, the National Dairy Development Board and Amul would purchase their produce.

Financial assistance

Mr. Shah accused the Congress of neglecting development in Arunachal Pradesh and providing inadequate financial assistance during its rule, claiming that under Mr. Modi’s leadership, the Centre has substantially increased its support for the State’s progress.

He said the Centre provided ₹33,530 crore to Arunachal Pradesh during the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance’s tenure between 2004 and 2014, but this rose to ₹1,64,664 crore during the 2014-2024 period under the Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance government.

The Home Minister said tax devolution to the State increased fourfold, while grants increased 18 times, compared to the time of the UPA government. “The figures reflect the Narendra Modi government’s commitment to the development of Arunachal Pradesh and the rest of the Northeast,” he said.

“The growth of Arunachal Pradesh’s budget from ₹12,000 crore to ₹36,000 crore suggests that development has expanded in the last 12 years,” he said.

Boosting preparedness

Inaugurating the NDRF campus, Mr. Shah said it would significantly strengthen disaster preparedness and response across the Northeast, one of the country’s most vulnerable regions to natural calamities.

He said the region is prone to various natural disasters and stressed the need for preparedness, modern warning systems and coordinated efforts to minimise loss of lives and property.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
World.content:
What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

World.title: BMTC spare parts ‘scam’: FIR against 21 officials, employees and suppliers over alleged ₹3.97-crore fraud
World.content:
An alleged scam involving the supply of spare parts to the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) has come to light, with Wilson Garden police registering an FIR against 21 officials and employees, along with companies supplying spare parts to the corporation.

The complaint was filed by an officer attached to the BMTC Vigilance Department.

According to the complaint, forged documents were allegedly created in the names of five companies claiming that 2,820 spare parts had been supplied to BMTC buses, even though the materials were allegedly not delivered.

The alleged fraud amounts to nearly ₹3.98 crore, the complaint said. The case was registered on November 20.

Although spare parts were allegedly never supplied, records were created to show that the materials had been received.

The complaint further alleges that BMTC’s Central Office had no corresponding records confirming the receipt of the materials. However, seals of the central office and forged signatures of vigilance personnel were allegedly affixed to the goods invoices to make the transactions appear genuine.

Fake warehouse-receipt documents and receipts were also allegedly generated. Signatures of a retired divisional mechanical engineer were reportedly forged on these documents.

World.title: Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media
World.content:
U.S. securities regulators are investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia, according to U.S. media, adding to the turmoil engulfing the artificial intelligence chip giant following the resignation of its chief executive.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) inquiry is in its early stages, The New York Times reported on Saturday (November 21, 2026), citing people briefed on the confidential investigation. The Wall Street Journal reported on the investigation earlier this week, although it was unable to establish its precise focus. The probe could end without any charges being brought against the company.

Questions about Nvidia’s financial disclosures have intensified amid scrutiny of its dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company investigated by American authorities over suspected shipments of restricted AI chips to China. Nvidia last year changed how it reported sales by geographical location, switching from customers’ billing addresses to the countries where they are headquartered, U.S. media reported.

The change removed Singapore from its geographical breakdown, despite the company’s significant business there. It remains unclear whether the SEC investigation is connected to those accounting changes or to the scandal surrounding former chief executive Jensen Huang.

Mr. Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of working for Beijing. China has denied the espionage allegations, while Megaspeed has maintained that it operates lawfully.

Nvidia’s board has appointed former chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive, and launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding Mr. Huang’s departure.

The upheaval has shaken investor confidence in one of the world’s most valuable companies, whose advanced semiconductors have been central to the global AI boom. Nvidia shares plunged 14% on Friday (November 20, 2026), bringing their losses for the week to more than 20%.

U.S. President Donald Trump nevertheless called on Friday (November 20, 2026) for Mr. Huang to be reinstated. “I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance,” Mr. Trump told reporters. But Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones has ruled out his return, saying board directors unanimously accepted his resignation.

World.title: Police fact-check claims about illegal Bangladeshi immigrants in Bengaluru
World.content:
The Varthur police detained a Bangladeshi national who was found staying in a labour shed in the city, following a call to the emergency helpline 112 alleging that several Bangladeshi nationals were residing illegally in the area. However, he had valid documents and was released on Sunday.

Acting on the information, the police rounded up five persons from the labour shed for verification. During the inquiry, one of them, identified as Babul Sheikh, was found to be a Bangladeshi national possessing a valid passport and tourist visa. The police verified his nationality and travel documents through the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) and subsequently released him.

Meanwhile, the other four persons claimed that they were natives of Assam and provided their local addresses. The police contacted their counterparts in Assam and verified their claims. The inquiry confirmed that the four labourers belonged to a village in Assam, following which they were released.

Meanwhile, social media posts claiming that illegal Bangladeshi nationals were residing in large numbers in Balagere triggered concern.

Clarifying the issue, Whitefield Division Deputy Commissioner of Police B.L. Srihari Babu said the social media post was false and misleading. He added that legal action had been initiated against those responsible for spreading the misinformation.

World.title: Botcha urges Governor to recommend dismissal of Chandrababu Naidu government
World.content:
YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) Legislative Council Opposition Leader Botcha Satyanarayana on Sunday (November 22, 2026) urged Governor S. Abdul Nazeer to recommend the dismissal of the Chandrababu Naidu-led government. He alleged that the ruling coalition was using State machinery to suppress political opposition and subvert the democratic process.

Mr. Satyanarayana, who led a delegation that submitted a memorandum along with supporting evidence to the Governor at Lok Bhavan, accused the government of allowing widespread violence, intimidation, and irregularities in the local body elections. He alleged that the police had disregarded directions issued by the Supreme Court and the High Court, while opposition candidates were being prevented from exercising their right to contest.

Referring to incidents of violence in Tadipatri, Kadapa, and Punganur, he condemned alleged petrol-bomb attacks, including the attack on YSRCP MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy. He also questioned the police explanation that firecrackers had caused the vehicles to catch fire during the attack on the residence of former MLA Kethireddy Peddareddy. He described the explanation by the DSP concerned as ‘shameful’.

“This government has no moral or constitutional right to continue in office even for a minute. We have requested the Governor to recommend its dismissal to the President and Parliament,” he said. He also demanded that the ongoing election process be cancelled and fresh elections conducted in a free and fair atmosphere.

Mr. Satyanarayana alleged that the State Election Commission (SEC) had failed to discharge its constitutional responsibilities, with the police ignoring its instructions. He referred to the SEC Commissioner expressing his willingness to resign and questioned the authority of the Commission in the face of alleged violations.

In a pointed attack on the Chief Minister and his son Nara Lokesh, Mr. Satyanarayana remarked that Mr. Chandrababu Naidu was effectively performing the duties of the Director-General of Police, while Minister Nara Lokesh was acting as the State's law-and-order DGP.

World.title: Naqvi hits back at minister for repeated criticism: report
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has hit back at a federal minister for what he said was repeated criticism against him, Geo News reported on Sunday.

The news website reported that Naqvi, without naming the minister, claimed the latter had been commenting on him on television almost every day to “gain attention”.

The report described the remarks as part of an informal conversation with Geo News and further quoted Naqvi as saying that he had been patiently listening to the minister’s statements for the past two-and-a-half years — the tenure of the incumbent government since the 2024 elections.

“The day I comment on this minister, he will not be able to show his face,” Naqvi warned, according to the outlet.

Naqvi also defended the businesspeople present at an economic forum who he said were criticised by the minister. He said the attendees were respectable citizens who had served as presidents and office-bearers of chambers of commerce at the federal and city levels, according to the report.

While the report did not quote him as mentioning any specific details in this connection, Naqvi’s remarks at the Pakistan Economic Summit in Islamabad in July had been making headlines in recent months. Naqvi had whipped up a political storm by calling for creating new administrative units in the country to “reset” the current “system” of governance while speaking at the forum, which was attended by businessmen.

In his remarks to Geo News, Naqvi stated that the businessmen were also among the country’s highest taxpayers.

“If these businessmen are so bad, why do you take billions of rupees from them in the name of party funds at every election?” the interior minister was quoted as saying.

Naqvi’s remarks have been reported a day after Inter-Provincial Coordination Minister Rana Sanaullah questioned the objectives of some of the businesspeople at that July forum.

In an interview on Geo News programme ‘Jirga’ aired on Saturday, Sanaullah said the “matter got worse in such a way that the debate on provinces began from an economic forum” and Naqvi started the discussion.

Sanaullah, also Naqvi’s predecessor, contended that there were “some objectionable businessmen sitting among the audience of that economic forum”.

“It has been their background that in each tenure, they keep on telling the incoming ruler, especially the army chief, that ‘sir, the whole world is looking at you and only you are the saviour,’” Sanaullah said.

The PML-N leader clarified that he was not referring to the entire business community, but rather “a few people who keep committing crime in business, and here as well”.

On differing stances among federal cabinet members on the issue of new provinces, Sanaullah contended that politicians could express their opinions, as “regimental discipline” could not be brought into the cabinet.

Sanaullah stressed that the debate on provinces was “not wrong”, but he contended that the “debate was being entangled with other matters; saying that the system has collapsed; after that some remarks were made about the prime minister, and similarly about politicians contesting elections in so and so manner”.

The PML-N leader also criticised PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari for further complicating the situation by referring to various matters in his Nov 17 speech, rather than merely voicing his objection to carving out new administrative units out of Sindh.

Sanaullah further termed both Bilawal and Naqvi as “sons” of President Asif Ali Zardari, adding that they were “under his discipline”.

Asked about the independent senator being “under President Zardari’s discipline”, Sanaullah reiterated, “Yes, definitely. He has not disowned him yet. He himself calls him (Naqvi) his son; it is not that we are saying so.”

Referring to a recent meeting between President Zardari and PM Shehbaz Sharif, during which Naqvi was also present, Sanaullah said a “ceasefire was decided” there.

He claimed that, according to information he had, a meeting was held at President House recently, which was attended by President Zardari, Bilawal and Naqvi, and it was decided to reduce tensions.

Replying to a query about the independent senator, Sanaullah remarked that Naqvi was a senator of both PPP and PML-N, as leaders from both parties contributed to the votes for his election.

In September as well, Sanaullah had said that the “debate should have been started in Parliament”, adding that issues of such magnitude should not be reduced to speeches, social media, seminars or business forums.

The PML-N leader has also taken jibes at the interior minister on a few other occasions since the ruling coalition came to power.

On the other hand, Sindh Local Government Minister Nasir Hussain Shah also took exception to Sanaullah’s remarks, asserting that Bilawal was the only son of President Zardari.

“Mohsin Naqvi sahib is worthy of respect in his place, but nothing about him compares to the chairman (Bilawal),” he told reporters.

Shah maintained there was “no such thing” as suggested by the PML-N minister, declaring, “There is only one Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, and only his words will prevail here.”

World.title: Oman to supply petroleum products, $200m credit facility to PSO under new agreement
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Oman on Sunday signed an agreement under which the Gulf country’s state-owned OQ Trading would supply petroleum products, as well as a $200 million credit line, to the Pakistan State Oil (PSO).

This could provide Pakistan with a means to strategically diversify its sourcing of petroleum products as the Strait of Hormuz continues to be choked by the US-Iran conflict into its ninth month.

According to an announcement from the Petroleum Division, the agreement between the two state-owned entities was signed during Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik’s visit to Muscat, where he met with Oman’s Minister of Energy and Minerals Eng. Salim Al Aufi.

The two sides discussed opportunities for strengthening bilateral cooperation in the oil, gas and minerals sectors.

During the meeting, both ministers discussed avenues for mutually beneficial cooperation and welcomed the establishment of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Working Group on Oil and Gas. They agreed to make optimal use of this institutional mechanism to further strengthen bilateral engagement and advance cooperation in the energy and mining sector.

Following the meeting, the two ministers witnessed the signing of a Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) for petroleum products between PSO and OQ Trading (OQT), Oman’s global commodity trading company. OQT has also agreed to extend a $200m credit line to PSO to facilitate petroleum purchases.

Welcoming the agreement, both ministers expressed confidence that its implementation would further strengthen Pakistan-Oman energy ties and support Pakistan’s efforts to enhance energy security through diversification of energy imports.

“The agreement marks an important milestone in the commercial relationship between the two companies and provides a structured arrangement for petroleum product supplies from OQT to PSO, supporting supply reliability amid continued volatility in regional energy markets,” the Petroleum Division’s statement said.

It noted that OQT has already established itself as a major supplier of gasoline to PSO, supplying more than 1m tonnes during 2026. The newly signed agreement builds on this established trading relationship and provides a framework for expanding commercial cooperation, the statement added.

Beyond gasoline, OQT has also strengthened its presence in Pakistan’s liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) market, supplying both state-owned and private sector buyers.

According to the Petroleum Division, OQT’s LPG supplies to Pakistan are expected to exceed 120,000 metric tonnes by the end of 2026, reflecting the company’s continued commitment to meeting market demand and maintaining energy flows amid regional supply disruptions.

The meeting and the signing of the agreement underscore the shared commitment of Pakistan and Oman to expanding bilateral energy cooperation, strengthening commercial partnerships and exploring new investment opportunities across the oil, gas and minerals sectors, the statement added.

Last month, Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi made a two-day visit to Pakistan, meeting its top leadership.

He attended the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC), during which both sides emphasised the importance of promoting exchanges of business delegations from both countries to unlock new opportunities for trade, investment and institutional collaboration.

World.title: Pakistan Shaheens post 313 against India A in heated Rising Stars Asia Cup clash
World.content:
Pakistan Shaheens made 313 in 49.2 overs after winning a controversial toss and opting to bat against India A in their Asia Cup Rising Stars match here on Sunday, with half-centuries from Maaz Sadaqat, Hasan Nawaz and Farhan Yousaf underpinning their total.

The toss took an unusual turn when the match referee initially called tails after India A captain Tilak Varma flipped the coin on Pakistan captain Abdul Samad’s call of heads.

Both captains inspected the coin before Samad pointed out the error, prompting the officials to recheck and correct the decision in Pakistan’s favour.

Samad chose to bat on a pitch both captains described as slightly dry. The sides did not shake hands after the toss, maintaining the protocol observed in recent India-Pakistan encounters.

Pakistan made a brisk start, with openers Shamyl Hussain and Maaz taking 65 runs off the first seven overs. Shamyl led the attack, striking 33 off 23 balls, including four fours and two sixes, as the pair put India’s pace attack under pressure.

Harshit Rana, in particular, responded with an aggressive approach, engaging both openers in heated exchanges as they scored freely.

The verbal contest continued through the powerplay and Rana gave Shamyl an animated send-off after the left-hander was caught by the bowler at short third off Ayush Badoni in the eighth over.

Rana struck again five balls later, trapping wicketkeeper Rohail Nazir leg-before for a duck to leave Pakistan 67-2.

Maaz and Hasan Nawaz then steadied the innings with a 54-run stand for the third wicket.

Maaz Sadaqat plays a shot during the Asia Cup Rising Stars match against India A on Nov 22. — Photo courtesy ACC

Maaz, registering his second consecutive half-century, made 59 off 63 balls, with six fours and a six, before being caught off Suryansh Shedge in the 20th over.

Hasan took charge, reaching his fifty off 43 deliveries with a six off Vipraj Nigam. He added 65 runs with Abdul Samad, who contributed 28 off 35 balls before being run out in the 31st over following sharp fielding by India captain Rinku Singh and wicketkeeper Kumar Kushagra.

Hasan was caught by Badoni off Shedge in the 39th over for 79 off 82 balls, an innings featuring five fours and four sixes, with Pakistan on 230-5.

Hasan Nawaz plays a shot during Asia Cup Rising Stars match against India A on Nov 22. — Photo courtesy ACC

Farhan Yousaf then struck 56 off 48 balls, hitting four fours and two sixes, while Mohammad Imran added a brisk 23 off 14 deliveries, including two sixes.

Farhan helped Pakistan cross 300 in the 47th over before being caught by Kushagra off Prince Yadav while attempting a ramp shot.

Pakistan’s lower order offered little resistance as Prince removed Ali Raza for two to end the innings at 313.

For India, Rana, Prince, Shedge and Vipraj Nigam claimed two wickets each, while Badoni took one. Rana conceded 77 runs in his 10 overs.

World.title: Multiple Karachi routes briefly closed as political parties hold demonstration, rally in Karachi
World.content:
Multiple roads were closed briefly in Karachi on Sunday as the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) staged a demonstration in the city and the Jeay Sindh Rehbar Committee (JSRC) — a conglomerate of four Sindhi nationalist groups — held a rally.

The JUI-F staged its main demonstration at Guru Mandir, while the JSRC organised a rally from Sachal Goth to the press club via Sharea Faisal, some stretches of which had been shut for vehicles, the traffic police said.

Traffic was allowed again on the stretch of Sharea Faisal leading to Drigh Road and Karsaz at 4:16pm after about an hour-long closure. Commuters coming from the airport had been diverted via Rashid Minhas Bridge towards Millennium Mall.

The route from Askari 4 to Drigh Road on Main Rashid Minhas Road was reopened for traffic at around 4:30pm following its reported closure at 3:30pm.

The route from Guru Mandir towards Jamshed Road was reopened for vehicles at around 5pm after being closed to traffic shortly after 2pm.

The stretch of Sharea Faisal from Avari Towers towards FTC was reopened at 8:45pm. Vehicles had been diverted from Avari Towers towards Fatima Jinnah Road and Sindh Club.

Both sides of Deen Mohammad Wafai Road had also been closed to traffic, with vehicles diverted from MR Kiani Chowrangi towards Thana Gali and from Fawara Chowk towards Zainab Market.

Main Korangi Road from CSD towards Sharea Faisal was closed at around 11am due to “security” reasons and was reopened to traffic at 9:30pm.
